member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3
member.summary: Where two bodies lie against each other, face to face.

remarks.para: Two bodies that only touch share no volume, so says false and says true, and neither says where. A column standing on a footing, a plate bolted to a flange: what bears on what is the patch where the two surfaces lie against each other.

Two faces are in contact where they lie in one plane and face opposite ways — back to back, one body on each side. Two faces flush and facing the same way are side by side, not in contact. The patch is the area the two faces share, which the plane library works out exactly through the coplanar lift, and the patches in one plane are joined, so a contact drawn across several faces comes back as the one region it is.

Both bodies are read as their material first, so a column standing over a bolt hole in a base plate does not report the hole as bearing. Only contact with area is a face: two bodies meeting along an edge or at a point have no patch, and the return type says so rather than inventing a face of no area.

member.summary: The region two convex bodies share, found by clipping one by the faces of the other.
member.remarks: Two convex bodies share at most one region, and it is convex: what is left of the first once everything in front of each face of the second is cut away. Clipping each face against a plane, and capping the cut, costs a pass over the corners per face of the second body, where the general boolean cuts the first into cells by every plane of both and sorts the cells. A round bar crossing another is the common case in a model: a reinforcing cage, a mesh, bolts through plates' clearance.
member.summary: Booleans of bodies that close only within the tolerance, worked out again on the bodies welded where they are not worked out as they came.
member.remarks: A body whose faces meet on copies of an edge a hair apart, a crack, closes within the tolerance and no closer. Where a plane of the other body crosses such a crack within a few thousandths, the cut leaves a rim gap at the plane wider than it bridges, the cell stays whole, and the boolean can be judged no further: a cracked box dipping 0.088 into an arm of a cracked U, the cracks 1.7E-5 wide and slanting 0.004 either side of the planes of the other, less the U, was not worked out. So where a boolean is not worked out, each body that closes within the tolerance and not at the rounding of its coordinates has its corners welded within the tolerance (see ) and its faces in one plane merged (see ), and the boolean is worked out once more on what that gives, by the same checks: the box less the U leaves 475.54, as it should. Of 45 000 booleans of such a U and a box, both cracked 1E-5 to 1E-4 wide, at a thousandth, a hundredth and 0.05, 5 788 were not worked out, and every one is right now. A boolean worked out as the bodies came is as it was, to the bit; so is one that is still not worked out.
member.summary:
Combines solids: the union of two bodies, the part they share, and one taken out of the other.
The method is the same one Splition3 uses to cut a plate against a body, carried up a dimension. One body is divided by the planes of the other's faces that come near it, which leaves cells that are each wholly inside or wholly outside the other body, since the surface of a body never leaves the planes of its own faces. The cells wanted for the operation are then glued back together: a face shared by two kept cells appears twice, once each way round, and dropping both leaves exactly the outer skin.
Dividing A by the planes of B already lays a face along every part of the surface of B that runs through A. That is why an intersection is just the cells of A that fall inside B, and a difference just the cells of A that fall outside it: the walls of the cavity are already there, and adding the faces of B on top of them would describe the same surface twice.
So every operation cuts one body only, the one fewer planes cut, and never by its own faces: they bound it already, and cutting by them is what took a bent bar apart into thousands of cells, since every plane of a bend runs on through the rest of the bar. A union keeps the part of the cut body beyond the other and the other whole; a difference cutting the body taken away keeps the body taken from whole, and the part of the other within it turned inside out. Where the whole body and the cells meet, their faces lie back to back in one plane, cut differently, and cancel by the area they share. Where a plane crosses a cell and leaves it whole, the other body is cut instead, and failing that both are cut by every plane of both, as they once always were.
Every operation reports false when the answer is nothing at all — two bodies that do not touch have no shared part, and a body wholly swallowed by another leaves nothing behind. That is an outcome rather than a failure, which is why it comes back as false with no result rather than as an exception or an empty body.
An opening on either body is honoured. A union or a difference cuts the openings into both bodies first (), so their faces are where their material ends; an intersection adds the planes of its own openings near the other to its knives, so no cell straddles a wall, and drops the cells filling them as not being material. Either way the result carries the cavity as real geometry rather than as an opening of its own. Two bodies too far apart to meet are the exception — nothing is cut there, and each keeps the openings it came with. An opening of either body of a common part, or of the body a difference takes away, that shares no space with the other body is left out, since it changes nothing the operation gives: its box further from the other's box than the tolerance, or it and the other closed, their faces further apart than twice the tolerance and no corner of either inside the other. A spiral girder less a spiral ramp holding a spiral tube as an opening, 80 under the girder's top all along it, was cut into 640 222 cells in 202 seconds and not worked out, the tube cut into the ramp; the tube left out, it is cut into 18 345 in 1.6 seconds and holds what slicing gives. The openings of a body a union or a difference keeps material of are cut in as before, wherever they lie. Walls of two openings of a body, or of an opening and the body, standing apart within the tolerance of one plane are each kept in their own: the openings of both bodies are cut in, and the operation worked out, within a finer tolerance, as cuts such openings, where no wall of the other body lies within the tolerance of the plane of a wall of the one. An L 100 by 80 by 50 with two blind openings whose walls stood 0.0009 apart, less a box across both walls, within a thousandth, held 130 189.39 one way round and 130 189.26 the other, where it holds 130 189.32, as it does now. Asked at a millionth or below, where the openings of a body cut in at once come out open, the operation is worked out again on the material gives, and that is taken where what came as before is not made, not valid, or holds another volume: a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two blind openings whose ceilings stood 0.00095 apart, less a box across both, at a millionth, held 1.05 too little and was not valid, and the two joined were not worked out. Asked below a thousandth, within a million of the origin, openings that come out open or with a piece judged whole, cut in at once by the cells each opening reaches, are cut again with every plane of the openings carried through every cell, so that the faces of cells side by side match: the plate less the box at a ten-thousandth and a hundred-thousandth, where the operation is not worked out again, held the same 1.05 too little and was not valid, and the two joined held as much too little or were not worked out; both hold what they should now.
A result of two closed bodies is closed as reads it, or not made: one whose corners close it, two copies of an edge about the tolerance apart taken for one, which Validate reads as open, is welded, or worked out another way, and where it stays open the operation reports false, logged, as one it could not work out.
A void, a chip or a slab no thicker than the point tolerance is within the tolerance of nothing and changes nothing; one thicker than the tolerance and a trillionth of the size of the coordinates of the two bodies is cut however thin: a cube of 100 less a box 40 by 30 and 0.0005 thick inside it is the cube, and less one 0.0015 thick holds 999 998.2. One exactly the tolerance thick, on a turned body that thick to a few bits either way, is read as no thicker, the same way by the common part and both differences; a union of the two can hold anything from the two less it to the two.
Asked within a few roundings of the coordinates, a quadrillionth of the largest of them, an operation reads a corner as on a plane within what rounding adds to the planar tolerance, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates, as the cut of openings does: a plate 200 by 100 by 3, turned and a hundred thousand out, less a slot 20 wide across all of it, within 9.5E-11, leaves its two pieces, 54 000, where it was said to leave nothing. Asked further below the rounding, below four tenths of it, nought among it, an operation is worked out as though asked at the rounding, and what it gives is welded to close within the tolerance asked: at nought, such a plate at the origin less a hole 20 by 20 through it leaves 58 800, where it came back whole, 60 000. Of a body that does not close within the rounding, what is given there is taken where it holds up against the common part of the two, and otherwise what the tolerance alone gives, where that holds up by the same checks; neither holding up, the operation is not worked out: at nought a cube 10 across cracked 0.0001 wide along three of its faces, less a box turned inside it, is not worked out, where it came back whole, and less a slab thousands long through it, sharing 249.85, is not worked out either, where it came back whole though the tolerance alone gave something too. The common part of two such bodies is taken only where it has no corner outside either, and leaves out no corner of one lying inside the other, and a difference or a union of them only where the common part they are checked by does so too: a U 30 by 10 by 10 and a box through its notch, both cracked 1.5E-5 wide, have their common part not worked out, where it came out 3.66 of the 34.02 they share. A difference or a common part said to be nothing is checked so too: such a U less a box dipping 0.81 into its notch's floor is not worked out, where it was said to leave nothing of 2 402.34.
A union of two bodies lying face to face within the tolerance of each other and apart, welded closed, is taken where it holds the two and the gap filled: two cubes of 100 side by side 0.01 apart, turned, joined within a hundredth, hold 2 000 000. What two bodies exactly the tolerance apart join into still depends on where they lie: turned another way the two cubes hold 1 999 933.3, part of the gap.
Two bodies exactly the tolerance into or apart, or nearer, are read as touching, closed across the slab or the gap: the part they share is nothing, each difference leaves its body whole, and the union holds the two less the overlap or the two and the gap filled, within the tolerance times the area where they lie face to face either way, each face within the tolerance of where it belongs. A column 300 by 300 by 1 000 and a beam 386.7 wide and 364.8 high running exactly 0.001 into its side, turned, joined within a thousandth, hold the two less 125.26, the overlap being 109.45 and the beam's whole end 141.07. A beam 160.1 by 160.8 standing exactly 0.01 clear of such a column, joined within a hundredth, holds the two and 214.5, filling the gap holding 257.4; closed at the default tolerance by a weld tilting the column's face by the tolerance, it held 661 more than the two and the gap.
Booleans of bodies standing far out from the origin, worked out near it.
member.remarks: A boolean reads a corner as on a plane within the tolerance and what rounding adds to it, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates (see ). A thousand million out that is a thousandth itself, and walls of a body and its openings standing a fraction of the tolerance apart could no longer be told apart: an L 100 by 80 by 50 a hundred million out, with two blind openings whose walls stood 0.0009 apart, less a box across both walls, held 130 189.39 within a thousandth, where it holds 130 189.32, and the box less the L 28 457.23, where it holds 28 457.68. So such bodies are moved near the origin first, by whole coordinates, the boolean worked out there as it is worked out near the origin, and what it gives moved back out. The cut of a body's openings, its material as its volume, area, centroid and mass read it, a section of it and its cells are worked out so too, and so is where a point, a ray, a segment or a line stands against it (see ).
member.summary: Combining two flat shapes that lie in one plane in space.

remarks.para: combined solids and nothing else, so a and a — which are areas, not bodies — could not be combined at all, though the plane library has done it all along and a curved loop in space already does it through its own lift.

Nothing new is worked out. Both shapes are laid out in the first one's frame, the plane library answers, and the answer is lifted back, so it is exact rather than approximate. Everything comes back as , because joining two areas can leave a hole in the middle and only a face can hold one — the same reason the plane hands back .

The second shape has to lie in the first one's plane, and is refused when it does not. Projecting it in would report two plates a metre apart as overlapping and say nothing about it. This is the reading the rest of the library takes, and SharesPlaneWith on either type asks the question beforehand. Winding does not matter: a shape wound the other way round is read as the same area, not as a hole.

member.summary: Cutting a body's openings into it, so that its faces are the surface of its material.

remarks.para: A keeps its openings as whole bodies subtracted from it, not as holes cut in its faces: a plate with a bolt hole has a top face that is a whole square, and a separate box where the hole is. That is the right way to hold a model read from Tekla or IFC, and the wrong thing to hand to anything that reads the faces as the boundary of the material — a pin through the hole crosses that whole square and looks like it touches the plate.

This turns such a body into one with no openings, whose faces are exactly where the material ends: the outer faces with the parts over each opening taken away, and the walls of each opening where they run through the body. It is the boolean machinery with one operand — split the body into cells, keep the cells that are material, glue them — and already knows which cells are material, nested openings included.

Each opening cuts only the cells near it. The knives are the face planes of an opening, and a plane is infinite: slicing the whole body by every one of them turns a plate with twenty bolt holes into a grid of a thousand cells. A cell whose box does not meet an opening's box is wholly outside that opening already, so it is left alone, and the work grows with the number of openings rather than with its square.

member.summary: Booleans of solids worked out with : the second body's faces lying against the first's put onto them, and a result that is not valid worked out again within the fallback tolerance.
The separate pieces a body is made of, and one body per region two bodies share.

remarks.para: hands back the whole shared region as one body, which is right for its volume and wrong for a clash report: a beam passing through two separate plates clashes twice, and one body with two shells does not say where either clash is.

A body is split where its material does not touch: two blocks that share only an edge or a corner share no volume, so they are two pieces. A cavity stays with the piece around it, and each opening goes with every piece it reaches. The work is , which the booleans already rely on to judge one piece of material at a time.

A weld that closed the result moved it by as much again (), no more than moving its corners can. Further off than both, and a hair for the rounding, the result counts some of the material twice or not at all, and is not taken: the union of a box 100 by 60 by 40 and a cube 1.25 across standing out through three of its faces by a hair more than the tolerance came out open and, closed, held 240 001.2065, the cube counted whole, where the two less their common part hold 240 000.0032 within 0.028.

A union of two bodies that share nothing at the tolerance holds the two and the gap between them filled, or part of it, or the two less an overlap no deeper than the tolerance, or part of it: anything from the two less twice the tolerance times the area where they lie face to face to the two and the gap, no more. Like , it takes nothing over the two, the gap aside, and reads the area alike; where that takes the two less once the slab at the least, this takes the faces where the two meet the tolerance further in as well, as a block whose foot runs exactly a thousandth into a turned cube's top at its corner, closed into the two less 1.67 times the slab, needs.

The common part, or the union for a common part, is worked out by the same boolean at the same tolerance; where that one comes out open on the way too, or cannot be worked out, the result is not taken either. A result that closes as it was is taken as it is, unchecked, at no cost.

The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.

remarks.para: A difference leaves no more than the body it was taken from, and no less than that less the whole of the body taken away; a union holds the larger of the two and no more than both; a common part holds no more than the smaller. Each within the tolerance times the area it can move across: the tool's for a difference, the smaller body's otherwise, where the corners of the two stand within the tolerance of each other and are made one, and a hair more for the rounding. A slab from a model less a wall that only touched it once came back 1 172 944 cubic millimetres larger than it was, where the wall's area allows 188 650.

The volumes are the faces', which bound the material from above. A body still carrying openings, as the bodies cut by every plane of both can, holds less than its faces, so no bound from below is asked of it.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.GlueOrKeep(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Boolean,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)
member.summary: Glues the cells of both bodies cut by every plane of both, unless that does no better than an open result already found by cutting one of them, which is then kept, as it was before cutting both was tried.
member.param: The faces of the cells kept.
The place of the cell of each face; see .
The open result cutting one body gave, or null.

Whether a cell a plane could not cut is judged apart across it (see ), so that what the cells glue into, closed or not, can hold the wrong volume. The open result is taken then where it welds closed, and otherwise kept where the cells glue into another volume than it holds, beyond the tolerance times its area. A slab of a Tekla model less a tool beneath it, cut one body at a time, came out open either way, the tool cut holding what it should; cut by every plane of both, the slab kept a cell the tool's top could not cut, judged within the tool, and closed three litres short. Taken wherever there was one, though, the open result left a cut skipped on eleven parts of that model cut one after another by the parts they meet, where it would not weld closed and the cells had glued into what they should; so taken, ten of the eleven take every cut.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CombineCuttingOne(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Boolean,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,System.Boolean@,System.Int32@,System.Boolean@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Joins two bodies without openings, or takes the second out of the first, cutting one of them only.
member.param: The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
true for the union, false for less .
The result, when there is one.
For a difference, true when a clean cut found no material of either body within the other: the second takes nothing from the first, and is left null for the caller to hand the first back as it came.
How many planes of the other come near the body fewer come near, of the two.
Whether a body cut came to be cut only where the planes reach; see .
For a union worked out again, whether a cell no thicker than the tolerance lying within the other body against its face is left out; see .
member.returns: Whether anything is left, as the public methods report it; null when neither body could be cut cleanly, or two closed bodies came out open whichever was cut, for the caller to cut both by every plane of both instead. An open result found on the way is then left in .
member.remarks:
The body cut is the one fewer planes of the other come near, as for an intersection, but a difference cuts the body material is taken from where that costs about the same as cutting the other. A union keeps the cells of it beyond the other, and the other whole. For a difference, cutting the body material is taken from keeps its cells beyond the other; cutting the body taken away keeps the other whole and the cells within it turned inside out, which are the walls of the cavity and take away the part of the whole body's faces it covers. Where the whole body meets the cells, the two lie back to back in one plane, each cut its own way, and takes from both the area they share.
A difference that finds nothing of the one body within the other takes nothing, and is not glued back together from the cells at all. Glued, it gave back only what the cutting rounded: two slabs side by side within a hundredth of a millimetre of each other, the larger cut along seventy metres by planes of the smaller a few thousandths off its own faces, came back twenty thousand cubic millimetres larger than it was.

member.summary: Keeps the wanted cells of the body one way of a union or a difference cut, and glues them, with the other body where the result takes it whole; see .

The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
true for the union, false for less .
For a union worked out again, whether a cell no thicker than the tolerance lying within the other body against its face is left out.
An open result found before, or this one where it comes out open and none was.
A result closed with faces wound against each other found before, or this one where it comes out so and none was.
The result, when there is one.
For a difference, true when no material of the body cut lies within the other.
member.returns: Whether anything is left; null when two closed bodies came out open this way, or closed with faces wound against each other.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.IsUnworkable(System.Exception)

member.remarks: Thrown out of a boolean, one of these took down whatever asked for it: the conversion of a whole IFC model, when the GeoSolid3 boolean cut the openings of one beam in it. The known causes are fixed; this keeps an unknown one to the boolean it happens in, and says so in the log.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.ForWork(GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Gets the tolerance a boolean cuts and glues within: the one given, with a planar threshold no wider than the point one.
member.remarks: The cut and the glue have to agree. A plane is taken to leave a cell whole when no corner of the cell stands off it by more than the planar tolerance, so the cell can stand past it by as much, and the glue matches corners within the point tolerance. A planar tolerance wider than the point one leaves more than the glue can close: two faces of a bent bar half a degree apart, whose far corners come within five hundredths of each other's planes, came out open at a planar tolerance of five hundredths and a point tolerance of one.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.NearTheRounding(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Determines whether a union, a common part or a difference of two bodies is asked within a few roundings of their coordinates, where it reads a corner as on a plane within the planar tolerance and what rounding adds to it, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates, as the cut of openings reads it (see ): the planar tolerance of the work below that trillionth, and the point tolerance no less than four tenths of a quadrillionth of the size of the coordinates.
member.param: The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.

remarks.para: Read within the tolerance alone, a corner of a face lying in a plane of the other body is put on either side of it by rounding, and the cells are cut along lines the bodies do not have: a plate 200 by 100 by 3, turned and a hundred thousand out, less a slot 20 wide across all of it, within its rounding of 9.5E-11, was said to leave nothing, where 54 000 is left; such a plate a hundred million out less a notch 20 by 20 through one end, within 4.9E-8, came back closed, wound two ways along its sides, and 320 short; and a plate a thousand out joined to a box 50 by 20 standing through it, within half its rounding, held the two whole, 77 000 where they hold 74 000, and was trusted. A common part or a difference is read so all through. A union is taken so where it closes wound alike and holds the two less the part they share read so too (see ), and is worked out within the tolerance alone otherwise.

Of 136 800 of each, plates and blocks less, sharing and joined to each of their openings taken as a plain body, turned at random, a thousand to a hundred million out, within half the rounding to a thousand times it: 583 differences said to leave nothing and 82 unions holding the wrong volume, all trusted, are right now, as are 5 637 differences, 4 196 common parts and 4 678 unions not worked out; 40 unions are still not worked out, and none that was right moved. Further below the rounding the point tolerance holds too little of what rounding moves for the reading to pay: at a tenth of it, read so, differences and unions that were right came out wrong. There the tolerance is raised to the rounding first (see ); at every tolerance at or above a trillionth of the coordinates a boolean is worked out as it was, to the bit.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.BelowTheRounding(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Tolerance@)
member.summary: Determines whether a union, a common part or a difference of two bodies is asked below a few roundings of their coordinates, nought among it: the point tolerance of the work below four tenths of a quadrillionth of the size of the coordinates, where begins; and gives the tolerance it is worked out within there, the one asked with each of its tolerances raised to that quadrillionth, the rounding.
member.param: The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
The tolerance asked raised to the rounding; the tolerance asked where the method returns false.

remarks.para: Worked out within the tolerance asked, a corner of a face lying in a plane of the other body was put on either side of it by rounding, as it is a little above, and the point tolerance held too little of what rounding moves for a corner to be read on the plane within the rounding: at nought a plate 200 by 100 by 3 at the origin, turned, less a hole 20 by 20 through it, came back whole, 60 000, where 58 800 is left, and was trusted; a hundred thousand out, less a slot 20 wide across it, it came back whole too, where 54 000 is left; a million out, it and a slot 100 by 10 along it were said to share nothing, where they share 3 000; and a thousand out, joined to a box 50 by 20 standing through it, it held 68 588.24, where the two hold 74 000. Raised to the rounding, the operation is worked out as it is within a few roundings, a corner read as on a plane within what rounding adds, and what it gives is welded to close within the tolerance asked (see ), as the cut of openings asked below the rounding is.

Of 71 820 of each, plates and blocks less, sharing and joined to each of their openings taken as a plain body, turned at random, at the origin and a thousand to a hundred million out, at nought and a tenth to four tenths of the rounding: 17 489 differences, 11 373 common parts and 9 785 unions wrong or said to be nothing, all trusted, are right now and valid at the tolerance asked, as are 16 990 differences, 20 078 common parts and 21 741 unions that were not worked out and 487 that were right but not valid; 5 unions are still not worked out, one that was wrong is not worked out now, and none that was right moved. Worked out at the tolerance asked first and raised only where that gave nothing, those made wrong stayed so: of a third of them, 3 813 differences, 1 565 common parts and 3 250 unions. At every tolerance at or above four tenths of the rounding a boolean is worked out as it was, to the bit.

member.summary: Works out a union, a common part or a difference asked below a few roundings of the coordinates within their rounding (see ), and welds what it gives to close within the tolerance asked where it does not close by its corners within it: corners the cut leaves a rounding apart are made one, the volume moved no further than the rounding times the area, as the cut of openings asked below the rounding welds its material. Of a body that does not close within the rounding, what it gives, nothing among it for a difference or a common part, is taken only where it holds up (see ), and otherwise what the operation worked out within the tolerance asked, as it was, gives, where that holds up by the same checks; where neither does, the operation is not worked out.
member.param: The operation, as the public methods work it out within the tolerance given.
The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
The tolerance asked raised to the rounding.
What came out open where two closed bodies gave nothing closed, for a closing to try.

remarks.para: Where the weld will not close it, what the operation gives is given as it came, closed within the rounding. Of a body open at nought, as a U with cracks up to 0.0001 wide in its faces is, the result is as open as the body, and no weld closes it: refused for that, 4 966 of 12 000 differences of such a U and a box at nought, holding what the two leave but for what the cracks hold, would have been refused with the rest.

Nothing such a body gives is checked on the way, as what two closed bodies give is, and within the rounding the operation is no longer turned down where the tolerance alone turned it down: a cube 10 across cracked 0.0001 wide along its top, its bottom and a side, at the origin, less a box 3 across turned inside it, came back whole, 999.998, where 973 is left, and was not worked out within the tolerance alone. What does not hold up is not taken: what the tolerance alone gives is taken in its place where it holds up by the same checks, and the operation is not worked out otherwise. Kept where the tolerance alone gave anything, what did not hold up was as a rule wrong: the cube less a slab thousands long through it, sharing 249.85, came back whole, 999.998, where 750.15 is left. Of 17 178 booleans of such a cube and a body through it at nought, 742 came out more than 0.01, what the cracks move, from what the uncracked cube gives, 429 differences, 2 common parts and 311 unions, and 126 were said to be nothing; 14 unions still do, with slabs thousands long whose faces stand off flat, 0.013 to 3.3 off of 480 000 to 58 million, less than those faces move the slab's own volume, and 4 of 15 698 within 0.01 are not worked out now. Of 36 000 of a U so cracked and a box, 4 372 differences, 2 common parts and 1 007 unions came out wrong, and 66 differences and 733 common parts were said to be nothing: 1 difference and 35 unions still come out wrong, and 202 differences and 29 unions of 13 630 within 0.01 of the uncracked U, none of them valid at nought, are not worked out now, the check, the common part of the two, not worked out within the rounding for most of them.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.HoldsUpOpen(System.String,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Says why what a union, a common part or a difference of two bodies worked out within the rounding gave does not hold up, where either body does not close within it; null where it does, or where both close.
member.param: The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
The tolerance the operation was worked out within.
Whether what does not hold up is the result, and not the common part of the two that a difference or a union is checked by, which another result of the same two would not get past either.

remarks.para: A common part lies within both bodies: one with a corner further outside a body that closes than a thousand roundings of the coordinates does not hold up. Of two bodies neither of which closes, each is read as though it did, and a common part holds up only where it has no corner outside either and leaves out no corner of one lying inside the other (see ); a common part said to be nothing holds up only where the skin of neither body runs into the other. A difference holds the first less the common part of the two, and a union the two less it, the common part worked out within the rounding too and holding up as a common part does; one that comes out not worked out, or as nothing where the skin of either body runs into the other, says nothing of the result, which does not hold up then either. A difference said to be nothing holds nothing. The volumes are read as reads them, each from a corner of its own. Faces that do not close hold a volume only from where it is read: read from anywhere in their box it moves by no more than a third of their open area, the faces' areas summed with their normals, times the diagonal of the box, and the result and the common part, which share the open faces of the bodies, by as much again between them. The volumes have to add up within twice that for each body that does not close, the tolerance times the area of the two, what the faces lying off flat move the volumes that enter (see ), and a hair for the rounding.

Read so, the cube 10 across cracked 0.0001 wide, its open area 0.0005, moves by no more than 0.0029. Less a box 3 across turned inside it, it came back whole, 999.998, where the cube less their common part, 27, holds 973.0; turned, joined to a box 7.5 by 6.2 through its corner whose floor stands 0.003 below its own, it held 1 232.638, where the two less their common part, 125, hold 1 107.638; and turned another way, its common part with a slab leaning through it, sharing 76.79, was the whole cube, its corners outside the slab. Two unions of such a cube and a slab thousands long, which hold what the uncracked cube gives within 0.01, missed the two less their common part by 0.023 and 0.57, within what the faces of the four off flat move, 0.18 and 16.2 at most, and hold up now; a union 36 over the two, of the cube cracked 0.001 wide and such a slab, their faces off flat moving 13.4 at most, does not. Turned another way and joined to a box through its corner, the cube held 1 010.4075, 0.0115 short of the two, and missed the two less their common part by 0.0098: within the open area of the cube times the diagonal of its box, 0.0133, and not within twice a third of that, 0.0089. Less a slab five million long sharing 27.28 with it, the cube came back whole, 27.28 over the cube less their common part, within the 44 the slab's faces off flat move the slab's volume, which does not enter a difference.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FlatForWork(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Gets a body as a boolean works on it: wound outwards, its openings too, and every face flat within the planar tolerance of the work.

remarks.para: A boolean reads which way the faces are wound: the faces a cut lays across a cell face out of it, the cells are kept by the side of the other body they fall on, and two faces meet back to back where they face apart. A body wound inwards came back in cells with its own faces facing in and the new ones out, a tool wound inwards was taken for material, and a plate less a duct so wound held more than the plate. Turned the right way out first, either is the body it is.

A face can be flat only to the wider planar tolerance a caller allowed: a modeller's cut leaves some a few hundredths out, as Tekla Structures left the top face of a notched beam 0.04 mm out at one corner. Cut at the tighter tolerance of the work, a piece of such a face is refused as not flat and leaves a hole. It is split into triangles on its own corners first instead, each exactly flat, which keeps the body closed and moves nothing. A body wound outwards with every face flat enough comes back as it is.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Flat(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Gets a body with every face flat within the planar tolerance of the work, its openings too.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.IsFlatWithin(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3,System.Double)

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.SharedPlanes(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoAabb3}@)
member.summary: Collects the face planes of both bodies, with duplicates removed, and the reach of each: the box of the faces lying on it; see .
member.remarks: Both bodies are cut by this one set rather than each by the other. That costs a few more cells and buys the thing that makes gluing work: where the two bodies meet, both sides have been carved by the same knives, so the two faces at the interface are the same polygon and cancel.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.KnivesFor(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoAabb3}@)

member.remarks: Near the body, the surface of the other lies on the planes of its faces that come near the body, so a cell crossing none of them does not cross that surface, and one point inside the cell says which side of it the whole cell is on. The body's own openings need cutting along only where the other is: a cell anywhere else is outside the other, and dropped whatever it holds. Each plane comes with its reach, the box of the faces lying on it, as gives it.

member.remarks: A region no face of a closed body crosses lies wholly inside it or wholly outside it, which is what lets a cell away from a plane's faces go uncut by it. A skin with a gap has no inside for the region to lie in, and the cells of the bodies of a boolean either of which does not close are cut by every plane wherever it runs, as they were: a cube 10 across cracked along its bottom, top and side, open read within nought, joined within nought to a flat body of 111 955 cubic millimetres it dips into, was not worked out cut every plane everywhere, and cut each plane where its faces are from the first cell came out 335 short of the 112 902.75 the two hold, trusted. A cell is read against the openings too, the other body's and its own body's, by the same one point, so each of those has to close as well. It is asked only once a body is in more than cells, so that a boolean of fewer pays nothing for it.

member.remarks: A plane that does not actually cut a cell leaves it alone, so the number of pieces grows only with the number of planes that really pass through the body rather than with how many were offered.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.SplitIntoCells(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPlane3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Divides a body by a set of planes, saying whether every plane that crossed a piece divided it.
member.param: The planes to divide it by.
false when a plane had corners of a piece beyond the tolerance on both sides and still left it whole.

member.summary: Divides a body by a set of planes, each where it reaches once the body is in more than cells, saying whether every plane that crossed a piece it was put to divided it, and which did not.
member.param: The other body of the boolean, which with the subject has to close for a plane to cut only where its faces are; see .
The planes to divide it by.
The reach of each plane, in their order: the box of the faces lying on it (see ); null where every plane reaches every cell.
false when a plane had corners of a piece it was put to beyond the tolerance on both sides and still left it whole.
Whether the planes came to cut only where they reach: the cells passed and both bodies close. Only then is read by ; below it every plane was put to every cell, as it always was.
The planes that did so, each once; null where they are not wanted.
The reach of each plane in , in its order; null where it is not wanted, as it is not where is null.
member.remarks:
Once the body is in more than cells, and where both bodies close (see ), a plane cuts a cell only where the cell's box comes within the tolerance of its reach. A face of the other body has to come near a cell to cross it, and far from its own faces a plane's cut makes cells only for the cells to be judged alike: the planes of a spiral ramp 7 600 wide in 56 facets over half a turn cross a spiral girder 600 by 500 in 66 facets, lying 100 into the ramp's outer edge, at many places along the turn, and cut by every one of them wherever it ran, the girder came apart into 263 911 cells for the common part of the two, which took 42 seconds. Cut so, it makes 18 345, in 2.5.
A cell is still on one side of every face of the other body that reaches it. A cell's box only shrinks as it is cut, so a face whose box comes within the tolerance of a cell's box came within it of the box of every cell the cell was cut from, and the face's plane, whose reach holds the face's box, was put to the cell it was cut from then: it cut that cell, left it on one side, or crossed it uncut and is among . A face whose box does not come within the tolerance of a cell's box does not reach the cell at all. So a cell crossing no plane it was left uncut by crosses no face of the other body, and one point inside it says which side of that body the whole cell is on, as before. The cells of a plane's two sides no longer meet face to face where it cuts one and not the other, and their faces lying back to back are cancelled by the area they share; see .

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CellsCutEverywhere
member.summary: How many cells a body is cut into by every plane wherever it runs before each plane cuts it only where its faces are; see .
member.remarks: Cut every plane everywhere, the cells of a body meet face to face, and what the booleans give of one cut into no more than these is as it was, to the bit: none of 72 000 booleans of U bodies, 17 452 of cracked cubes, 32 400 of a cube and boxes about its faces nor 600 cuts of plates with blind holes moves. Each plane cut where its faces are from the first, the cells of a plane's two sides meet face to face only where it cuts both, and the faces of the cells glued and merged come out otherwise: a beam 2 000 by 200 by 300 less a bar 16 across bent through a right angle in forty steps, its end 0.001 off the beam's floor, both turned in space, was cut cleanly into 130 cells where every plane everywhere leaves 2 995 and one it could not cut, and its cells merged held 119 941 187.15 where 119 941 219.82 is left; 1 093 of the U bodies and 196 of the cracked cubes moved, within the tolerance times their area. The bodies cut into thousands of cells are those every plane of the other crosses again and again.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CellsMade

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.IsSliver(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Checks whether a piece is thinner than twice the point tolerance, so that no point of it is further than that from its skin.
member.remarks: A plane crossing such a piece may leave nothing on one side wide enough to be a polygon, and fail to cut it. That leaves it no worse judged than it is anyway, by the middle of its thickness; a cut counted unclean for it was thrown away whole. A slab cut by the planes of its neighbour kept a wedge a hundredth of a millimetre at its widest, three metres long, which two planes crossed and could not cut, and the difference went on to cut both slabs by every plane of both: sixteen seconds, and sixty-nine thousand cubic millimetres more than the two share; the other way round, it came out open.

member.summary: Whether a cell a plane crossed and could not cut holds material on its two sides that would be judged apart: kept on one side of the plane and not on the other.
member.param: The planes that crossed a cell and could not cut it.
The body the cells were cut from.
The body deciding inside from outside.
true where the cells within that body are kept, false where those beyond it are.
member.remarks:
Such a cell is judged by one point of it, which is right for both sides where the other body lies the same way to both. Where it does not, part of the cell is misjudged, and the answer with it: a slab wrapping the corner of another was cut by the other's planes into a cell holding the tip of the wedge the two share and the part of the slab beyond the other's end, joined at the corner, where the other's end could not cut it; judged by a point beyond the end, the cell was outside the other, and the common part lost 6.4 m of the wedge.
A point either side of each plane alone misses a cell the other body takes an edge or a corner of, every such point lying beyond it. A cell of a body that closes is read too as reads a piece of a body cut for its openings: by the middles of its parts either side of each plane, of the four two planes make, and of the eight three make that meet within the other body's box. A cube 10 across whose top, bottom and one side are each two faces meeting along a crack 0.0001 wide, less a box x from -4.1 to 4.993, y from -3.04 to 5.008 and z from 4.9986 to 11.03, none of whose planes would cut it, was one cell read beyond the box by every such point: taken whole, the difference held 1 000 cubic millimetres where it holds 874.94.
The middle of a part is read only where it lies in the material of the cell, out of the body's openings: a part of a cell that is not convex can have its middle outside it. A U 30 across with a notch 10 wide, none of the planes of a box standing in the notch cutting it, had the middle of its part above the box's floor, its two arms, in the notch at (15, 5, 7.25), read as in the box, and was taken for misjudged where the box touches none of its material. Nor is a cell read where the other body does not close, having no inside to be part in.
Where one plane crosses a cell, or two, or three that meet at a point within the other body's box, or three of which two are parallel, the parts all of them make are read too, each middle wherever it lies (see ). A box dipping 0.088 into an arm of a U, its sides and its floor crossing the U uncut, takes 2.55 between its sides and over its floor that no one or two of its planes part from the rest; the parts they do part from it held the box's piece with more of the U beyond the box, or had their middles in the notch, and the U was left whole: 2 667.83 cubic millimetres, trusted, where 2 665.28 is left.

member.summary: Whether, of the parts every plane crossing a cell makes of it, where no more than three do, one holding more than the tolerance times the cell's area has its middle within the other body and another beyond it, each middle read where it lies out of the openings, in the cell's material or not.
member.param: The planes crossing it that could not cut it, each with the other body.
Whether a middle is read, given the cell and the middle.
member.remarks: The cell lies to one side of every other plane of the other body whose faces come near it, and a part of it bounded by every plane crossing it to one side of those too, and no face whose box stays clear of the cell's comes into the cell's box, which holds the part and its middle; so no face of the other body runs between the part and its middle: the middle, outside the material where the cell is not convex, lies within the other body where the part does. Not read: more than three planes, three meeting at a point outside the other body's box (see ), three meeting along one line, and three parallel.

The body the cells were cut from.
The body deciding inside from outside.
true where the cells within that body are kept, false where those beyond it are.
The reach of each plane in , or null; see .
member.remarks: Each such part lies to one side of every plane of the other body whose faces come near the cell, so wholly within the other body or wholly beyond it, as its middle does (see ), and what the parts judged otherwise than the cell hold is what the cell puts on the wrong side. says only whether there is any, and weighs a part against the tolerance times the area of its cell, which says nothing of what is left: a cracked box dipping 0.088 into an arm of a cracked U, less the U, its cells cut by every plane of both judged apart, was left whole, 478.10 cubic millimetres, trusted, with nothing else to take, where 475.54 is left; its cells hold 2.554 on the wrong side, and the box was 2.554 over. A box dipping 0.028 into the arm, the U cut by the box's planes one cell judged alike on both sides of them, its 0.84 beyond the box no more than the tolerance times the U's area, said the box took nothing of the U, and the box was left whole, 0.84 over, where the tolerance times its area is 0.45. Of 1 767 differences of 45 000 booleans of such U's and boxes weighed so, it came within a thousandth of what the result was off by on 1 649, and on none was it within the tolerance times the area of the result where the result was off by more, nor past it where it was not; the furthest read 6.02 where the result was 4.74 off.

Whether the cells kept are joined to the other body whole, as a union that came out wound against itself is worked out again: a cell no thicker than the tolerance, read on the other's skin, is then taken as within it where its side lying nearest flush on a face of the other faces the same way, so that it is not held twice. A beam whose end ran exactly a thousandth into a column, joined to it within a thousandth, kept the slab of its end within the column, the column whole beside it, and came out wound against itself, 101 cubic millimetres more than the two less their common part. Only then: read so by every union, a chip exactly the tolerance deep is cut by the union where the common part and the differences read it as nothing; see .

member.remarks: A cell no thicker than the tolerance lies within it of a face of the other with both its sides: a slab inside the top of a box has its top on the box's, facing the same way, and its floor the slab's thickness beneath, facing the other way; one on top of the box has its floor on the box's top, facing the other way, and its top above. The side lying nearer says which.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.IsMaterial(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Double,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3@,System.Nullable{GeometryHelper.Tolerance}@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Checks whether a cell holds material of the body it was cut from, and finds a point inside it.
member.remarks:
The cells come from the gross boundary, so one of them can be filling an opening. Every plane bounding an opening is among the knives, so no cell straddles the wall of one and a single sample settles the whole cell.
Dropping such a cell is what carves the opening into the result. The face between a cell that is kept and one that is dropped is traversed once rather than twice, so it survives the gluing and becomes the wall of the cavity — which is why the result needs no openings of its own.
member.param: The body the cell was cut from.
What rounding the coordinates of the bodies of the operation can add to the tolerance (): a cell no thicker than the two together is within the tolerance of nothing.
The tolerance the sample is read within where the tolerance given reads it on the skin of another body; null where that reading stands. See .
Whether a cell thicker than the tolerance and thinner than twice it is left out where, across its thickness, all of it but the tolerance from one side lies in an opening; see .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.LocateSample(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Nullable{GeometryHelper.Tolerance})
member.summary: Locates the point a cell is judged by against another body: within the tolerance, and where that reads it on the body's skin, within the finer tolerance the cell's thickness allows, where it has one.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.IsAlongOpening(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3,System.Double,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Double)
member.summary: Whether a cell thicker than the tolerance and thinner than twice it, its middle on the skin of an opening, lies in the opening across its thickness all but the tolerance from one side, read within the rounding of the coordinates.
member.param: The body the cell was cut from.
Where the cell's thickness starts, on its skin.
What rounding the coordinates can add to the tolerance; see .
member.remarks: A plane of an opening cuts every cell that reaches the opening's box, and cut in at once a plate's first cells reach all of its openings. Twelve boxes hidden 0.01 inside the faces of a plate 300 by 200 by 12, cut within a hundredth, the first 1.7E-7 deeper than the tolerance, had a skin cut off the whole plate by the plane of that box's floor, and the fourth, 5.7E-6 nearer the faces than the tolerance, kept that skin over and under it: the plate came out valid and held 9.68 cubic millimetres more than the most its skins can leave. Cut in alone, the plane of the fourth's own floor lies within the tolerance of the face and cuts nothing, and the skin goes with the box. A cell so cut holds no more than the tolerance of material beside the opening where, across its thickness, all of it but the tolerance from the side on the body's own skin lies in the opening, read within the rounding, and it is left out as the opening alone leaves it. A wall thicker than the tolerance between two parts of an opening is not: across it, the tolerance in from either side is still out of the opening. Nor is a cell whose side out of the opening is not the body's skin: read from either side, of 4 800 cracked cubes less two boxes set as much as a whole millimetre apart or into each other, six came out otherwise, two of them further from what they hold, one by 0.06 cubic millimetres.

member.summary: Whether a point lies on a face of a body, its openings not read.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryGetInteriorPoint(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3@)
member.summary: Finds a point strictly inside a body.
member.remarks: The centroid of a concave body can fall outside it, so it is checked rather than trusted. When it fails, the search steps a little way inwards from the middle of each surface triangle, along the inward normal. The step shrinks on each round because a body can be thinner in one place than the first step assumes, and a step that overshoots comes out the far side.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryGetMidpointOfThinBody(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3@,System.Double@,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3@)
member.summary: Finds a point inside a body too thin for to find one: the middle of its thickness under the middle of one of its largest surface triangles.
member.remarks: A ray from inside a triangle of a closed skin, run along the inward normal, is in the body from the triangle to where it next meets the skin, so halfway there it is as deep in the body as that ray goes. The point is checked all the same, within a tolerance a quarter of that depth: a skin wound the wrong way somewhere sends the ray out of the body instead. The depth is handed back with the point, and where the thickness starts on the skin.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryGlue(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)
member.summary: Glues a collection of cell faces into one closed body.
member.remarks:
A face between two cells that were both kept is interior to the result, and it appears twice among the collected faces, once each way round. Dropping both leaves exactly the outer skin — when the two copies match vertex for vertex, which they need not; see for the pairs that do not. The survivors are then merged where they are coplanar and touching, which undoes the subdivision the cutting introduced.
Taking from two faces the area they share is worked out in the plane, where a piece of either is dropped as a seam when it is no wider on average than the point tolerance, and two edges within the tolerance of each other leave a needle between them; the faces beside keep their edges all the same, and a skin closed before it is open after. Each sliver it is open by, no wider than four point tolerances, is closed by a face across it, where that closes the skin; see .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryGlue(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)

member.param: For each face, the cell or the body whole it came from; null where that is not known.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryCloseBackToBackGaps(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)
member.summary: Closes the slivers taking faces lying back to back from each other left a skin open by, where the faces were closed before and the slivers close them again.
member.remarks: A union of an I 11 long and a prism of twelve sides passing the corner of its flange came out open twice. Taken from the end of the I, the prism's face there left a corner of it 0.0006 square millimetres across, every side of it longer than the point tolerance, which the clipping took for a seam and dropped, while the faces beside it kept their edges round it. And a corner of the prism stood 0.002 off the flange's edge, so that taken from the flange's side, its face left a needle 5.9 long beside that edge, on the piece of the side kept. Each is a sliver, and a face across each closes the union.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.DropMatchedPairs(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Drops each face together with the first later face that is it turned over, vertex for vertex: the two sides of a wall between two cells that were both kept.
member.remarks: Two such faces have the same corners, so the corners of their boxes lie within the tolerance of each other. The faces are filed by the low corner of their box, and each is compared only with the later faces filed near its own — in the order, and by the test, that comparing it with every later face would use, so the same pairs are dropped without comparing every face with every other.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CancelBackToBack(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Takes from the faces still lying back to back in one plane the area they share.

remarks.para: The two copies of a face between kept cells need not match vertex for vertex. A cut that reaches the cell on one side and not the one on the other leaves one copy in two pieces, or with a point along its edge that the other copy lacks, and the exact match lets both through. They would stand inside the body as a sheet of no thickness: the volume never notices, since the two cancel, but everything that reads the boundary does — a point a millimetre from the sheet measured a millimetre to the boundary, the surface mesh carried the sheet, and splitting the body into pieces failed on it.
Whatever two faces lying back to back share is inside the body however it was cut, so it goes from both, and what is left of either is boundary.

Two faces lie back to back when either lies in the plane of the other, and each is cut in its own plane, the other laid out in it (): a small face a hair out of a long one's plane lies in it, but the long one's far end stands off the small one's by more than the tolerance.

What a face shares goes with one face lying against it, the nearest, and not with each. A cell thinner than the tolerance lies against its neighbour on one side and against its own far side on the other, both within the tolerance of it: the thin end of a wedge a cutter's face left on a slab, where the face crossed the slab's own at 5E-5 rad, lay against the slab beyond the cutter's face, in that face's plane, and against the slab's wall, a few hundredths off it. Taken from each, the wedge's face took the wall with it as well as the slab's face against it, and the slab was left open by a wall 750 long and 400 high. A face lying against two that overlap each other is paired with the nearer, the one in its own plane where there is one, and a pair is cancelled only where each takes the other.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CancelBackToBack(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Takes from the faces still lying back to back in one plane the area they share, as does, but for two faces of one closed piece.
member.param: For each face, the cell or the body whole it came from; null where that is not known.
member.remarks: A cell is closed, and two of its faces facing apart within the tolerance of each other are its two sides where it is thinner than that, not a wall inside the result: taken from each other, they leave the cell's edges round the hole. A block whose low step's top was out of flat by 0.0012, read as triangles, less a box whose top lay along it, was cut by the box's top into cells a hair thick between that plane and the triangles, and each such cell's top and bottom were taken for back to back with each other, 37 000 square millimetres more of the top than of what lay under it: the difference came out open.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CancelStrips(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Takes from each other, both laid out within the tolerance of the work, the faces left lying back to back where one is a strip narrower than the global tolerance: what they share bounds no material.
member.param: The faces left once the faces lying back to back took from each other.
For each face, the cell or the body whole it came from; null where that is not known.

remarks.para: A face is laid out in its plane within the global tolerance however fine the work (see ), and a strip narrower than that is nothing there: it shares nothing with a face against it, and nothing is taken from it. Where the cut of openings left a cell that thin between two walls a fraction of the tolerance apart, its face and the strip of the face against it stayed, a sheet inside the material, bounding none. An L 100 by 80 by 50 with two blind openings whose far walls stood 0.0009 apart, cut with the opening down from the top first, kept a sheet 0.0009 by 13 under that opening, its area 0.0234 too much; a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two openings up from its floor whose ceilings stood 0.00015 apart kept one 0.00015 by 100 beside the first opening, 0.03 too much.

Such a strip is read again, laid out within the tolerance of the work with the faces against it, as faces lying back to back are read: two of one cell are never taken so, its two sides where it is thinner than the tolerance (see ). A face no strip lies against comes out as it came.

A strip more than a million out, as reads the reach, is read so only within a tolerance times what rounding can move a corner off a plane there, and is otherwise left as it came. A body a thousand million out is cut 3.9E6 from the origin (see ), and its strips are read; a boolean asked below the gate of the far frame is worked out where the bodies stand, within the rounding, and read so there too, 13 of 16 800 booleans of such prisms ten million to a thousand million out, at nought to a millionth, that were right came out wrong, by as much as 0.68, or not valid.

member.summary: How far out the bodies of a boolean must reach before they are moved near the origin for it: 2^20, a little over a kilometre.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FarTimesSize
member.summary: How many times the size of their box the bodies of a boolean must reach out before they are moved near the origin for it.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FarLift
member.summary: How far from the origin, as a part of how far out the bodies reach, the least corner of their box is put in the frame they are worked out in: a 256th, so that a trillionth of the coordinates there, which a boolean reads a corner on a plane within, is still at least thirty times what rounding moved their corners by where they stand.
member.remarks: The corners of bodies far out were rounded where they stand, to half a ten-millionth a thousand million out, and walls meant to lie in one plane, of two openings or of an opening and the body, stand that far off it. Put at the origin, where a trillionth of the coordinates is a ten-thousand-millionth, such walls read as standing apart, and the walls of openings a fraction of the tolerance apart could not be told from them: of 1 196 unions, common parts and differences ten million to a thousand million out at a thousandth, 241 were wrong, and 190 were so moved to the least corner, 14 put a 256th of the reach out, 8 a 512th and 41 a 1 024th.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FarFinest
member.summary: How fine a tolerance, as a part of how far out the bodies reach, a boolean may be asked within and still be moved near the origin for it: a trillionth of the coordinates in the frame, what rounding can move a corner off a plane there.
member.remarks: Finer, the corners carry more rounding from where they stand than the frame allows for: moved near the origin at nought, a trillionth and a thousand-millionth, 58 of 5 292 such booleans that were right came out wrong or were not worked out. There the boolean raises the tolerance to the rounding where the bodies stand, as before; see BelowTheRounding.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FarFrame
member.summary: The frame a boolean of bodies far out is worked out in: their coordinates less an origin on each axis, the least corner of the box of all of them less of their reach, where every coordinate of theirs along it lies between half and twice that origin, so that each difference is exact (Sterbenz's lemma), and a corner moved in and back out is the one given, to the bit. Only the corners the boolean makes are rounded, once, as they are moved out: to about a ten-millionth of a millimetre a thousand million out, ten thousand times finer than the default tolerance.

remarks.para: Bodies are moved only where they reach more than out and more than times the size of their box, and where neither the point nor the planar tolerance asked is finer than of how far out they reach: otherwise a boolean is worked out where the bodies stand, as it was, to the bit. Bodies moved into a frame are not moved again by what the boolean asks of them. A face or a body the boolean hands back untouched goes out as it was given, the very one; a polygon moved in has its normal and area measured again where it lands, as a body built there has them.

The cut of a body's openings, the material its volume, area, centroid and mass are measured on, a section of it and its cells are worked out in a frame of the body alone, by the same rules; a volume and an area are the same in the frame as out of it, and what has a place, a corner, a plane, a box, is moved back.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FarBody
member.summary: A body far out moved into the frame it is asked where a point, a ray, a segment or a line stands against it: the frame of the body alone, as makes it, the body moved in once and kept with it, the probe moved in with it for each question, and what has a place in the answer moved back out.

remarks.para: A body is a value and cannot change, and its frame is set by its box alone, so the body moved in is made the first time it is asked within a tolerance the frame admits and kept, as the cut of its material is: two threads that make it make the same body, either of which is complete. What the moved body works out and keeps of its own, the regions its gaps are measured with among them, is kept with it, as it is with the body where it stands.

A probe is moved coordinate by coordinate, as the body is. One near the body moves exactly, by Sterbenz's lemma, and comes back out as it was given; one standing as far again from it moves to the rounding of its distance from the frame's origin, a part in ten thousand million million of how far it stands from the body.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.LiesIn(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPlane3,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Determines whether every one of some points lies on a plane, within the planar tolerance.
member.param: The points fixing a shape: its corners, and a point along each curved edge.
member.returns: true when the whole shape lies in the plane, so that work in the plane's frame is exact.
member.remarks: A shape lies in a plane when all of it does. Planes parallel within the angle tolerance with one point of the shape on this one are not enough: the angle tolerance is a whole degree, so a shape turned half a degree about a line through that point passed — a metre long, its far end stood nine millimetres off the plane, and it was projected onto it without a word. Two faces crossing at a shallow angle read the same way as two lying back to back, which is how a boolean once took a piece of real boundary for the inside of the body.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.SubtractLaidOut(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Takes one face from another lying back to back with it, in the plane of the first: the second is laid out in that plane whether or not all of it lies there.
member.remarks: For the gluing of a boolean (), which pairs two faces when either lies in the plane of the other. A small face a hair out of a long one's plane lies in it, but the long one's far end can stand millimetres off the small one's, and taking the long face from the small one was refused as lying in another plane, which threw out the whole boolean. Near the small face, where anything is taken from it, the two planes are one within the tolerance, so the long face laid out in the small one's plane takes away what it should, and what is left of the small face stays where it was.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Combine(GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Combination,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoCoordinateSystem3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Combines two faces of one plane by laying them out in it, combining them there and lifting the answer back.
member.remarks: A face with no area left once laid out — a sliver whose corners come within the plane's point tolerance of one another — adds nothing and takes nothing away: sharing with it gives nothing, taking it out changes nothing, and joining it or keeping what the two do not share gives the other. Laid out as it was, it threw, and took with it the union or difference of two bodies whose gluing compared such a sliver with the face lying against it.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Flatten(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoCoordinateSystem3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3)
member.summary: Lays a face out in a frame, or gives null when nothing with an area is left of it there.
member.remarks: The plane merges corners within the global tolerance, a thousandth by default, whatever tolerance the work is asked within, so a strip of a face thinner than that is nothing to it: where the cut of a body's openings glued its cells, the strip of one cell's face between two walls 0.00095 apart neither took from the face against it nor was taken from, and a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two blind openings whose ceilings stood that far apart came out of the cut open, 1.05 short. Laid out within the tolerance asked, every face, in every gluing, keeps corners the plane merged within a thousandth, and that is worse: of 25 200 unions, common parts and differences of prisms with such openings and boxes, between nought and a ten-thousandth, 37 that were right came out wrong or not worked out, a box less a prism at nought by 26 860, the prism's openings lost; floored at a trillionth of the coordinates, the same. Laying out again only a face the plane leaves nothing of, and only where a boolean's cut of openings came out open, at a millionth and below within a million of the origin, closed that plate's cut the first time but moved no boolean of those prisms from right, wrong or not worked out, the cut being cut again already (see ); further out it turned 15 not worked out into trusted and wrong. The layout is left as it was; a strip it leaves nothing of, still lying against a face once the gluing has taken what it could, is read again laid out within the tolerance of the work (see ).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FlattenFinely(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoCoordinateSystem3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Lays a face out in a frame merging only corners within the tolerance of the work, or gives null when nothing with an area is left of it there; for the strips reads.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Lift(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoCoordinateSystem3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace2[],GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Lifts the faces the plane gave back into the plane the two shapes share.
member.remarks: Each piece is built as thin as the point tolerance allows (), since the faces it came from can be that thin: a body cut near a corner keeps slivers a few thousandths across, and the gluing of a union takes such faces from one another here. Built within the ordinary tolerance, a sliver of the answer threw, and took the whole union with it. A piece with nothing left of it once lifted, its corners within the point tolerance of one another or of a line, is dropped rather than thrown over: the plane draws finer than space does, and such a piece has no area to speak of.
