member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryCutOpenings(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Turns a body with openings into one without, whose faces are the surface of its material, within a tolerance.
member.param: The body with every opening cut into it, or the body itself when it has none; null when the method returns false.
member.returns: true when some material is left; false when the openings take all of it, which is an outcome and not an error, as it is for the booleans, or when the cut cannot be worked out, which is logged.
member.remarks: The material of a closed body with closed openings is closed as reads it, as a boolean's is, or not given. Where cutting the openings in at once leaves it open, it is welded within the tolerance, and where that does not close it the openings are taken out one at a time by a difference, which tries more ways of cutting and keeps only what closes; where one will not come out so, or what they leave is not valid as Validate reads it, wound two ways where the differences met, the method returns false. Each difference reads a corner as on a plane within the planar tolerance and the rounding of the coordinates, a trillionth of their size, as cutting them in at once does: within the tolerance alone, a plate 300 by 200 by 12, turned and far from the origin, with twelve holes ending 0.01 under its top to within a millionth, cut within a hundredth, came out valid and 130.70 cubic millimetres short of the plate less every hole through; it holds 666 668.11, within what its skins can leave. They are taken out so too where a plane of an opening runs through the body and will not cut it, leaving a piece part in the opening and part out of it, which cut in at once would be kept or dropped whole. A plate 300 by 200 by 12 with two blind holes ending 0.015 under its top, turned and far from the origin, came out of the cut within a hundredth open by four edges 0.015 long; the holes are taken out one at a time, and it closes, holding 711 120.61 as measures it. Cut in together, each opening keeps or loses a skin the tolerance thin as it would cut in alone: a plate with twelve holes ending 0.01 under its top to within a millionth, one 2.0E-6 nearer the top, cut within a hundredth, kept a skin over that one that the plane of another hole's floor cut off the whole plate, and came out valid and 3.71 cubic millimetres over the most its skins can leave; it holds what they can leave now. Where the point tolerance is below the rounding of the coordinates, a quadrillionth of the largest of them, the openings are cut within that rounding, as the queries read them; a planar tolerance below it alone changes nothing. Where cutting them in together leaves the material open they are cut in at once one at a time, each kept only where it closes, not taken out by a difference, which within the rounding can come back closed and wrong, and the corners the cut leaves a rounding apart are made one where that closes the material within the tolerance given. Cut at a tolerance of nought, a plate 200 by 100 by 3 turned about in space, with a hole 20 by 20 through it, came back as a shell of 7 faces, its bottom lost, and the method returned true; it comes back closed, holding 58 800. Walls of two openings, or of an opening and the body, standing apart within the tolerance of one plane are cut within a finer tolerance, where what that gives closes within the one asked: an L 100 by 80 by 50, a million out, with two blind openings 27 apart whose walls stood 0.0009 apart across it, cut within a thousandth, held 153 674.08 where it holds 153 673.56, the second opening's wall cut in the plane of the first's. A body far out is cut near the origin and its material moved back, as a boolean of such bodies is worked out. See for what it refuses, what the measures of the body read at nought, and a body far out.
member.exception: Thrown when the body is null.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.WithWallsApart(GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Operation,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)
member.summary: Works out a union, a common part or a difference of two bodies within a finer tolerance where walls of one of them and its openings stand apart within the tolerance of one plane (see ): the openings of each cut into it within that tolerance, as cuts them, and the operation worked out on the two so cut; what it gives is taken where it is made and closes within the tolerance asked.
member.param: The operation, as the public methods work it out within the tolerance given.
The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
What the operation gives; null when the method returns false.
What came out open where two closed bodies gave nothing closed, for a closing to try.
member.returns: true where such walls stand apart and the operation so worked out made a body that closes; otherwise, false, and the operation is worked out as before.
member.remarks: A boolean cuts the openings of a body into it at once, and the plane of one opening cut the whole of what it reached: a plane of another within the tolerance of it was read as that plane, however far away, as the cut of openings read it. An L 100 by 80 by 50 with two blind openings 27 apart whose walls stood 0.0009 apart across it, less a box 65 by 20 by 40 across both walls, within a thousandth or a hundredth, held 130 189.39 one way round and 130 189.26 the other, where it holds 130 189.32, and the box less the L 28 457.23 and 28 457.88, where it holds 28 457.68. Of 4 800 unions, common parts and differences of prisms with two or three such openings, turned about in space or not, at the origin and a thousand to a thousand million out, and boxes, at 1E-3 and 1E-2, 1 363 that were wrong are right now, every one a million out and nearer among them, and none that was right moved, but in its last bits; at a millionth and below, where no walls stood so near, nothing changed, to the bit. Where a wall of the other body lies within the tolerance of the plane of a wall of either, or the finer tolerance would come within a few roundings of the coordinates (see ), the boolean is worked out as before: of 4 800 more, a face of each box a tenth to six tenths of the tolerance off the plane of a wall, 5 changed, all to right.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FinerRoundings
member.summary: How many times what rounding can move a corner off a plane, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates, the finer tolerance a boolean is worked out within where walls stand apart (see ) has to be; a boolean whose finer tolerance would be less is worked out as before.
member.remarks: Of 4 800 unions, common parts and differences of prisms with such openings and boxes, at 1E-3 and 1E-2, 3 that were right came out wrong within a finer tolerance two to four times that trillionth, all ten million and more out, the worst 0.98 off a thousand million out. None does within eight times it, and up to a million out every one still comes out right; 354 further out that came out right within the finer tolerance are worked out as before, and wrong.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.MaterialWithin(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)
member.summary: A body with its openings cut into it within a finer tolerance, as cuts them, where what that gives closes within the tolerance asked; the body itself where it has none.

Works out a union, a common part or a difference of two bodies again on the material of each whose openings, cut in at once by the cells each opening reaches, come out open, or with a piece of it judged whole part in an opening and part out (see ), whether or not the boolean's own cut, cut again, closes (see ): the openings of that body cut into it as cuts them, and the operation worked out on what that gives. What it gives, made and closed within the tolerance the boolean works within, is taken where what the operation gave as before is not made, not valid as reads it, or holds another volume, further from it than the planar tolerance and the rounding of the coordinates times its area; more than a million out, only where it is made, valid and holds another volume. Asked above a millionth, the operation is as it was.

remarks.para: The planes of an opening cut only the cells its box reaches, and a cell beside one that was cut kept a face the other's faces did not match: a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two blind openings up from its floor whose ceilings stood 0.00095 apart, at the origin or a hundred thousand out, cut in at once at a millionth or below, came out open. The plate less a box across both openings held 22 717.96, 1.05 short, and was not valid, and the two joined were not worked out; TryCutOpenings closes the cut by a weld or takes the openings out one at a time, and on what it gives both come out as they hold.

Of 12 000 unions, common parts and differences of prisms with two or three openings whose walls stood 0.000 15 to 0.03 apart and boxes, turned about in space or not, at nought, 1E-12, the rounding, 1E-9 and 1E-6, the 6 020 within a million of the origin held 221 trusted and wrong, 806 not worked out and 751 not valid; 38, 55 and 21 do now, and none that was right came out otherwise. Worked out again on the material wherever it was not made or not valid, the 5 980 further out, where rounding moves a corner off a plane by more than a millionth and the material cannot tell such walls apart, turned 106 not worked out or not valid into trusted and wrong; there, only what came out made, valid and holding another volume is taken worked out again, and 125 of 780 trusted and wrong are right. Looked for at 1E-3 and 1E-2 too, it moved none of 7 200 such booleans but for one more warning logged, and made the four booleans of a plate with twelve holes and a box a fifth to a half slower; above a millionth the operation is left as it was (see ). At a millionth and below they take that much longer still, and the booleans above, many of them worked out again, half as long again at 1E-9 and 1E-6 and more than twice as long at nought.

member.summary: Determines whether two walls of a body and its openings, of two openings or of an opening and the body, standing apart, lie within the tolerance of one plane and further apart than the rounding of the coordinates, and gives the tolerance they are cut within then: one between the gap of those walls and the most that walls that meet, or a face off flat, stand off one plane within the tolerance.

An L 100 by 80 by 50, a million out, with two blind openings 27 apart whose walls stood 0.0009 apart across the L, cut within a thousandth, held 153 674.08 where it holds 153 673.56, its section 0.014 off, and with the openings the other way round 153 673.30. Walls that meet within the tolerance are made one plane by the cut, as they are meant to be, and a face off flat is laid flat, so the finer tolerance stays wider than either; where it cannot, the walls are cut as before.

member.remarks: Where the point tolerance is below the rounding of the coordinates the openings are cut within it, as cuts them: cut at nought, a plate 200 by 100 by 3 turned about in space, with a hole 20 by 20 through it, was meshed by into triangles holding 29 999.99 where it holds 58 800, and a point in the middle of the hole was projected 1.5 from it, onto a face across the hole, where its wall stands 10 off.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TryCutOpeningsAtOnce(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Cuts every opening of a body into it at once, as a boolean reads its operands, whether what comes of it closes or not; a cut that cannot be worked out is logged.
member.param: The body with its openings cut in, or the body itself when it has none; null when the method returns false.
member.returns: true when some material is left; otherwise, or when the cut cannot be worked out, false.
member.remarks: A boolean closes what it gives itself, and cuts both bodies by every plane of both where cutting one does not, so it takes the cut as it comes: handed a plate whose twelve openings the tolerance inside its faces were taken out one at a time, the union of the plate and a box at its corner went that way and came out wound two ways, 718 137.69 where it holds 722 622.74. A cut that left a piece of the body part in an opening and part out of it (see ) is taken as it comes too, as it was before that was looked for, and noted in the debug log: the boolean of such an operand can be off by the piece.

The body less the opening; null when the method returns false.
What was thrown where the cut could not be worked out; null otherwise.
Whether the difference reads a corner as on a plane within the planar tolerance and the rounding of the body's coordinates, as the cut of openings does (see ); see .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CutOpenings(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3},GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Boolean@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Cuts some of a body's openings into it at once: parts the body by the planes of the openings, keeps the pieces that are material and glues them.
member.param: The body with the openings cut in; null when the method returns false.
Whether a piece was left part in an opening and part out of it by a plane that would not cut it, and judged whole; see . The material is given all the same, as it was cut.
Whether a cut that comes out open, or with a piece judged whole, is cut again; see the remarks.
member.returns: true when some material is left; false when the openings take all of it.

remarks.para: The planes of an opening cut only the cells its box reaches, and a cell beside one so cut keeps a face the other's faces do not match. Their gluing takes from each such face what the other shares, and where two walls stand a hair apart, a strip of a face that thin was lost: a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two blind openings up from its floor whose ceilings stood 0.00095 apart, cut within a ten-thousandth to a thousand-millionth, came out open, 1.05 cubic millimetres short. Where a boolean cuts its operands () below a thousandth, a cut that comes out open, or with a piece judged whole, is cut again with every plane of the openings carried through every cell it crosses, as the cut once was, so that the faces of cells side by side match, and that is taken where it closes with no piece judged whole; see .

Of 51 prisms with two or three openings whose walls stood 0.000 15 to 0.03 apart, within a million of the origin, turned about in space or not, 14 came out of the cut open within a millionth, and none does now; 16 within a hundred-thousandth and within a ten-thousandth, and 2 do now; 25 at nought, and 2 do now. More than a million out, where rounding moves a corner off a plane by more than a millionth, the cut is not cut again: of 8 820 booleans of such prisms so cut again and boxes, between nought and a millionth, 1 700 more came out right, but 27 that were right came out wrong, by as much as two tenths. At a thousandth and above it is not cut again either; see .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.FirstCut(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3},GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Cuts all the openings of a body, or some of them, into it at once by the cells each opening's box reaches, or, where all were cut so within the same tolerance before, gives that cut as it came.
member.param: The openings to cut; a cut of all of them, the body's own list, is kept with the body.
member.remarks: A boolean at a millionth and below cuts the openings of each operand at once, and then asks whether that cut came out open (see ), which cut them again, the same way, within the same tolerance: the second cut is the first, to the bit, and is read from the body. Of the four booleans of 60 prisms with openings and boxes, at a millionth 308 of 549 such cuts were read so; at 1E-9, 303 of 621; at nought, 283 of 755. The booleans gave what they gave, to the bit, in a quarter less time at a millionth and a sixth less at 1E-9.

member.summary: How many times as many cells as the first cut the cut again, every plane carried through every cell, may come to before it is given up and the first cut kept: carried through every cell, each plane of each opening runs on across the body, and the cells of a plate with many round holes, each a dozen facets or more, grow as the square of the planes.
member.remarks: Of 300 prisms with two or three openings, the cells carried through came to at most 3.8 times those of the first cut, and 1.6 times on the whole.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.CutAgainBelow
member.remarks: At a thousandth and above, walls a hair apart lie within the tolerance of one plane, and the cut that came out open was read by the boolean as it came: a plate 300 by 200 by 12 a hundred thousand out, its twelve openings standing the tolerance inside its faces, joined within a hundredth to a box at its corner, holds 722 622.74, and with its openings cut again 722 728.78. Of 7 200 booleans of prisms with openings and boxes at 1E-3 and 1E-2, cut again, three of one prism moved, nearer.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.MostPlanesForEighths
member.summary: The most planes of one opening running through a piece uncut whose eighths are read, the first to come: the threes of them grow as the cube of their number, and an opening crossing a piece with many more planes than a box has is a round cut into facets, a cone, a countersink or a ball, not the corner of a box the eighths are read for: the 128 facets of a cone make 341 376 threes, every one meeting at its tip.
Whether a piece of the body, a plane of an opening running through it uncut, lies part in that opening and part out of it, which judged whole by one point puts the one part on the side of the other.
member.param: The pieces of the body, each in one piece.
The planes that ran through a cell and would not cut it, each with the opening it is of.
Whether the middle of a part of a piece is read, given the piece and the middle; every one is where null. The middle of a part of a piece that is not convex can lie outside it; see .
member.remarks: A plane can run through a cell and the cut still be refused, where the rim it leaves does not close: a half of a body, cut near a face, is often closed only within the tolerance, and one crossed by the floor of a box opening left a rim open by a gap 0.007 wide. Left whole, such a piece is judged by one point and kept or dropped with the opening: a hull cut within a hundredth by a plane 0.019 inside a face, a box 3.5 by 3.5 by 5 standing through the cut, left a half holding 1 465.33 cubic millimetres where it holds 1 434.77, the box left in, with every opening said to be cut out. A piece is read so where the middle of its part on one side of the plane is in the opening and of the other out of it, and, where two planes of one opening run through it uncut, the middle of one of the four parts they make is in it and of another out: a cube 10 across under the corner of a box 4 by 4 lying along an edge of it, both planes uncut, holds 40 of the box, and each plane alone leaves both its parts out of the box. Where three that meet at a point run through it uncut, the eight parts they make are read so too: a cube 10 across with the corner of a box 7 across standing in it, x, y and z = 5 uncut, holds 125 of the box, and each plane alone or any two leave the middles of all their parts out of it; the threes are read of the first planes of an opening only (see ). A piece the plane runs through clear of the opening, or only grazes or takes a sliver off (see ), is judged as before.

A box dipping 0.088 into an arm of a U, its sides x = 9.74 and 19.14 and its floor z = 7.1, holds 2.55 of it between its sides and over its floor, a part no two of the planes part from the rest.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Grid(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPlane3})
member.summary: The parts planes make of a body where they fall into no more than three families of parallel planes, whose ways meet at a point where there are three, each part with its volume and its middle; null for more families, three meeting along a line, or more parts than .
member.remarks: Each part lies between two planes of each family, or beyond the last, and is read, as reads two parallel planes, from the parts beyond one plane of each of some of the families: a slab is what lies beyond its nearer plane less what lies beyond its further one, and each part beyond is read as cones from the point where its planes meet nearest the middle of the body's box, so that none of the sections closing it adds to it. Planes within the rounding of the coordinates of each other along their way are read as one. A comb 50 by 10 by 10 with two notches 10 wide, its bottom cracked under the sides of two boxes dipping 0.088 into the tooth beside each notch, is one cell crossed by the four sides and the floor the boxes share, ten parts.

member.summary: Takes the material of a body with its openings cut in at once where it closes as reads it, or where the body or an opening does not; otherwise welds it within the tolerance, and where that does not close it takes the openings out of the body one at a time by a difference, as a boolean closes what it gives.

Why no material could be had; null otherwise.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.TakeOutOneAtATime(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3},System.String,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Boolean,System.Exception@)
member.summary: Takes the openings out of a body one at a time by a difference, or within the rounding of the coordinates cuts them in at once one at a time, the way back where cutting them in at once together gave no material to trust.
member.param: What the cut at once gave, to begin the reason a failure gives.
What cutting them in at once gave, null where it left nothing; the body less the openings, or null where none is.
Whether the tolerance is the rounding of the coordinates, a caller's below it raised to it, where a difference cannot be trusted (see ).
Why no material could be had; null where none was wanted.
member.returns: false where the openings take all of the body, or one could not be taken out closed, or what they leave is not valid as reads it.
member.remarks: Each difference comes out closed, and reads a corner as on a plane within the planar tolerance and the rounding of the coordinates besides, a trillionth of their size, as the cut of openings does (see ), all through: its cells, its faces and what it closes. Within the tolerance alone, a plate 300 by 200 by 12, turned and far from the origin, less a hole 22 across whose floor lay 0.001 under its top to 2E-15, within a thousandth, had its sides cut along a line falling from the top to the floor across the plate, each face within the tolerance of where it belongs. With twelve such holes, one of them 1.8E-7 deeper, the twelve differences came out wound two ways at the top, which Validate reads as not valid, holding 666 653.98; they hold 666 657.36, eleven holes through and one under a skin 0.0010002 thick. With twelve 0.01 under to within a millionth, cut within a hundredth, a plate came out valid and 130.70 cubic millimetres short of the plate less every hole through; it holds 666 668.11, within what its skins can leave. Read so where it parts the cells only, the difference reads the rest otherwise: of 600 such plates cut so, 4 that are right came out wrong and 10 were refused. With the point tolerance widened by the rounding too, a cube 10 across, cracked, less a box, cut within a hundredth, came back 0.32 cubic millimetres short where it is exact. A difference read so that will not come out is worked out within the tolerance alone, as it was: a plate with twelve boxes hidden 0.001 inside its faces, near the origin, had one that came out open whichever way it was cut, and was refused; taken out so, it holds what its skins can leave. What the differences leave is still refused where it is not valid.

Cut in at once, one at a time, the holes take 1 766.21 and 4 592.47 out of it, as they do.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.LeaveOutOpeningsApart(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.Boolean,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3@)
member.summary: Leaves out of the bodies of a boolean whose material the result does not keep each opening that shares no space with the other body, its box further from the other's box than the tolerance or the opening itself clear of the other's faces (see ): both bodies of a common part, or the body a difference takes away. Leaving such an opening out is exact: what two bodies share is what they share without it, and a body less one with an opening apart from it is the body less the other whole.
member.param: The first body; for a difference, the one material is taken from, which is left as it is.
The second body; for a difference, the one taken away.
true for a common part, whose bodies both lose such openings; false for a difference, whose second body alone does.
The first body less the openings left out; the body itself where none is.
The second body less the openings left out; the body itself where none is.
member.returns: true where an opening is left out; false where none is, or the bodies' boxes do not meet.

remarks.para: The tolerance is the widest the boolean reads: the point and planar tolerances, raised to the rounding below it as raises them, and what rounding moves a corner off a plane by for each body. An opening whose box comes exactly that far from the other's box, or nearer, is left out only where it is clear of the other's faces by twice that.

An opening of an opening kept is left out too where it shares no space with the other body either: what the boolean reads of such a body is only what lies within the other. The openings of a body whose material is kept, either of a union or the one a difference takes material from, are cut in as they were, so that the faces of what the boolean gives are still where its material ends.
Two bodies whose boxes do not meet are left as they are, and so are two with no opening apart, which are worked out as they were, to the bit.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.WithoutOpeningsApart(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSolid3,GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Clearance)
member.summary: A body less each opening that shares no space with the other body, as a clearance reads it, and less each such opening of an opening kept, at every depth; the body itself where none is. The openings kept keep their order.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Boolean3.Clearance
member.summary: The other body of a boolean, as an opening of one is asked whether it shares any space with it: an opening whose box stays further from the other's box than the reach does not, nor does one whose faces close, as the other's do, with no triangle of either within the clearance of a triangle of the other and no corner of either inside the other or within the clearance of its faces. member.remarks: A box is not enough on a curved body. A spiral ramp 7 600 wide and 300 thick in 56 facets over half a turn, with a spiral tube 110 by 100 inside it as an opening, from 100 to 200 over its floor, less a spiral girder 600 by 500 in 66 lying 100 into its outer edge, its top 20 over the floor: the tube's box and the girder's both reach round the half turn, and the tube, 80 under the girder's top all along it, was cut into the ramp. The girder less the ramp was cut into 640 222 cells in 202 seconds on .NET 10 and was not worked out; with the tube left out it is cut into 18 345 in 1.6 seconds and holds what slicing gives, 10 044 789 407.964. Clear surfaces and no corner inside settle it: two closed bodies sharing space have surfaces that cross, or one lies wholly inside the other, every corner of it with it.

does; and closes a cut that one would skip, by , where that closes it and the body closed holds what the cut can leave.

Thrown when one of the tools is null.

remarks.para: Every cut the other overload takes is taken here the same, bit for bit. Only a cut it would skip, whose result is valid neither within the options' tolerance nor within the fallback, is closed: the result worked out within the tolerance first, the tool put onto the body as the contact says; where that does not close, the result worked out within the fallback, where there is a fallback and it gave a body. A cut that could not be worked out at all, giving no body, is skipped as before, and so is one neither result of which closes.

No cut is closed where the body before it, or the tool as put onto it, carries openings: such a cut is skipped as without closing. Cut out of a body not closed, an opening takes material before any closing can: a box cracked open, with an opening, holds 5 400 of material where the whole box with it holds 5 640, and its cut by a post closed to 5 160 where 5 400 is right.

A body closed is taken only where it is valid within the options' tolerance as well as within the closing's, both checks passing whichever tolerance is the finer; and where it holds what a difference can leave: no more than the body before the cut, and no less than that less the whole of the tool, each within the options' point tolerance times the area of the two, and a hair more for the rounding. A closed body holding more or less is refused, and the next tried or the cut skipped; says which cuts were skipped so. The volumes are read by the faces, as the check of a boolean reads them, so a body before the cut that is not valid, as one with a face given twice, can refuse a closing that is right: the bound errs on the side of skipping.

A subject not valid as given leaves its first cut that would be skipped not valid either, whether or not the tool reaches it, and that cut is closed: a tool clear of the body takes nothing, and the closing closes the subject itself there.

Of the 35 cuts that 17 parts of a Tekla model left skipped, cut within a thousandth with a contact and a fallback of a hundredth, closing the result within the thousandth with a gap of 0.005, holes up to 100 and 0.01 out of flat closed 23, each within 2.1E-6 of what the cut within the hundredth holds.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.BoxFit.HullCorners
member.summary: The corners of a hull once each, and the edges between its faces: what a box standing on a face is fitted round, and what tells, before it is fitted, that it cannot be as small as one found.

remarks.para: Each corner of a hull is a corner of several faces, and the box on a face was fitted round all their copies: 3 000 points on a sphere make a hull of 6 000 triangles, and each face sorted 18 000 points for the rectangle round them. Copies to the bit change nothing in the hull of the plane, the rectangles on it or the depth, so each corner is taken once, where no coordinate it is read at is nought or beyond what a product holds: those are the only numbers two copies of which compare as one and differ in their bits, which a sort could then order otherwise, and the face is fitted round every copy as it was.

A face is passed over where every box on it is larger than the least so far beyond rounding, which it would lose to. The rectangle on a face holds the hull of the plane, which holds every point within the tolerance; so grown by the tolerance on every side it holds the hull of any of the points, and is no smaller than the least rectangle round them. The corners on the rim the hull shows along the normal, those on an edge between a face turned towards it and one turned away, are the ones on that hull, and calipers round them, each reach read no further than it goes, give no more than that least rectangle; less what growing by the tolerance adds, and times the depth, no box on the face is smaller. Of the 6 000 faces of the sphere 8 are fitted: 0.40 seconds where it took 7.7, and the same box to the bit. The bound is used only where the tolerance is more than a hundred-millionth of the size of the points, so that the rim's hull turns the wrong way nowhere by more than rounding allows for.

The bound read every corner, for how far the hull reaches along the normal, and every face and edge, for the rim, on every face: 12 000 points on a sphere make 24 000 faces, and the box took 7.7 seconds. On a hull of more than 1 536 edges the corners, and the edges between two faces by the box round their two normals, are laid out in trees of boxes: the corners reaching furthest either way are found in the few boxes that can hold them, and the edges of the rim in the boxes the plane square to the normal passes through, taken in the order of the edges as before. The bound is the same to the bit, and so is the box: 1.9 seconds.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.ClosestEdge2
member.summary: Picking the one piece of a shape that lies nearest something else.

remarks.para: This answers a different question from , which builds the segment joining two shapes. Nothing is built here: one of the shape's own edges is handed back, whole, the one lying nearest the probe.

The probe is always a single primitive — a point, a segment, a circle or an arc. A shape that is itself made of edges is not offered, because the nearest edge of one such shape to another is really a pair of edges, and that is a different answer from the one this name promises.

Each edge is measured on its own, so a probe lying inside a closed shape still names the edge nearest it rather than reporting nothing, which is where this parts company with . Where two edges are equally near — and a probe crossing the outline touches several at nothing at all — the earlier one in the shape's own order wins, so the answer does not drift from one run to the next.

Every shape measures each of its edges as its own distance does: a straight side no longer than the point tolerance is the side it is, not the point at its start, and a segment you give no longer than the tolerance is read as its start where it crosses no side. At a hundredth, the loop (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 0.006), (0, 10) names its side 0.006 long for the point (10.03, 0.003), 0.03 from it, where read as its start it stood 0.0301496 off, as far as the side along the bottom, which came first. A polygon, a polyline and a rectangle take no tolerance here: they measure every side exactly, and read a segment you give as its start by the global tolerance. The rectangle 10 by 0.0006 on the origin names its right-hand side, 0.0006 long, for the point (10.03, 0.0003).

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Core.ClosestEdge2.Exactly
member.summary: A tolerance of nought, for measuring a straight side as it is however short: a side longer than any tolerance projects a point to the same place at nought as at the tolerance.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3
member.summary: Closes an open solid with the least change that does it, and says what it changed, or why it could not and where.

remarks.para: The steps are those lists, each tried only where the ones before it did not close the body. The reason given for a body not closed is that of the first step that could not go on, where none after it closed the body either.

A body valid within the tolerance already is handed back as it is, the same instance, and nothing is measured: the same body back says nothing was done. Made so far are the cleaning, the turning, the reading of the loops, the welding and the filling of holes, flat and out of flat. The faces are cleaned: those covering nothing within the tolerance dropped, a face given twice taken once, and of a face and a copy of it lying back to back, the one wound against the faces round it dropped. They are turned so that each shell is wound alike, the stretches longer than the widest gap read first and the shorter ones only where they are whole edges of both their faces, and each closed shell inside no other outwards, with every shell inside it, a shell inside another keeping its winding against it, a block within it or a cavity; an open shell, and a shell inside one, keep their winding until closed. A face no other runs an edge of, lying back to back on a face of the body, is a sheet of no thickness, and is dropped. An edge left open past a fin, a face standing off the surface, stops the closing there, where the fin is longer than the widest gap; a shorter one is a piece of a gap. Edges left open running back alongside each other are the two sides of a gap, and an edge left open no longer than the widest gap is one by itself; the whole body is welded shut before any loop of it is read as a hole: corners across the gaps made one, the nearest first, two corners of one face only where they are copies of one corner beside each other across an edge left open, each group going to the corner that bends the faces round it least by their areas, within the least reach that closes the body, up to the widest gap allowed; and only where no reach of that closes it, corners standing off open edges put on them as well, moved onto them within their own face's plane where the crack lies there. A face welded stays one face where its corners lie flat about their middle. Where a reach leaves nothing open, the faces are oriented again, every shell now closed. A fin left after the welding, or one a reach would have left, stops the closing. No body is taken with a ring running out to a corner and straight back, with a face it was not given lying back to back with another, or with a face welded through another, an edge of either passing through the inside of the other: each reads valid, and none is a body. A gap a reach would close only through what stands in it, a blade in a crack, is blocked rather than too wide, and where no reach closes the body and no fill does, the body is still open where the face would pass through.

What is left open is followed round into loops, a corner two holes meet at stopping the closing there. Where no fill is allowed, a hole stops it, and a gap the welds could not close is a gap too wide. Where fills are allowed, every loop is filled, gaps too wide for the welds as well as holes, the gap's reason kept should nothing close the body: a loop flat within the planar tolerance by one face on its own corners, the loops in its plane inside it its holes; the two ends of a hole through a shell whose walls are missing, straight, slanting or tapering, capped or walled as the strategy says; and a loop out of flat by no more than allowed, with nothing inside it, by the triangles of least area across it on its own corners, of the ways lying on no face of the body and turned back against the loop nowhere, where those ways close one volume within the planar tolerance times its area or the strategy takes the least anyway. No fill is taken that is larger than allowed, that lies back to back with a face of the body, or that crosses one, or a face of a fill taken before it, an edge of either passing through the inside of the other, though both read valid: caps crossing the body are no way, and leave the walls the one way where those may be taken, and a face or triangles crossing it leave the hole open. Once the fills close the body, every shell is read again for which way it faces, as the turning reads a closed shell. Any other body not valid at the end is reported still open.

Nothing thrown for a reason of the geometry leaves this: a shape the work builds refused by its constructor, or a direction asked of a vector with none, is reported as a body still open, and the log says what was thrown, as the booleans report one they could not work out.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.MayFill(GeometryHelper.SolidClosingOptions)
member.summary: Determines whether options allow any hole to be filled: a largest hole above nought, and a strategy that fills.

Fills the loops left open, holes and gaps too wide for the welds alike, each hole by the faces the options allow, and takes the body where it comes out valid; false, the trouble noted, where a hole cannot be filled or what comes of it is not a body.
member.param: The faces of the body as the welding left them.
For each, the face given it comes of, by index.
The loops left open in them, in order.
The body filled; null when the method returns false.
What was done to it; null when the method returns false.
member.returns: true where every loop is filled and the body comes out valid.

remarks.para: The holes are those reads, each filled in the order of its first loop, and the first that cannot be filled stops the filling there. A face added lying back to back with a face of the body is a skin of no thickness that reads valid and holds nothing, and is not taken: a face lying on the top of a box, every edge of it open, would be filled by itself turned over. Nor is one crossing a face of the body as filled so far, a face it was given or one added across a hole before, an edge of either passing through the inside of the other, which reads valid as well (see ). Where a hole has one way of filling it lying on no face of the body and crossing none, that way is taken, whatever the strategy: the caps of a hole through a plate whose walls are missing, a post standing in the hole through the plane of a cap, are no way, and the walls round the post are the one. Where it has two, as the two ends of that hole have with nothing in it, capped or walled, takes neither and the report says , and takes the one adding the least area, the caps where the two add as much. Where no way may be taken, the hole is left open, at a point where its face or a cap lies on a face of the body, or where an edge passes through one.

A hole out of flat is filled by the triangles of least area across it, of the ways lying on no face of the body, as says. Only the triangles taken are set against crossing the body as filled so far, not the three million or so the ways across a loop of 256 corners are made of, so that where they cross it the hole is left open, , rather than filled another way: of two boxes over one square, open towards each other, their rims well out of flat, the triangles across the second rim would cross those across the first, and the second hole is left open where they do. The faces taken across each hole are held to , and a hole needing more is , at a point within the faces it would take.

The way each shell faces is read again on the body closed: a shell open by a hole encloses a volume only from where it is measured, and the volume a closed shell encloses says which way it faces for certain; see . Then the body is checked as the welding's is: valid within the tolerance, no ring running out to a corner and straight back, and no face new to it lying back to back with another.
Each hole filled is one change: its size is the area added across it, and its place the middle of the faces added, where they would balance.

member.summary: Chooses the faces a flat hole is filled by: its face, or for the two ends of a hole through the body, the caps or the walls, as the strategy says where both may be taken, lying on no face of the body and crossing none of it as filled so far, the walls closing it; false, the trouble noted where the face or the caps meet it, where neither may be.
member.param: The faces filed by their boxes.
The fills taken before, of the holes before it.
The fills taken; null when the method returns false.

member.summary: Takes the body filled where it is valid within the tolerance, with no ring doubling back and no face new to it lying back to back with another; false, the trouble noted, otherwise.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.ReadHoles(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Loop},GeometryHelper.SolidClosingOptions,GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.FaceShells)
member.summary: Reads the loops left open as holes to fill, in the order of their first loops: a loop flat within the planar tolerance is filled by one face on its corners, the loops lying in its plane inside it the other way round taken as the holes of that face; two such faces of no holes at the two ends of a hole through a shell can be walls between them instead; and a loop out of flat by no more than the options allow, with no loop inside it, is filled by triangles.
member.param: The loops left open, in order.
The shells of the faces the loops are left open in.
member.returns: The holes, each with the reason it cannot be filled where its loops cannot be read as one.

remarks.para: A loop is flat where none of its corners stands further than the planar tolerance off the plane through the average of its corners square to its area. Each face is built on the loops' corners as the body has them, bit for bit, facing the way a face closing the edges would: a box missing its top is filled by a face on the very corners of the faces round the hole, though the ends of the stretches the check reads along them can stand a rounding off them.

A flat loop lies inside another where it lies in the other's plane, within the planar tolerance, and a corner of it, the first not on the other's edges, lies inside the other, seen square to it: the middle of a loop round a corner need not lie inside it. Of the loops it lies inside, the smallest holds it. A loop held by the boundary of a face and running the other way round is a hole of that face; one held by a hole of a face is a face of its own again, an island, as is one running the same way round as the loop holding it.

Two faces of no holes on loops of one shell are the two ends of a hole through it whose walls are missing where flat walls run between them, each from an edge of the one to an edge of the other (see ): the faces cap it, and the walls close it round the hole instead, straight through it, slanting or tapering. A box missing its top and bottom has two such loops, and the walls there lie on its sides; a plate missing the walls of a hole through it has two, and the walls lie on nothing; a channel pierced through its top and its bottom has two, and the walls cross its plates on their way, which is no way of closing it either (see ).

A loop further out of flat than the planar tolerance and no further than is filled by triangles on its corners (see ), and one further out is . Triangles are found across a loop of no more than 256 corners, and one out of flat with more is , at its corner furthest off flat. They are found across a loop with nothing inside it only: a loop out of flat holding another, or a flat one holding a loop out of flat, which its face cannot take as a hole, is whatever the strategy, at the middle of the loop holding it. Where either loop is out of flat, one lies in the other's plane within the planar tolerance and as far again as a hole may stand out of flat. A loop out of flat held by a hole of a flat face is an island, and filled by triangles of its own. A loop enclosing no area, or one whose face cannot be built, leaves the body still open.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.WallsBetween(GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Loop,GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Loop,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: The walls between two loops that are the two ends of a hole through a body: each wall on four of their corners, from an edge of the one to the edge of the other matched with it; null where they are no such ends.

remarks.para: The two are such ends where they turn at as many corners, three or more, a corner a rim runs straight on through, within the point tolerance of the line between its neighbours, not counted; where the faces across them face opposite ways, and away from each other, the middle of each further than the point tolerance behind the other's face; and where corner c of the one, matched with corner s less c of the other for some s, makes every wall flat within the planar tolerance and convex. Of several such s, the one whose walls add the least area is taken.

So the walls of a hole slanting through a plate are parallelograms, and those of one tapering through it trapezoids, whichever corner each rim is listed from. Two holes in the faces of a channel's arms facing each other across its gap face each other, not away, and are no ends of one hole: walls between them would lay a bar across the gap.

remarks.para: Validation reads no face crossing another. A box 30 by 20 by 10 missing its top, a post 4 by 4 standing in it 5 through the plane of the top, is closed by the top with every edge paired, valid and holding 6 208, the four walls of the post through it; walls through the gap of a channel, from a hole in its top to one in its bottom, close it as well, crossing the plates on their way. Neither is a way of closing the hole. A face of the body is set against a face added only where it stands across the face added's plane (see ).

Two flat fills cannot cross unseen: every edge of a flat face or of a cap is an edge of a face given as well, and is set against the other fill with it. The diagonals of triangles and the edges of the walls between the two ends of a hole are edges of no face given, and two fills can cross by them, each crossing nothing given: two boxes over one square 6 by 6, open towards each other, their rims about 1.8 out of flat, are filled the lower by triangles rising to 16 across the middle and the upper by triangles dipping to 14.5 there, and the two closed would read valid, 861. So each fill is set against the fills taken before it as well, in the order the holes are filled, each face by its box: a body has few holes.

member.remarks: A face touched at an edge or a corner is not crossed: an edge lying in its plane, or one ending in it, has no end further off it than the planar tolerance. Nor is one an edge runs from, out of a corner of it or a point on its edges: a straight edge meets the plane of a flat face once, where it touches. The plane is read through the face's first corner, from which a corner of a face a hair out of flat can stand twice the planar tolerance off: a hopper missing its top, a corner of its rim lifted 0.0036 and the rim flat within the tolerance, has the edges of its walls sloping in under the hole from such a corner meet the plane of the top 0.002 in from both its sides, where they only touch it.

remarks.para: A shell open by a hole was turned by the volume it enclosed measured from the middle of its box, which for a shell missing much of itself says little; closed, it says which way the shell faces for certain. remarks.para: A stretch one face runs is open, and the face that would close it runs it the other way. A stretch an odd number of faces more than one run is open past a fin, a face standing off the surface: which of them a face across it would close with cannot be told, and a face across the loop round the fin would be the fin again turned over, two faces back to back that read as closed. So would a stretch run by an even number of faces not as many each way, after the turning. Either is , at the middle of the stretch, found before anything is welded or filled.

A stretch so run that is no longer than the widest gap is a piece of a gap, and is left to the welding: on a prism of a thousand sides each face on copies of its corners a thousandth or two apart, the edges beside a corner run on so nearly straight that copies of three of them come within the tolerance of one line for a thousandth or two. Such a stretch left after the welding is a fin, and stops the closing there.

remarks.para: The edges are matched as matches them for , by overlap along a line within the point tolerance, so that a stretch read open here is one the check reads open: edges no longer than the tolerance are left out, two edges are on one line where each end of the shorter stands within the tolerance of the longer's line and they share more than the tolerance of it, and a line is cut into stretches at every end of an edge along it, those closer together than the tolerance taken as one.

Unlike the check, every stretch is given, those closed alike as well, and each with the face of every edge on it and which way that edge runs it. The ends of a stretch are corners of the faces, not points on the line through them, so that the stretches of two lines meeting at a corner meet at that corner. Wherever two things weigh alike, the first by index is taken: the order the faces come in decides, never the order a sort happens to leave.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.DropCopies(GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Work)
member.summary: Takes each face given more than once, on the same corners either way round, once or not at all, as the faces round it want it.

remarks.para: A face given twice the same way round puts three edges on each of its edges, two running it one way, and the body reads open; the copy goes, the face first given staying. A face and a copy of it turned over lie back to back, and read the same; the one wound alike with the faces round it, which run each of its edges the other way, stays, and the one wound against them goes, whichever comes first. Two faces back to back with no face round them are a sheet holding nothing, and both go. Two faces back to back between two blocks, the wall they share, each close one of them, and both stay; see .
The faces are filed by the low corner of their box, and each compared only with the later faces filed near it, by its corners within the tolerance: two copies have the same box.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Settle(GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Work,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Boolean},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32}[])
member.summary: Settles which of a group of faces on the same corners stay, by how the faces round them run their edges; see .
member.param: The faces, by index, lowest first.
For each, whether it runs the way the first does.
The stretches each face has an edge on.

remarks.para: What the faces round the group need of it is read stretch by stretch along the edges of its first face. Where an odd number of them run each stretch, one face of the group closes it, and one stays: the one wound alike with most of them, which run its edges the other way, the first face where as many are each way. A face round it wound the wrong way is turned after, and which of the copies stayed makes no difference to the body then, only to which change is reported. Where an even number run each, as round the wall two blocks share, one of each way round stays, and where none do, the group is a sheet holding nothing and goes whole, or, all one way round, a face on its own given more than once, and one stays. Where the stretches disagree, one of each way round stays, and the open edges say the rest.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.TryTurnAlike(GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Work)
member.summary: Turns faces over so that each shell is wound alike, and each faces outwards, or inwards where it lies inside an odd number of other shells, as a cavity does; false where a shell cannot be wound alike.
member.param: The work, its stretches found and its copies dropped.
member.returns: false, the trouble noted, where the faces of a shell cannot be wound alike whichever are turned.

remarks.para: The faces are taken shell by shell, a shell being the faces joined by stretches two of them meet on. Two faces wound alike run such a stretch one each way, and where they run it the same way, one of them is to be turned over. Of the two sides that leaves in a shell, the one of less area is turned: the least change that winds the shell alike, the side of its first face staying where the two are as large. Where the stretches ask a face to be turned both ways, the shell cannot be wound alike: a surface with one side only. The stretches longer than the widest gap are read first, and they alone refuse: on a prism of a thousand sides each face on copies of its corners a thousandth or two apart, the bottom edges of two sides beside a corner run on so nearly straight that their copies come within the tolerance of one line for a thousandth or two, both running it the same way, and read so, they would turn a side over. A shorter stretch then joins two faces not joined yet only where it is the whole of an edge of each (see ), and never refuses: a quad 0.004 a side wound against a patch of such quads in a top, closed within a gap of 0.005, has no stretch longer than the gap and is turned back all the same.

Then the volume a closed shell encloses says which way it faces, each shell on its own: the faces of two shells, one wound each way, enclose nothing together, and the whole body would say nothing of either. Only a shell inside no other is turned so, where it encloses its volume inwards, and with it every shell inside it; a shell inside another keeps its winding against it, a block within it wound the same way and a cavity wound the other, since both read valid (see ). Which shell is inside a closed one is read from where a point on it lies, by how much of the sphere round it the closed one's faces cover; a shell still open is taken to hold every shell within its box until it closes. A shell enclosing no more than the tolerance times its area, such as a face on its own, says nothing of which way it faces, and is left as it is; and so is a shell that is open, any of its stretches run an odd number of times, which keeps its winding as given until the welding or the filling closes it (see and ), as is a shell within the box of one that is open.
Every face turned over is one change, of its area, reported once the stray faces are dropped; see . The way a shell open by a hole faces is read again once the hole is filled; see .

member.summary: Orients the faces of a body welded shut again, now that every shell of it closes, and turns them over in place where they are to be; the faces given whose faces were turned are given back, to be reported so.
member.param: The faces of the body welded; turned over in place where they are to be.
For each, the face given it comes of, by index.
The stretches read again where faces changed, by the places of their faces among those read.
For each face read again, its place among the faces welded.
member.returns: The faces given whose faces were turned over, by index, in order.

remarks.para: The faces are joined as the turning joined the faces they come of, which it wound alike, and along the stretches read again where faces changed, as it joins them: the long ones first, and then the short ones that are whole edges of both their faces, only between faces not joined yet. A shell the welding joined of shells the turning could not, patches of a sphere each face of which stood on copies of its own corners, is so wound alike the way the faces of it given were, its side of less area turned to the other. Then each shell, closed, is read as the turning reads a closed shell: one inside no other enclosing its volume inwards is turned over whole, with every shell inside it, and a shell inside another keeps its winding against it (see ). A box whose faces stood on copies of their corners, every face wound inwards, open all round as given, is turned out once welded shut.

Only the stretches where faces changed are read: elsewhere the faces are as the turning joined them. A body of six thousand faces, one copy of a corner of it welded, is so oriented in no more than it takes to add its volume.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.TurnedOutwards(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoFace3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32}},System.Boolean[],System.Boolean[],GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: For each shell, wound alike once its faces are turned where they are to be, whether it is to be turned over whole: an outermost closed shell, inside no other, that encloses its volume inwards, and with it every shell inside it.
member.param: The faces of each shell, by index.
For each face, whether it is turned over to wind its shell alike; null where none is.
For each shell, whether it is closed.

remarks.para: A shell inside another keeps the way it is wound against it: the same way, it is a block within it, the other way a cavity, and neither is turned, since the check reads only the sign of the whole body's volume and both read valid. A part of a Tekla model came with three boxes inside its main shell, all wound outwards; with one face of the main shell wound the wrong way, the boxes read as nested were turned into cavities, and the part lost 3.9 % of its volume, where the one face is all that is turned now. A box with a box inside, both wound outwards, 6 600, one face of the outer turned, gets that face turned back and holds 6 600.

An outermost shell wound inwards is turned with every shell inside it, so that each keeps its winding against the one round it: a box inside out with a cavity comes back a box with a cavity. A shell within the box of a shell still open may lie inside it, however little of the sphere round it that shell's faces cover, and is no outermost one until that shell closes: a cavity in a box missing its top and bottom stays a cavity, though the four sides cover about a third of the sphere round it. A shell enclosing no more than the tolerance times its area says nothing of which way it faces.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.TurnedBack
member.summary: The cosine of the least angle a triangle across a loop must be turned against the loop's normal by, to be turned back on it: 120 degrees.
member.remarks: Across a concave rim nearly flat, a way of filling it that runs a diagonal outside the rim folds a triangle back over the outside, facing nearly against the loop; such a way is no way of filling the hole, and counted, it parts the volumes the ways close by far more than the ways across the inside do. Across a loop well out of flat, as the one round two faces of a box left out side by side, the faces again stand square to the loop's normal, and are kept.

member.summary: Fills a loop out of flat by the triangles of least area across it on its own corners, of the ways of filling it none of whose triangles lies back to back with a face of the body; false, and why, where no way lies on no face, or where the strategy takes only an unambiguous fill and the ways part in the volume they close.
member.param: The loop, by index, which the fill closes.
The faces filed by their boxes.
The triangles taken, one change; null when the method returns false.
Why the loop is not filled; none when the method returns true.
A point at that trouble; the origin when the method returns true.

remarks.para: The ways of filling a loop of n corners with triangles on them are the triangulations of a polygon of n corners, and the least area across it, with the least and the most volume the ways close, are found by the dynamic program over the runs of its corners: each run from one corner to a later one is closed by a triangle on its two ends and a corner between, and the runs either side of that corner, the least of every choice kept. Each triangle is weighed once, so that a loop of 256 corners is some three million triangles. A triangle standing no higher than the point tolerance over its longest side is a needle, and no way takes it.

A triangle lying back to back with a face of the body is a skin of no thickness, and no way taking it is one: the least area across the loop round two faces of a long box, its top and front, is the plane through the box's diagonal, but each end of it is a triangle lying on the end face of the box it stands in. Such a triangle has its three corners on that face, so each corner is read once for the faces it lies on, and a triangle is looked at closer only where its three corners share one. Nor is a way taking a triangle turned back against the loop's normal, folding over the outside of a concave rim (see ): an L-shaped top of 300 lifted 0.005 at a convex corner is filled within a bound of 0.3 by its ways across the inside, which part by 0.25, where counted with the ways folding over the outside of its inner corner it read as ambiguous.

The ways are taken as one where the most volume any of them closes and the least are no further apart than the loop's area times the planar tolerance, the uncertainty a face the library calls flat carries already: a top of four corners, one of them lifted by six times the tolerance, is filled either way across within it. Further apart, takes none, at a point within the least area, and takes the least area anyway. The volumes are measured from the middle of the loop's corners: the ways share the loop, so they part by the same, measured from anywhere.

Welds shut the gaps a body is open by: the corners across each made one, within the point tolerance, then twice it, four times and so on while below the widest gap, and the widest gap last, the first reach that makes the body valid taken; and where no reach of welds alone does, the same again with the corners standing off edges left open put on them as well.
member.param: The faces of the body as the steps before left it; on return, as this step leaves them.
For each of the faces, the face given it comes of, by index; on return, for each this step leaves.
The edges left open in them; on return, those this step leaves.
The body welded valid; null when the method returns false.
What was done to it; null when the method returns false.
member.returns: true where a reach makes the body valid.

remarks.para: The whole body is welded before any loop of it is read as a hole: the faces of a box each on copies of its corners a few thousandths apart leave every edge open, each face's outline a loop as large as the face, and every edge of it a side of a gap. Each reach starts from the body as the steps before left it; see . The least that closes the body is taken, so that a corner moves no further than it has to: a chamfer 0.05 along each side, its ends 0.07 apart at the top and corners of edges open where a corner beside them stands 0.0015 off, would be made one within a tenth, and the corner is welded within two thousandths.

A corner put back onto the corner it was moved off is the change the faces round it want, and it is tried at every reach before any corner is put on an edge: a corner of the top of a prism half a degree sharp, moved 0.003 into it, stands within a thousandth of both sides there, and put on both it closes the prism by a seam of no width from the sides' corner to it, where welding it back closes it as it was; a strip 0.03 wide missing from a top has its corners on the edges of the faces beside it, and welding its corners across it closes it, the edges beside it split for nothing.

Where no reach makes the body valid, the least reach that leaves the fewest sides of gaps is kept for the steps after, the first that leaves none, holes still open, ending the search. A fin left on what is kept, a stretch more than two faces run that the welding was to make one, is , and so is one a reach would have left longer than the widest gap, which is why that reach was not taken: a flap 0.004 square beside a corner moved out by 0.003 is a fin whatever the gap allowed, and welding its corners away would only hide it. A gap left is wider than the widest allowed, , where it is widest, the reason given unless a fill closes the body after; but where a reach was not taken for welding a face through another, the gap is blocked rather than too wide, and the body where the face would have passed through: a crack 0.004 wide along a top, a blade 0.002 thick standing in it, closes within a gap of 0.005 only through the blade.

A body open by holes only is not welded; but an edge left open no longer than the widest gap is welded with nothing running back alongside it: copies of a corner a hair further apart than the tolerance leave one stretch a hair longer than it open, which bounds no hole and is a gap of no width.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Closing3.Reaches(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: The reaches the corners are welded within, in order: the point tolerance, twice it, four times and so on while below the widest gap, and the widest gap itself last.

Welds the corners of the edges a body's faces leave open within a reach, as does, and again with the corners of any edge the welds opened that read closed before, until they open no more or a round leaves no fewer edges open than the one before, eight times at the most; null where nothing comes of it, or what comes of it cannot be taken.
member.param: For each, the face given it comes of, by index.
The corners of the edges they leave open, as the check matches edges.
Whether corners standing off edges left open are put on them, after the welds.
member.returns: The body welded, as the last round that came to anything left it.
member.remarks: Copies of a corner a hair apart whose edges lie within the tolerance of each other's lines read closed, and stay where they are; but welded, the corners beside them can turn those edges off each other's lines. On a prism of a thousand sides, each face on copies of its corners a thousandth or two apart, the copies of a corner of the top read closed until the corner 0.06 along the top from them was welded, and open after: their corners are taken with the rest, and the reach welded again. A round that leaves as many edges open as the one before has welded nothing new, and the next would not either: a sphere of six thousand faces each on copies of its own corners, too far apart for the reach, was welded three times over at it for nothing.

member.summary: Welds the corners of the edges a body's faces leave open within a reach, and puts those standing off edges left open on them where asked; null where nothing comes of it, or what comes of it cannot be taken.
member.param: For each, the face given it comes of, by index.
The corners of the edges they leave open, as the check matches edges.
Whether corners standing off edges left open are put on them, after the welds.
member.returns: The body welded, valid or not, with what was done to it and the edges it leaves open; null where nothing moved, fewer than four faces are left, a ring doubles back, a face lies back to back with another or crosses one, the volume moved further than allowed, or a fin longer than the widest gap is left.

remarks.para: The corners that move are those of edges no ring pairs corner for corner that stand within the reach of an edge left open, as the check matches edges, within the point tolerance as beyond it: corners of a closed body a rounding apart far from any gap, as at the pole of a sphere meshed by rings, stay where they are. The corners within the reach of each other are made one, the nearest two first, and two corners of one face only where they are copies of one corner of it, beside each other on a ring across an edge left open (see ): a corner of a face is no copy of another corner of it as a rule, and made one with it, it pinches the face. A slot 0.0035 wide beside a gap, its corners across its mouth within the reach of a corner of the gap and on edges no ring pairs corner for corner, keeps its mouth so. Each group goes to the corner of it that takes the most of it within the reach and of those bends the faces round it least, each face weighed by its area (see ): a copy of a corner moved in the plane of its own face goes back onto the corner the faces beside it keep, nothing tilts, and a large cap is not tilted to spare a narrow side. Then, where asked, each corner standing within the reach of an edge left open, between its ends, is put on it; see . A face whose corners moved is built again on them, one face where they lie flat about their middle and triangles on its own corners where they do not; see .

A ring running out to a corner and straight back is no face, though it reads valid: a corner 0.02 off the corner the faces beside it keep is 0.014 off the two edges of its face beside it, and put on both within a reach of 0.016, it closes the face by a needle out to the corner moved and back. Such a reach is not taken, and the next welds the two. Nor is one that leaves a face built again lying back to back with another, a skin of no thickness that reads valid too (see ), nor one whose faces built again sweep out more volume than the reach times their area, each measured from where it was (see ): a corner moved no further than the reach sweeps no more. Nor is one that leaves a face built again crossing another, which reads valid as well: the two halves of a top 0.004 apart, a blade 0.002 thick standing between them, are welded into one through the blade. Where it is crossed is noted, as the trouble should no reach close the body (see ). A crossing is one the reach makes, through by more than the widest gap: two faces crossing as the faces they were built from did are the body's own, as a blade standing through the top away from the strip is; and faces round corners the reach does not weld yet stand through each other by as much as the copies of a corner stand apart.

What a reach leaves open is read again only where its faces changed, from them and the faces beside them; the rest is open as it was (see ). Where nothing is left open, every shell closes, and the faces are oriented again before the body is judged (see ): a shell open before, its sign not read, is turned out now where it encloses its volume inwards. The whole body is checked only then, so that a reach that closes nothing costs what its faces cost, not what the body does.

member.summary: The edges a body built again leaves open: where its faces changed, read again from the faces reaching there; and elsewhere those left open before; null where a fin longer than the widest gap is left.
member.param: The faces of the body built again.
For each, whether it was built again.
The boxes of the faces that changed, as they were and as they are.
The tolerance edges are matched within.
The middle of the fin left, where one is; the origin otherwise.

For each face read again, its place among the faces of the body.
member.remarks: A stretch of edge lies where its faces' boxes are, and an edge the faces that changed reach is an edge of a face whose box meets one of theirs: the stretches those faces run in the boxes of the faces that changed are the body's there, matched as the whole body would match them, and away from them nothing changed. The boxes are filed, each on its own, so that faces changed in many places, as copies of corners all over a sphere, are read where they changed and not across the box round them all (see ).

remarks.para: Every corner is put within the reach of an edge as it stands after the welds, and the pieces a split leaves are not split again: put on the pieces of a split, a corner could stand within the reach of a piece and not of the edge, and a gap wider than the reach would close by steps no wider.

Where a crack lies in the plane of one face, its corners standing off the edge of the face beside it within that plane, they are moved onto the edge, within their own face's plane, and the edge is split at them: both faces stay flat. Split through a corner where it stands, the edge would bend out of its face's plane along the face the corner is of, and the face built again on its corners would fold under that one as flat triangles lying against it, a skin of no thickness. A corner is moved so only where the edge lies in the plane of every face it is a corner of, and it is put on no other edge; otherwise it stays, and the edge is split through it: where it lies in the plane of the edge's face, which stays flat, and where the crack is twisted between the two, which bends.

The middle of a face is its centroid, as the boxes of the two first say may lie on it, and a middle lying on a face lies in its box, so each face new is set only against those whose boxes meet its own (see ): a sphere of six thousand faces each built again is not six thousand times read.

remarks.para: A face crossing another meets its box, so each face new is set against those whose boxes meet its own, as for a skin, the faces filed once for both; and a pair of two new faces is looked at once. Most pairs are passed over on the corners of the one of fewer alone: a face lying to one side of the other's plane, as a face of a smooth surface lies to one side of its neighbours', crosses it neither way (see ), so that a wall is set against a cap of a thousand corners by its own four; and a face touching another along an edge or at a corner crosses nothing (see ).

A pair crossing is set against the faces the two were built from, and where those crossed as well, the crossing is the body's own, not the weld's: a blade standing through the top of a box beside a strip welded shut is crossed by the half built again as it was by the half given. And an edge reaching through a face by no more than the planar tolerance of either side is not read as crossing it: on a prism of a thousand sides, each face on copies of its corners up to 0.002 off, the walls stand through the top and the bottom by up to 0.0025 where the first reaches weld some corners of those and not the walls' beside them, and those reaches, welding nothing through anything, are tried as they were.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Collision2
member.summary: Whether a straight shape touches or overlaps one that curves.
member.remarks: The rule is the one used everywhere else in this class: two shapes collide when their boundaries meet, or when one lies inside the other and the two never cross at all. A polygon, a rectangle and a circle are closed and so have an inside; a segment, a polyline and an arc do not, so for those nothing but a meeting counts. Two shapes meet where they cross or come within the point tolerance of each other, measured edge by edge along the arcs.
member.summary: Provides static calculation methods for checking spatial collisions and geometric overlaps.
Whether a ray in the plane touches another shape.
member.remarks: A ray runs on for ever in one direction, so against a shape with an end to it, it is cut: into the segment from its origin out past the farthest the shape reaches along it, by a margin of a millimetre or a hundred point tolerances, whichever is more. Nothing past that end is nearer the shape than the end itself, so the segment touches what the ray touches, and is asked as any segment is. Against the square 100 by 100 with a corner at the origin, the ray from (-50, 50) along X is asked as the segment from there to (101, 50). Against another ray nothing is cut, as there is no end to cut past.

member.summary: Determines whether a segment touches an arc, within a tolerance.
member.remarks: Neither has an inside, so they collide where they cross or come within the point tolerance of each other, as two segments do. At a tolerance of a thousandth, a segment ending half a thousandth short of an arc collides with it, and one ending two thousandths short does not.
