member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.MeshLift3
member.summary:
Lays the rings of a flat shape of space out in a frame, for the meshing of the plane, and puts the vertices of the mesh it gives back into space.
A corner of the shape goes back to the corner it was laid out from, exactly, wherever the shape has it. A shape a hair out of flat, as the faces from a modeller are, keeps its corners where they are, off the plane by up to the planar tolerance; a point the meshing put on one of its sides goes back onto that side in space, at the same share of its length, so that the faces along the rim meet the shape's edges; and a point inside goes onto the plane. Put onto the plane as well, a point on a side beside a corner off it would stand between the two, and the faces there would stand on end.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.Newell
member.summary:
Computes the area vector of a closed loop of 3D points by Newell's method.
A polygon in space has no single pair of coordinates to take a shoelace sum over, and picking one by dropping the axis the polygon leans on least works but breaks down near the changeover. Newell's method sidesteps the choice: it sums a signed contribution per edge on all three axes at once, and the resulting vector points along the polygon normal with a length equal to the area. It is also forgiving of vertices that are not exactly coplanar, which is what makes it the right tool for deciding whether a nearly flat loop is flat enough.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.Newell.GetAreaVector(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3})
member.summary: Gets the signed area of a closed loop as a vector normal to it.
member.param: The vertices of the loop, in order. The loop is treated as closed, so the last vertex is joined back to the first without needing to be repeated.
member.returns:
A vector along the loop normal whose length is the area of the loop, or the zero vector when the loop has fewer than three vertices or encloses nothing.
Note the difference from , which is a bare cross product and so comes back at twice the area. The halving is applied here.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.PointGrid
member.summary: Items filed under a point, so that the ones whose point lies within the tolerance of another are found without looking at every item.
member.remarks: Space is cut into cubes twice the tolerance wide. Two points within the tolerance of each other differ by less than a cube along every axis, so they sit in the same cube or in neighbouring ones, and a search of the 27 cubes about a point finds every item that could match it — along with some that do not, which the caller rules out with the exact test it would have made anyway. That is what lets a comparison of every pair keep its answer while only looking at the pairs that could agree.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.StripTriangulation
member.summary:
Breaks the material of a flat face into triangles by cutting it into strips at its corners, whatever its rings do to each other.
Ear clipping needs the rings of a face to stand apart, since it joins them into one loop that must not touch itself. This needs nothing of them. The region is first resolved as the booleans read it, but each ring within rounding rather than the tolerance, inside the boundary and outside every hole, into loops that neither cross nor overlap: holes that touch or overlap are taken together, and one reaching past the boundary takes away only what it covers. Lines across the plane through every corner of those loops then cut the region into strips. Within a strip no edge ends and none crosses another, so the material between two edges in turn is a trapezoid, two triangles; a trapezoid running on between the same two edges into the next strip is carried on, so that a strip line ends a piece only where something changes.
The triangles lie within the material and leave every hole open. They keep the face's own corners, but meet its edges at points of their own as well, where a strip line crosses them.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Core.StripTriangulation.WithinRounding
member.summary: What each ring's corners are read within before the strips are cut: nothing but rounding. Only its point tolerance is read, so corners are merged only where they stand on each other and dropped only within a few steps of the grid Clipper2 rounds to of a straight run.
member.remarks: The faces that come here are the ones whose rings come within the tolerance of each other, and corners read within the tolerance lose what lies within it. A wall of a cut plate 50 by 1.50015, with corners at 1.5 up both its sides, had the corners 0.00015 apart merged at a thousandth, the one kept on one side and the other on the other, and its triangles came to 0.00375 less than the wall; the plate's mass read through them held 0.175 too much. A corner a hundredth of the tolerance off a straight run was dropped, and a notch 0.0002 wide closed. Read within rounding, the triangles cover what the face covers; only a loop thinner than the tolerance is still left out.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.VertexWelder
member.summary:
Gives every distinct position a stable index, treating positions within tolerance as the same one.
Matching within a tolerance cannot use a dictionary directly: two points that should match may round to different keys, and a hash of a coordinate says nothing about which coordinates are near it. The way round is to lay a grid over space with cells the size of the tolerance, so anything close enough to match is in the same cell or one of the twenty-six touching it. Searching those twenty-seven buckets turns matching a vertex from a scan of everything seen so far into a scan of its immediate neighbourhood, which is what takes welding a surface from quadratic time to linear.

member.remarks: The three indices cannot be packed into a long without limiting how far from the origin the geometry may sit, so they are hashed instead. A collision costs only a few extra comparisons, because every candidate is checked against the real coordinates before it is accepted.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.ClipperRegion
member.summary:
The bridge to Clipper2, which resolves regions for and .
Everything crossing it is in a local frame: the caller moves its shapes so that one of their vertices sits at the origin, because Clipper2 rounds coordinates to a fixed number of decimal places and works on the integers that gives. Near the origin eight decimal places fit comfortably; a drawing hundreds of kilometres out would not, and would lose the digits that matter.
A region handed to Clipper2 is a set of loops read under a fill rule; what comes back is cleaned up in three steps before the rest of the library sees it. A loop that touches itself at a vertex, as two pieces meeting at a point come back, is split there into simple loops. Every vertex then gets its full precision back: one that is an input vertex rounded is replaced by that vertex, and one where two input edges cross is replaced by their crossing computed in double precision, so rounding to the grid leaves no trace in the answer. Last, points closer than the point tolerance are merged, loops thinner than it are dropped, and the loops are grouped, every outer boundary with the holes directly inside it.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.ClipperRegion.GetPrecision(System.Double)
member.summary: Chooses how many decimal places Clipper2 rounds to: eight, its finest, unless the drawing is so large that the integers would grow past 1e14, which leaves room for the products its tests form.

member.summary: The distance below which a point lying off a straight run counts as lying on it, used to drop the points splitting leaves along straight edges: a hundredth of the point tolerance, but never finer than the grid Clipper2 rounds to.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.ClipperRegion.Resolve(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint2}},GeometryHelper.Clipper.FillRule,System.Int32,GeometryHelper.Tolerance)
member.summary: Resolves a region given by loops under a fill rule and groups the result.
Combines two regions, each given by loops, and groups the result.

Combines two regions as does, but hands the loops back as Clipper2 gives them once their vertices have their full precision back: a loop running through a vertex twice is split there, and the loops are grouped, but nothing is merged within a tolerance and no thin loop left out. Pieces cut from one region side by side then keep the very points where they meet, as a mesh of them needs; only a point repeated in a row, a point standing on a straight run within rounding, and a loop enclosing nothing at all go.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Core.ClipperRegion.DropStraight(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint2},System.Double)
member.summary: Drops the points of a loop that stand on the line between their neighbours, within a distance.
member.remarks: Where edges of the two regions run along each other, Clipper2 can split the edge across from where they end, and hand the split back as a point of its own, rounded to its grid: a cell laid along the side of a rectangle came back with a corner halfway along its other side. Such a point is no crossing and no input vertex, so nothing gives it its digits back, and the pieces either side of that side would meet at it only in part. A point the pieces beside need is put back on the side by the mesh that joins them.

member.summary: The input vertices and edges, used to give the vertices Clipper2 returns the digits its rounding took off.
member.remarks: A crossing was restored from the edges filed under the cell of a grid 64 cells across the drawing that the point falls in, each edge filed under every cell of its box. On a long shape those cells grew long with it, and every point looked through thousands of edges: a comb of 40 000 teeth took 4.4 seconds to offset by a half, where Clipper2 itself took a third of one. The edges are found in cells sized and shaped by them now, each filed under the cells along it rather than the whole of its box, and still kept only where they lie in the point's cell of the 64 and within reach of it, in the order they were added; and each input vertex is filed once, under its own cell, rather than under every cell a grid step from it. The same points are restored to the bit, and the comb is offset in 0.8 seconds.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Core.PointTree3
member.summary: A set of points of space laid out in a tree of boxes, so that the ones lying near a stretch of a line are found without looking at the others.

remarks.para: The points are cut in two at the middle of their longest side, over and over, until a box holds eight or fewer. A stretch of line is then taken down the tree, into a box only if the stretch comes within the reach of it, so that a thousand points far from the line cost the one look at the box that holds them. This is what the edges of a fan need: sorted along an axis, all the edges of a cone of 16 000 sides overlap the others at the apex and are tried against each other, 768 million pairs; asked which points lie along each edge, each is asked of the few near it.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgContainer
member.summary: The parts of a DWG file taken out of its container, as the decoders of objects need them whatever the version: the version and the code page, the data of the header variables and of the classes, and the object map with the bytes its offsets count into. Reading the container is the only step that knows where a version keeps its sections. Of R2000 (AC1015) the sections lie in the file as they are, found through the section locator records of the file header; of R2004 (AC1018) and of R2010 to R2018 (AC1024, AC1027, AC1032) they are compressed pages, read in DwgContainer.R2004.cs; R2007 (AC1021) has a container of its own, read in DwgContainer.R2007.cs.
member.content: The container of R2004 and later (AC1018, AC1024, AC1027, AC1032): a file header whose second part is masked, then pages, each on a 32-byte boundary. Two system pages map the rest: the page map gives the place of every page, the section map gives the pages of each named section. The pages of a section are decompressed and joined, and the sections the reader needs are taken from them: the header variables, the classes, the object map and the objects.

The container of R2007 (AC1021): a file header of 0x400 bytes at 0x80, coded by Reed-Solomon (255, 239) in three interleaved blocks and compressed, then pages from 0x480 on. As in R2004 a page map places the pages and a section map gives the pages of each named section, but both are system pages coded the same way, the data pages are coded by Reed-Solomon (255, 251), the compression is a variant of its own () and the check sums are CRCs of 64 bits. The parity bytes of the Reed-Solomon code are not used: the data bytes are taken out of the blocks and the CRCs and sums say whether they are whole.

From R2004 on the map is a section of its own, the same in form.

member.summary: The data of the file header of R2007, 0x110 bytes: the 0x400 bytes at 0x80 are three Reed-Solomon blocks, interleaved, whose data begins with a CRC, a key, the CRC of the compressed data and its size, then the data. Of each page the mirrored CRC of 64 bits of its compressed bytes and the sum of its data are checked.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgContainerWriter
member.summary: Puts the sections of a DWG file into the container of R2004 and later (AC1018, AC1024, AC1027, AC1032), the mirror of 's reading of it: the file header with its masked second part, then the data pages of each section, then the section map and the page map. A data page holds at most the page size of its section; a compressed one is filled out to that size with zeros and compressed whole, as AutoCAD writes its pages, an uncompressed one is filled out with zeros. Each page stands on a 32-byte boundary, the gap filled with the series the file header is masked with, and every sum is written as the reader checks it.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgContainerWriter21
member.summary: Puts the sections of a DWG file into the container of R2007 (AC1021), the mirror of 's reading of it (DwgContainer.R2007.cs): a file header of 0x80 bytes, then 0x400 bytes of the header proper, compressed and coded by Reed-Solomon (255, 239) in three interleaved blocks, then the pages from 0x480 on: the page map and its copy, the data pages of the sections in turn, the section map and its copy, and a copy of the 0x400 bytes of the header at the end. A data page of coding 4 is its data, compressed where that makes it shorter (), coded by Reed-Solomon (255, 251) in interleaved blocks, and takes 255 bytes of every 251 of data, to a multiple of 32; a page of coding 1 is its data stored as it is, filled out to the page size of its section, and 32 bytes. A system page, the page map or the section map, holds its data, compressed where that makes it shorter, as many times over as its place takes, in blocks of Reed-Solomon (255, 239). Every sum is written as checks it: the sum of the data of a page, the CRC of 64 bits of the bytes stored, and the CRCs of the page maps and of the header.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgCrc
member.summary: The check sums of a DWG file. The 16-bit one, which the Open Design Specification calls the 8-bit CRC after its table of 256 entries: the reflected polynomial 0xA001, each byte folded in as (crc >> 8) ^ table[(crc ^ b) & 0xFF]; sections and objects start it from 0xC0C1, the file header of R2000 from 0. From R2004 on also the 32-bit CRC of the file header and the sums of the pages.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgDataStore
member.summary: The data store of a DWG of R2013 and later (the section AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b), which holds the ACIS data of the REGION, 3DSOLID and BODY entities as SAB, one record an entity by its handle. The store is bytes, not bits: a head naming the segment of the index of segments, then segments each with a head of 0x30 bytes. The index of data gives for each record its data segment and where its head stands; the head gives the handle and where its bytes stand after the heads; the bytes are a size and that many, or past 0x40000 bytes a reference to pages in segments of their own (blob01). The layout follows the Open Design Specification for .dwg files, chapter 24.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgDataStoreWriter
member.summary: Writes the data store of a DWG of R2013 and later (the section AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b) that holds the ACIS data of the REGION, 3DSOLID and BODY entities, the mirror of . The store is a head and segments, each with a head of 0x30 bytes and padded with 0x70 to a whole number of 0x80 bytes, laid out as AutoCAD 2021 lays them: the index of segments (1), the index of data (2), the data (3), the index and the data of the schemas (4 and 5), a segment for each page of a record past 0x40000 bytes (blob01), and the search segment last. The layout follows the Open Design Specification for .dwg files, chapter 24, and AutoCAD's own files.

member.summary: Turns the SAT of each REGION, 3DSOLID and BODY that holds text (a DXF of R2000 to R2010: its lines after AcDbModelerGeometry, no GUID) into the SAB of , as AutoCAD 2021 does when it saves such a drawing as a DWG of R2018: the entity names its data by a GUID (the one its extended data kept, which is taken out, else one made of its handle, so that the same drawing gives the same bytes), the data joins , and the date of the SAT stays the date of the SAB. member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgDxfWriter
member.summary: Writes the DXF a DWG file is turned into, as bytes: the texts of the DWG go in as the bytes they are, in the drawing's code page, so the DXF reader decodes them as it decodes any DXF file. A control character in a text is written the way DXF writes it, a caret and the letter 64 above it, and a caret as a caret and a space. The bytes are made in one array that doubles as it fills, with no stream and no string made for a code, a whole number, a handle or a number that is whole: a DXF of 46 MB, 300 000 entities, is some 4 million groups.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgLz21
member.summary: The decompression of R2007 (AC1021), a variant of LZ77 of its own, as the Open Design Specification for .dwg files gives it (paragraph 5.10) and the reader of ACadSharp (MIT) reads it: runs of bytes taken from the input, in an order of their own within each run, alternate with runs copied from earlier in the output. A run that would write past the output, copy from before its start or read past the end of the input refuses the data, so no hostile length allocates or loops beyond the bytes of the file.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgLz21.Orders
member.summary: The order in which a run of 1 to 31 literal bytes is laid into the output: entry n gives, for each byte written, the index of the input byte it comes from. A run of 32 or more is laid 32 bytes at a time, in four groups of eight from the last to the first, and its rest by this table.

member.summary: Decompresses the bytes of from into , from its start; returns the number of bytes written. Throws where the data would run past either end.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgLz21.Compress(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Compresses into the form reads: a run of literal bytes of 8 or more, then copies from earlier in the data, each followed by 0 to 7 literal bytes in the last byte of its code, or by a run of 8 or more after it. The data is searched for the longest copy of 3 bytes or more, from 65 535 bytes back and 255 long, by chains of the positions that begin with the same three bytes, and a copy is taken where it is longer than the bytes its code takes (2 to 4). Returns null where the data is shorter than 16 bytes or the result is not shorter than it, as AutoCAD stores such a page as it is; the result is read back before it is given.

The long form of the shortest codes (a length of 19 to 50) begins with 0 after a run of literal bytes and with 15 after another copy, as the reading of a code that begins with 0 there takes it for a run.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader
member.content: The objects of the associative network a dynamic block keeps for its constraint parameters and user parameters: the networks, the variables, the dependencies and their bodies, and the constraint parameters that lean on them. No source gives their layouts: each is read from AutoCAD 2021's own DWG bytes and checked, group for group, against its DXF of the same drawing.
member.summary: Decodes the objects of a DWG file of R2000 into records. An object is its size, its type, the data every object carries, the data of its type, and at the end the handles the data refers to; the two runs are read side by side. The field orders follow the Open Design Specification for .dwg files and the reader of ACadSharp (MIT), whose notice stands in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.
member.content: The objects a dynamic block keeps: the evaluation graph and the expressions it owns (the parameters, grips and actions of a linear, visibility, flip, rotation, XY, polar, point, base point, lookup and alignment parameter and of a stretch, polar stretch, move, scale, rotate, flip, array and lookup action, and the components of the locations of the grips), and the representation data of its anonymous blocks. The layouts follow ACadSharp (MIT) and are checked against AutoCAD 2021's own DXF of the same drawings.
The entities: each reads its data in the order of the file and adds its groups in the order of DXF.
The objects of fields and of the draw order: SORTENTSTABLE, FIELDLIST and FIELD.

The multileader and its style. A MULTILEADER keeps its context first (the leaders and the content as drawn) and its own properties after; DXF writes the context between CONTEXT_DATA{ and }, its leaders after its content, and gives each colour as the one number of a CMC colour ().
The objects that are neither entities nor tables: dictionaries, records of free data, layouts and the like.
The table content of R2010 and later (), which an ACAD_TABLE holds in place of the cells of R2007, and the cell styles a TABLESTYLE holds.
The tables: their control objects and their records.

The detail and section view styles a new drawing holds from AutoCAD 2013 on, in every version AutoCAD saves them, and the manager of the persistent names of subentities beside the solids. The file keeps each property in an order of its own; DXF gives them in groups marked 71 0 to 71 4, which these put them back into.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocAction
member.summary: The start of every action (AcDbAssocAction): a version, a status, three numbers DXF gives after its two pointers (the network it belongs to, as a soft pointer, and an action body, hard owned).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocValue(System.Int32)
member.summary: A value an association keeps (an AcDbEvalVariant): a kind (none, a text, a real of 40 or a whole number of 90) and the value under the code that names its kind, left out for none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocVariable
member.summary: A variable (AcDbAssocVariable): its version, name, expression, evaluator and a text, its value, two flags and the objects it feeds, each a hard owned pointer and a number.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocNetwork
member.summary: A network (AcDbAssocNetwork): its version, the highest index of its actions and their count; each action is a pointer, hard owned (360) where a bit before the list is set and soft (330) where it is not; then the count of a second list of soft pointers (330), 0 in the networks of AutoCAD's dynamic block samples and 1 in one its API made (the action it holds is listed again).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocDependency
member.summary: A dependency (AcDbAssocDependency): the numbers, flags and pointers every dependency carries.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocGeomDependency
member.summary: A dependency on a piece of geometry (AcDbAssocGeomDependency): a number, a flag, the class of the way it names the edge (without a number, or with two numbers after a third) and a flag.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.EdgeName
member.summary: The class of the way a dependency names an edge: its name as a text, and from R2013 a flag and a number of a short, 1 for AcDbAssocSingleEdgePersSubentId and 3 for AcDbAssocEdgePersSubentId.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocValueDependency
member.summary: A dependency on a value (AcDbAssocValueDependency): a number, a name and the value.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocDependencyBody(System.String)
member.summary: The body of a dependency that holds a dimension or a block parameter (AcDbAssocDependencyBody and the base of AcDbImpAssocDimDependencyBody): two versions and a text; is the marker of the last class, which holds a number.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocConstraintGroup
member.summary: A group of 2D constraints (AcDbAssoc2dConstraintGroup): a number and a flag, the plane it lies in (an origin and two axes), the actions it owns, two numbers (the next identifier and the count of its nodes) and the nodes, the geometry and constraints the solver keeps. A DWG of R2010 keeps the nodes in an order of its own, which DXF gives by identifier; a group of the version 2 (AutoCAD 2018) is read by .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadConstraintNumbers
member.summary: The identifiers of the constraints a piece of geometry takes part in: a count and each number.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadConstraintNode
member.summary: One node of a constraint group: its class (a text), the group (330, which the file does not repeat), its identifier and a byte, and what its class adds. Returns the identifier.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadConstraintFields(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: What a node of a constraint group holds past its identifiers (and past its byte, in the layout of R2018), by its class: the pointer, numbers and points of a piece of geometry, or the flags and pointers of a constraint.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadAssocConstraintGroup2(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: The rest of a group of the version 2 of AutoCAD 2018, past the next identifier: two numbers and a flag, then the table of the classes of its nodes (a count and the names, in the order the nodes first name them), the count of the nodes, a directory of every node (its class by the number of the table, from 1, and its identifier) and then the nodes themselves, each with its identifier first, then its identifiers, a byte, and what its class adds. DXF gives the same in that order: the numbers and the flag, the count, the directory as class name and identifier, and the nodes without their class.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadBlockConstraintParameter(System.String)

member.summary: A block properties table: a parameter of one point, its name and a number, the columns (each the parameter it reads or sets, the names of its property and connection, the node it stands for, two values, five flags and a text; DXF gives the parameter before them and a second pointer after) and the rows (a number and a value for each column), and the row count again with three flags.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadBlockRepresentationData

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadEvaluationGraph
member.summary: The evaluation graph of a dynamic block: two numbers DXF repeats, the nodes (index, flags, id, the expression they hold and four numbers) and the edges between them (index, flags, count, the two nodes and five numbers).

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.LongText
member.summary: The pseudo group code of the text of an MTEXT, which DXF writes in pieces of 250 under 3 and the rest under 1.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadShape
member.summary: A SHAPE: its place, size, turn, width, slant, thickness and extrusion, and the number of its shape in the file of shapes of its text style, which the transcoder writes as the shape's name where it finds that file. DXF leaves out a turn, slant and thickness of 0, a width of 1 and the extrusion (0, 0, 1).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.FarApart(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3})
member.summary: Whether finite points lie so far apart that the distance from the first to one of them is past the largest double.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadText(System.Int32)
member.summary: A TEXT ( 0), an ATTRIB (1) or an ATTDEF (2); false for an attribute of several lines, which is not read yet.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadEmbeddedMText(System.Int32@)
member.summary: The MTEXT of an attribute of several lines (R2018): its common entity data, read past as the file has it, and its own data, whose groups DXF writes after 101 Embedded Object; then the annotative data, whose last value DXF writes as 72 of the attribute.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMTextColumns
member.summary: The columns of an MTEXT of R2018, read past: a bit, where it is set a version, a flag, the handle of an application, the attachment, two points, four numbers and the kind of columns, with their sizes and heights.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadOwned
member.summary: The entities a polyline owns: before R2004 its first and last vertex, from R2004 a count in the data and that many handles; then its SEQEND.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadOwnedHandles(System.Int32)
member.summary: Before R2004 the first and the last owned entity, which lead one to the next; from R2004 the owned entities.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadViewport
member.summary: A VIEWPORT of a layout. Its number (group 69) and status (68) are not in the file: the transcoder gives them from the order of the viewports of its layout, so the groups carry a here.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadHatch
member.summary: A HATCH: from R2004 its gradient, then its plane, its pattern name, its boundary paths (a polyline with or without bulges, or edges: lines, arcs, elliptic arcs and splines, with fit points from R2010), the objects each path follows, its style and pattern lines, and its seed points. DXF writes the gradient at the end, and from R2004 only for a solid fill.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadHatchEdge
member.summary: One edge of a boundary path of a HATCH: its kind (group 72) and its data.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadLeader
member.summary: A LEADER: the kind of its annotation and path, its points, its plane and offsets, the size of the box of its text, its hook line and arrow, and the handles of its annotation and dimension style. DXF leaves the arrow out where it is on, the path where it is straight, the annotation kind and the box where there is none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadOle2Frame
member.summary: An OLE2FRAME: its version, the space it stands in, the object's binary (AutoCAD's head of 128 bytes with the four corners of the frame, then the compound file) and, last, how it is plotted. DXF holds the same binary in lines of 127 bytes under 310, with the corners as 10 and 11, and the kind (71) and user type (3) that the compound file gives, as the library's reader of an OLE2FRAME takes them from there; the pairs of 71 and 3 and of 10 and 11 are left out where the file holds no head or no compound file.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTolerance
member.summary: A TOLERANCE, a feature control frame: its point, direction, plane and text, and its dimension style.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadRasterImage(System.String)
member.summary: An IMAGE or a WIPEOUT (): its corner and pixel vectors, its size, its display flags and levels, and its clip boundary, two corners or a polygon. A wipeout names no image definition and no reactor, and DXF writes both as 0.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadPdfUnderlay
member.summary: A PDFUNDERLAY: its normal, insertion point, turn (radians, DXF has degrees), scale along the three sides, display flags, contrast and fade, its clip boundary (a count and that many corners, two for a rectangle) and by handle its definition.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMLine
member.summary: An MLINE: its scale, justification, start, plane and flags, then for each vertex its point, direction and mitre and for each line of the style its segment and fill parameters; the style by handle, and DXF names it too.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMLineParameters(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgGroup},System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: A count of parameters (a bit short) under and the parameters under .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadModelerGeometry(System.Boolean)
member.summary: A REGION, a 3DSOLID or a BODY ( for a 3DSOLID): its ACIS data as DXF carries it. Before R2013 the data is SAT text in blocks, each character but a line end kept as 0x9F less it, and DXF writes it so, a line a group 1 (pieces past 255 under 3). From R2013 the data is in the data store of the file, which DXF writes in its own section; the entity carries its GUID, after the wireframe and silhouettes, which are read past. From R2004 AutoCAD keeps the data as SAB (version 2), which turns into the SAT AutoCAD writes of it; false where it cannot.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddSatLines(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Byte})
member.summary: The SAT text of an ACIS entity, a line a group 1; a line past 255 bytes in pieces of 255, each but the last under group 3 and the last under 1, as AutoCAD writes it.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadWireframe
member.summary: The wireframe and the silhouettes of an ACIS entity from R2013, read past.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTable
member.summary: An ACAD_TABLE before R2007: a block reference to its anonymous block, then its flags, direction, rows and columns with their sizes, its style, its cells (a text or a block each, with overrides) and the overrides of the whole table. DXF writes the overrides' flags (93 to 96) and the overrides before the sizes.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddTableReference(System.Boolean,System.UInt64,System.Double[],System.Double[],System.Double,System.Double[])
member.summary: The block reference a table is, as DXF writes it before the table's own groups.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTableCell(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgGroup})
member.summary: One cell of a table before R2007: its kind, edges, merging and size, its overrides, and its text or block.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadCellValue(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgGroup})
member.summary: The value of a table cell from R2007, between 301 CELL_VALUE and 304 ACVALUE_END: its flags, its type and, unless flag 1 says it is empty, the value (a string as UTF-16 counted in bytes), its unit type, its format and the text it shows.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadFlagged(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgGroup},System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Char)
member.summary: A value present where is set in , under : S a bit short, B a bit, C a CMC colour (its index), H a handle, D a bit double.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTableOverrides(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgGroup})
member.summary: The overrides of a whole table before R2007; returns their flags.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadBorderOverrides(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgGroup},System.Int32)
member.summary: The border overrides of a whole table before R2007, 18 borders by flag: 0 colours, 1 lineweights, 2 visibilities. Returns their flags.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadSortEntitiesTable
member.summary: A SORTENTSTABLE, the draw order of a block: its count, then for each entry the sort handle in the data (the handle the entity is sorted by, which need not name an entity) and the entity in the handles, after the block's own handle. DXF gives the block, then each entity (331) followed by its sort handle (5).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadFieldList
member.summary: A FIELDLIST, the fields of the drawing: a count, a flag DXF does not give, then each field as a soft pointer.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadField
member.summary: A FIELD: its evaluator and its code (DXF breaks a code over 250 characters into pieces under group 3, the rest under 2), the fields it holds and the objects it names, the format before R2007, its options and state, the error it ended in, its value, the text it shows and the values it keeps by name. DXF gives the values by name first, then the value of the field itself as ACFD_FIELD_VALUE, then the text and its length.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.CompareBytes(System.Byte[],System.Byte[])
member.summary: Two texts compared byte by byte, the shorter first where one begins the other.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadFieldValue
member.summary: A value of a field (20.4.99): from R2007 its flags (1 where it holds nothing), its type, the value, its unit, its format and the text it shows; before R2007 the type and the value alone. A date is kept as its bytes.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.CustomDataFlag
member.summary: The bit of the options of a DATALINK that says its custom data follow; DXF leaves it out of group 90.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadDataLink
member.summary: A DATALINK, a link of a table to data outside the drawing: its adapter, description, tooltip and connection, its options, the time of its last update, the objects it fills, and its custom data, a map from names to values that the file holds only where the options say so (DXF writes the map, empty, either way).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddFieldValue(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgCellValue)
member.summary: A value of a field in DXF: its flags (from R2007), type, the value, and from R2007 its unit, format, text and the closing 304.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMultiLeaderContext
member.summary: The context of a multileader: its leaders, read first and written last, and its text or block content.

member.summary: One leader of a multileader, between LEADER{ and }: its landing, breaks and lines.

member.summary: One line of a leader of a multileader, between LEADER_LINE{ and }.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddHandle(System.Int32,System.UInt64)

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadImageDefinition

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadPdfDefinition
member.summary: A PDFDEFINITION: the path of the PDF file and the name of the page, its number as text.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadImageDefinitionReactor
member.summary: An IMAGEDEF_REACTOR: its class version, then its image, its owner, which DXF writes again.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadSpatialFilter
member.summary: A SPATIAL_FILTER, the clip boundary of a block reference or an external reference: the number of points and the points, the normal and the origin of the clip coordinate system, whether the clip is on, the front and back planes where they are on, and the two matrices of twelve numbers each.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadRasterVariables
member.summary: The RASTERVARIABLES of the drawing: its class version, whether frames show, the quality and the unit of images.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadWipeoutVariables
member.summary: The WIPEOUTVARIABLES of the drawing: whether the frames of wipeouts show.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadDynamicBlockPurgePreventer
member.summary: The ACDB_DYNAMICBLOCKPURGEPREVENTER_VERSION a dynamic block keeps in its extension dictionary: a version of one, which AutoCAD takes as the sign that the block is not to be purged as unused.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadBookColour
member.summary: A DBCOLOR, a colour of a book: from R2004 a CMC colour with its name and its book, which DXF writes as 62, 420 and 430; before R2004 an index, which DXF does not write.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTableStyle
member.summary: A TABLESTYLE before R2010: its description, flow, margins and what it suppresses, then the styles of the data, title and header rows, each a text style, height, alignment, colours, from R2007 a data format, and six borders. False from R2010, whose styles are cell styles, not read yet.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMaterial
member.summary: A MATERIAL: its name and description, its ambient, diffuse and specular colours, each a way (0 the object's own, 1 its own colour), a factor and the colour itself where its own, then a map of each kind, diffuse, specular, reflection, opacity, bump and refraction, among them the gloss, the opacity and the index of refraction, and from R2007 the translucence, self-illumination, reflectivity, illumination model, channels and mode. DXF writes what differs from a new material's values, as AutoCAD's DXF of it does; the settings of R2010 on are in the records of its extension dictionary.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMaterialColour(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: A colour of a material: its way (), its factor, and its colour where it is its own.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadMaterialMap(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: A map of a material: its blend factor, its projection, tiling and automatic transform, its matrix of 16, its source (0 the scene, 1 a file) and the file, written in the order DXF gives them.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.VisualStyleKinds
member.summary: The kinds of the 58 properties of a visual style of R2013 and later, in their order: 9 a whole number (DXF 90), 4 a real (40), 6 a colour (62 and 420), 2 a yes or no (290), 1 a text (1).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadVisualStyle
member.summary: A VISUALSTYLE of R2013 and later: its name, type and version, whether it is for AutoCAD's own use, then each of its 58 properties, a value and how it is applied (176: 0 taken from the style it derives from, 1 set), which DXF gives after their count (70 58).

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.VisualStyleCodes2010
member.summary: The DXF groups of the 28 properties of a visual style of R2010, the first 28 of the later 58.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadVisualStyle2007
member.summary: A VISUALSTYLE of R2004 and R2007, each property in a place of its own, put into the order of DXF: the face's lighting, its colour (62 always 5, which the file does not hold) and its mono colour, the edges, the display.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadStyleColour
member.summary: A colour of a visual style: a CMC colour, no colour (0xC8) given as 257.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadXRecord
member.summary: The data of an XRECORD: groups one after another, each its code as a short and a value whose form the code decides, the way a binary DXF file writes them.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadPlotPart
member.summary: Reads the part of a LAYOUT or a PLOTSETTINGS that is the page setup, its data and its handles, and gives back what adds its groups, AcDbPlotSettings, to the record once the rest of the object has been read.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadPlotSettings
member.summary: Reads a PLOTSETTINGS, a named page setup: the page setup part of a LAYOUT alone.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.StylesOf(System.UInt64)
member.summary: The cell styles of the table style of a handle, by id, read once by a reader of its own; none where the object map is not given or the style cannot be read.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddCellStyleMap(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Object[]})
member.summary: The CELLSTYLEMAP AutoCAD writes in DXF for a table style, which a DWG does not hold: each of its cell styles, its format, then its id, class and name; kept on the style for the transcoder to put under its extension dictionary.

member.summary: The CELLSTYLEMAP object of a DWG of R2007 and before, which keeps the cell styles of a table style that a DXF of AutoCAD 2007 does not hold in its rows: a count, then each style as a table style of R2010 and later holds it (its id, kind and name after it).

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.Looks
member.summary: The properties of a cell's looks, in the order AutoCAD 2021 writes a cell's own: 170, 7, 63, 64, 283, 140.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.Looks.Take(System.Int32,GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgContentFormat,System.Int32)
member.summary: Takes from a cell style or a content format the properties its flags override that are not taken yet.

member.summary: Takes the properties of a cell style of its own that differ from those of the kind of row, not taken yet.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTable2010(System.UInt64)
member.summary: An ACAD_TABLE of R2010 and later after its block reference: a version and two values of no known use, its content, its direction and its break data; written as DXF writes it, in the groups of R2007: the table's own overrides (93 to 96 and their groups), its rows and columns with their sizes, then each cell with how it is merged, its overrides and its value.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddTableOverrides(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableContent)
member.summary: The table's own overrides of R2007, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them from R2010: the flags 93 to 96, then their groups in its head, the margins of the table's own cell style (40 horizontal, 41 vertical), then of the first row of each kind (title, header, data) the looks and the lines its cell style overrides, by property: heights, alignments, fills, colours, the lines' colours and showing, whether filled, text styles and the lines' lineweights; each line of a kind in the order top, inside horizontal, bottom, left, inside vertical, right.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.MergeOf(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableContent,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: How the cell of row and column is merged, as groups 173, 175 and 176 give it: whether another cell covers it, and the columns and rows it spans.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.RangeOf(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableContent,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: The merged range (top row, left column, bottom row, right column) that holds a cell; null for none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddTableCell(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableContent,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.Int32,GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgCellStyle},System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: A cell in the groups of R2007: its kind, edges, merging, flags, rotation, block, the overrides AutoCAD 2021 writes for it and its value. Its looks are its content's own, else its cell style's, its row's, its column's, else those of a cell style of its own (101 on, of the cell, else its column, else its row) where they differ from those of its kind of row; written 170, 7, 63, 64, 283, 140. Its edges are its top and left, and its right and bottom in the last column and row: each its own border, else the one its neighbour shares, else its row's outer one where the edge is the row's, else, at the top of a row of another style than the cell above, the bottom border of that style; written right, bottom, left, top, each a lineweight, whether hidden where that is overridden (1 hidden) and a colour. A merged range gives its edges on its last cell alone, the borders of its first cell, without the edges inside the range: a title over three columns, its top and right on its third cell.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.CellAt(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableContent,System.Int32,System.Int32)

member.summary: The cell style a cell takes: its own, else its column's, else its row's.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.Own(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableCell,System.Int32)
member.summary: The border of an edge a cell overrides itself; null for none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.Outer(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableLine,System.Int32)
member.summary: The outer border of an edge a row's cell style overrides; null for none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.Boundary(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTableContent,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.Int32,GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgCellStyle},System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: The bottom border of the style of the cell above where it is not the default and not the top border of the cell's own style, a style of a kind of row, as AutoCAD writes the line under a title of lineweight 0.35 on each cell of the header below; null where there is none to write.

member.summary: A TABLESTYLE of R2010 and later: a version, its description, its flags, the next number of a cell style of its own and the cell styles Table, _TITLE, _HEADER and _DATA; written as DXF writes it, in the groups of R2007: its direction and margins from Table, then the data, title and header rows, each its text, colours, format and six borders (top, inside horizontal, bottom, left, inside vertical, right).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddRowStyle(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgCellStyle)
member.summary: A row style of R2007 from a cell style: its text, colours, format and borders.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.IndexOf(System.Int32)
member.summary: The colour index of a CMC colour given as its one number: 256 by layer, 0 by block, else its index.

member.summary: A collection of custom data: its count, then for each a name and a value.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadValue
member.summary: A value (20.4.99): its flags, its type, the value unless it holds nothing, its unit, format and text.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadContentFormat
member.summary: A content format (20.4.101.3).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadCellStyle
member.summary: A cell style (20.4.101.4): its type and, where it has data, what it overrides.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.ReadTableContentObject

member.summary: The custom data in DXF: its count, then each item its name and its value.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddTableFormat(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgCellStyle)

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectReader.AddContentFormat(GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgContentFormat)

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectWriter
member.content: REGION, 3DSOLID and BODY. From R2013 the entity carries the GUID of its ACIS data, which the data store of the file holds (); in R2004, R2007 and R2010 the entity holds the SAB itself, and in R2000 the SAT text.

The objects of the associative network of a dynamic block (DwgObjectReader.Associations): each is written from the groups of its DXF in their order, its pointers in the handle stream in the order DXF gives them, a soft pointer (330) as code 4 and a hard owned one (360) as code 3.
member.summary: Encodes the records of a DXF file into the objects of a DWG file, the reverse of and the transcoder: each record's groups are put back into the fields of its object in the order of the file, its handles into the handle stream, its texts from R2007 into the string stream. An object is its size, from R2010 the size of its handles, its data and its check sum. The field orders follow the Open Design Specification for .dwg files and the writer of ACadSharp (MIT), whose notice stands in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md; each is the mirror of the reader's, which the round trip of the tests holds them to.
member.content: The objects a dynamic block keeps: the evaluation graph and the expressions it owns (the parameters, grips and actions the reader names), and the representation data of its anonymous blocks. Each is written from the groups of its DXF in the order AutoCAD gives them, the layouts of DwgObjectReader.DynamicBlocks.
The entities: each writes its data in the order of the file from the groups of its DXF record.
The objects of fields and of the draw order: SORTENTSTABLE, FIELDLIST and FIELD.

The multileader and its style, the mirror of the reader's: a MULTILEADER's context first, its leaders before its content though DXF writes them after, then its own properties; each colour the one number of a CMC colour.
The entities whose DXF groups come in runs that repeat: viewports, hatches, leaders, multilines; and tolerances.
The objects that are neither entities nor tables: dictionaries, records of free data, layouts and the like.

The ACAD_TABLE of R2000, R2004 and R2007, the mirror of DwgObjectReader.ReadTable: DXF keeps it as its block reference, its flags, rows and columns, the overrides of the whole table, the sizes and then each cell with its flags and the values the flags name; the file keeps the sizes first, then the cells, then the overrides of the whole table. R2010 keeps a table as a TABLECONTENT instead (WriteTable).

The ACAD_TABLE and the TABLESTYLE of R2010 and later, the mirror of the reader's: DXF keeps a table in the groups of R2007, its cells one by one, and the file keeps its content () with rows, columns, cells and merged ranges; a table style keeps its rows as the cell styles _TITLE, _HEADER and _DATA beside Table.
The tables: their control objects and their records.

The detail and section view styles and the manager of the persistent names of subentities, from the groups their DXF gives, into the order the file keeps (the reader's ReadDetailViewStyle and the like give the other way).

member.summary: Whether an ACIS entity is written. From R2013 it names the GUID of its data (group 2) and the section ACDSDATA holds that data under its handle. In R2004, R2007 and R2010 it is written where holds the SAB of its version (20800, 21200 or 21500, as makes it of the SAT a DXF of those versions gives). In R2000 it is written where its SAT is the text of ACIS 4.00 ().

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgObjectWriter.WithAsciiTexts(System.Byte[])
member.summary: The proxy graphics of a drawing of R2007 or later (a size, a count and the pieces, each a size, a type and its data) as a file before R2007 holds them: a text is the piece of type 38 with its strings in 16 bits there, and the piece of type 11 with them in 8 bits here, and AutoCAD refuses a file of R2004 (ErrorStatus 53) that has the first. Each piece of type 38 is made a piece of type 11, as AutoCAD makes it when it saves such a drawing as R2004: the text, the font and the big font in 8 bits, each with its closing zero and padded to four bytes, the nine numbers before the text and the length, the one and the four numbers after it as they were, and the seven words of flags and the three of R2007 that follow the numbers left out but five. A piece that does not hold a text as expected is left out, and the size and the count follow; graphics that is not made of whole pieces is kept as it is.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgReader
member.summary: Reads a DWG file as the drawing its DXF would give: the same that makes and the same that opens, so everything that works on a DXF works on a DWG.

remarks.para: DWG files of AC1015 (AutoCAD 2000), AC1018 (AutoCAD 2004), AC1021 (AutoCAD 2007), AC1024 (AutoCAD 2010), AC1027 (AutoCAD 2013) and AC1032 (AutoCAD 2018 and later) are read. A file of another version, R14 and older among them, or one protected by a password, is refused with a that names the version.

The file is turned, in memory, into the DXF that says the same, record for record with the handles of the file: the header variables, the classes, the nine tables, the blocks, the entities and the objects. Read are LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, SPLINE, RAY, XLINE, LWPOLYLINE, the 2D and 3D POLYLINE with their vertices, the polygon and polyface mesh, TEXT, MTEXT, ATTDEF, INSERT, alone or as an array, with its ATTRIBs, SOLID, TRACE, 3DFACE, SHAPE, DIMENSION, VIEWPORT, HATCH, LEADER, MULTILEADER, TOLERANCE, MLINE, OLE2FRAME, IMAGE, WIPEOUT and ACAD_TABLE, and of the objects DICTIONARY, XRECORD, LAYOUT, GROUP, MLINESTYLE, MLEADERSTYLE, TABLESTYLE, MATERIAL, VISUALSTYLE, the detail and section view styles, the FIELD and FIELDLIST of fields, the SORTENTSTABLE of the draw order, the CELLSTYLEMAP of a table style of AutoCAD 2000 to 2007, the data of a dynamic block of a linear parameter and a stretch action, the DATALINK of a table linked to data and the small ones a new drawing holds (see the guide for the full list); the ACIS data of the solids comes as SAT text to AutoCAD 2010, turned from the SAB AutoCAD keeps from AutoCAD 2004 into the SAT AutoCAD writes of it, and from AutoCAD 2013 from the data store of the file as the section ACDSDATA; each with its layer, linetype, colour, lineweight, owner, reactors, extension dictionary and extended data. A SHAPE is named from the file of shapes of its style where holds it, and else gives its number (group 70), as AutoCAD writes a shape whose file it does not find. An OLE2FRAME comes as the DXF of AutoCAD writes it, its binary in the groups 310, so that it is read as a . The preview image of the file, where it holds a picture, comes as the section THUMBNAILIMAGE of the DXF, last. The types not read yet (those AutoCAD 2021's own sample drawings hold are the other objects of dynamic blocks and of associative dimensions; and there are the proxies) are left out and counted by type in one Debug line of .

The check sums of the file are checked. A wrong one in the file header, the header variables, the classes or the object map, or from AutoCAD 2004 in a page of the file (from AutoCAD 2007 to 2009 its CRCs of 64 bits), refuses the file with a , and so does a file cut short there; one object with a wrong check sum, or that cannot be decoded, is left out, the others are read, and a Warn line counts them.
remarks.code: DxfDocument drawing = DwgReader.Read("plan.dwg", new DxfReadOptions { PlanAs2D = true }); DxfDatabase database = DwgReader.Open("plan.dwg");

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgReedSolomon
member.summary: The Reed-Solomon codes of R2007 (AC1021), as the Open Design Specification for .dwg files names them and AutoCAD's own files carry them: a block of 255 bytes holds data and parity, the parity being the remainder of the data, taken as a polynomial with its first byte the highest term, divided by the generator whose roots are consecutive powers of 2 of a field of 256 elements. The file header and the page maps use (255, 239), 239 data bytes and 16 of parity, in the field made by x^8 + x^6 + x^5 + x^3 + 1 with the roots 2^239 to 2^254; the data pages use (255, 251), 251 data bytes and 4 of parity, in the field of x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1 with the roots 2^251 to 2^254. Both were found by taking the blocks of AutoCAD's files and testing which field and which roots make them codewords. The reader does not use the parity ( takes the data bytes out and lets the CRCs say whether they are whole); AutoCAD may, so the writer lays it down right.

member.summary: The code of the file header and the page maps: 239 data bytes and 16 of parity in a block of 255.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgReedSolomon.Of251
member.summary: The code of the data pages: 251 data bytes and 4 of parity in a block of 255.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgReedSolomon._times
member.summary: For each term of the generator below the first, the product of the term with each byte: one run of 256 per term.

member.summary: Codes as blocks of 255 bytes laid out one byte of each block after the other (byte i of block j at i * blocks + j), as the file header, the page maps and the pages of the sections of coding 4 are. The data goes into the blocks in turn, 239 or 251 bytes to each, and what lacks of the last block is zero; the data must fit the blocks.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgSat
member.summary: The SAT of R2000, ACIS 4.00, turned into the ASM records of R2004 and back. Of the same body, AutoCAD 2021 writes R2000's text with no asmheader (so every pointer stands one lower), with no history on a record (a whole number of -1 and a pointer after the first value of the ASM record, the whole number alone on an attribute and on a transform), with no parameters and no convexity on an edge, with a text as its length and the word (13 text, not @13 text), with no fourth enum on the name attribute of a loft, and with no full before the spline of an exact curve or surface; every other value is the same. Going up, the parameters of an edge are worked out from its vertices and its curve (a line's from its root along its direction, an ellipse's as the angle of the vertex from the major axis, a spline's from its first and last knot where its ends are the vertices), the way AutoCAD 2021 does as it reads such a file; the convexity is unknown, the only word R2000 can give it.

The ACIS data of a REGION, 3DSOLID or BODY of a DWG of R2004 to R2010, which AutoCAD keeps as SAB, binary, and writes in DXF as SAT, text: the SAB turned into the SAT AutoCAD writes of it, line for line. SAB gives each value a tag of its kind (a whole number, a real, a position, a reference, a word of the record's own), where SAT gives the words of a flag (forward or reversed, I or F before a bound) and breaks the data of a spline over lines; which word a flag takes and where a line ends depend on the record and on the subtype a spline holds, and the grammars below give them for the records and subtypes AutoCAD writes for its solids, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them in DXF of R2004, R2007 and R2010. A value the grammars do not place, or a record or subtype they do not know, refuses the data, so that no SAT is written that is not AutoCAD's.
member.remarks: A real is written to 19 significant digits, the shortest of them, as C's %.19g does: 25.4 is 25.39999999999999858 and 1E-6 is 9.999999999999999547e-07; -0 keeps its sign. The normal of a plane, an ellipse, a cone and a torus is divided by its length first, as AutoCAD writes it. The head gives the version, the count of records, the count of bodies and the flags of the SAB, the count followed by spaces to a width of 12; then the product and the ACIS version, each by its length, and an empty date, as AutoCAD writes it; then the unit and the two tolerances of the SAB.
member.summary: The other way: the SAT of a body read back into the SAB it came from. A SAT value says what it is no better than its look does (0 is a whole number or a real, a vector is three numbers), so the records are read by the grammars of turned round, and the records whose values the grammars leave to "*" (the transform, the edges and the tolerant ones, the point, the name attribute) by a layout of their own that gives each value its kind. A record, a subtype or a value that fits no grammar refuses the data, so that no SAB is written that is not AutoCAD's. The SAT of R2000, ACIS 4.00, is read as the records of R2004 (DwgSat.Acis4.cs) and written from them.

The number of a vertex that has none is that of the end it stands at, 0 at the start of its edge and 1 at the end of it, which AutoCAD writes for most; a vertex of a closed edge has 0, where AutoCAD gives 2 to the seam of a swept surface. ACIS 4.00 comes in as the records of R2004 (its vertices numbered 2 from R2007) and goes out as them less the header, the history and what is left of the edges (Lower). False where the version is one whose records are not known.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgSummaryInfo
member.summary: The section AcDb:SummaryInfo of a DWG of R2004 or later, where AutoCAD keeps the properties of the drawing that DWGPROPS shows, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it (read from the files it saved of R2004, R2007, R2010, R2013 and R2018, the same in all but the letters). Eight texts, each a count of characters with the end mark, then the characters and the end mark: UTF-16 in R2007 and later, the bytes of the drawing's code page in R2004. They are the title, subject, author, keywords, comments, who saved it last, the revision and the base of the hyperlinks. Then the time spent editing as two whole numbers (days, milliseconds), the date it was made and the date it was saved, each a Julian day number and the milliseconds of that day in universal time, a count of custom properties (16 bits), each a name and a value as texts, and two whole numbers of nought. A drawing of R2000 has no such section: its properties are the DWGPROPS record among its objects.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTranscoder.NumberPaperSpaces
member.summary: Names the blocks a DWG keeps without their number the way DXF does. A DWG calls the block of every layout *Paper_Space; DXF keeps that name for the layout that is current and numbers the others from *Paper_Space0 in the order of the block table. An anonymous block is kept as *D or *U, and DXF numbers them from 1 in the same order: *D1, *D2.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTranscoder.NumberViewports
member.summary: Gives the viewports of the current layout the number (group 69) and status (68) AutoCAD writes, which a DWG does not hold. From R2004 a layout lists its viewports, the one showing the paper first, and they are numbered from 1 in that order. An R2000 layout lists none: the viewport that shows the paper itself (its view centre and height its own) is number 1 and the others follow in the order of their handles. The status is 0 for a viewport that is off, else its number from R2004 and -1 in R2000. The viewports of the other layouts are 0 and 0.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTranscoder.LeaveOutIncompleteGraphs
member.summary: Leaves out what a dynamic block keeps whole or not at all: an evaluation graph that names an expression not read (a constraint parameter whose dependency is not read is no expression), a network that names an action not read, a parameter that points to a variable or dependency not read, and each object of the network (variable, dependency, group, body) whose owner is not read. A graph that names an expression the drawing lacks is no graph, and AutoCAD drops its nodes; one that leans on a network with a hole in it would lose its constraints and be refused. The block stays an ordinary one.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgTranscoder.RenderPlan
member.summary: The entities of a section written on several threads. The walk over the blocks, on the calling thread, decides which entities are written, in what order and under which owner, a handful of table lookups an entity, and hands them on in runs of as it goes; the other threads write the records of a run into a buffer of its own, and the buffers are put in the DXF in the order of the runs, so the bytes are those of one thread writing the entities as the walk met them. The runs and the buffers are used again as they are done, so that a section of 300 000 entities makes some ten of each and not three hundred, where a collector of a drawing's 300 000 objects would take the added memory for a reason to collect.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dwg.DwgWriter
member.summary: Writes a drawing as a DWG file, the mirror of : a with every record it holds, or a as the drawing makes of its shapes.

remarks.para: The drawing is written as its DXF, and each record of that DXF is encoded into the object of the DWG that says the same, with the handles of the drawing: the header variables, the classes, the nine tables, the blocks, the entities and the objects. Written are the tables and their records, the blocks, LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, SPLINE, RAY, XLINE, LWPOLYLINE, the 2D and 3D POLYLINE with their vertices, the polygon and polyface mesh, TEXT, MTEXT, ATTDEF, INSERT, alone or as an array, with its ATTRIBs, of one line or of several, SOLID, TRACE, 3DFACE, DIMENSION, VIEWPORT, HATCH, LEADER, MULTILEADER, TOLERANCE, MLINE, OLE2FRAME, IMAGE, WIPEOUT, ACAD_TABLE, and REGION, 3DSOLID and BODY with their ACIS data in the data store of the file, and of the objects DICTIONARY, XRECORD, LAYOUT, GROUP, MLINESTYLE, MLEADERSTYLE, TABLESTYLE, DBCOLOR, IMAGEDEF, RASTERVARIABLES, WIPEOUTVARIABLES, MATERIAL, VISUALSTYLE (in the form of each version), the detail and section view styles, the manager of the persistent names of subentities beside solids, the TABLECONTENT and TABLEGEOMETRY a table keeps for a round trip, the data of a dynamic block of a linear parameter and a stretch action (from AutoCAD 2007; a block whose graph holds another expression is written without it), and the small ones a new drawing holds, so that a new drawing is written whole. A table goes in the form of R2010: its cells, their overrides and borders, merged ranges, sizes and style from the groups DXF keeps of R2007, the cell styles of its rows, columns and whole from the TABLECONTENT it keeps for a round trip or else from its own overrides (93 to 96), and its table style's cell styles from the style's rows, then those of its own (101 on) from the CELLSTYLEMAP AutoCAD writes in DXF alone; that map, and the extension dictionary of the table style that holds it, are not written from R2010, as AutoCAD writes no such object there (a file before it holds them). A REGION, 3DSOLID or BODY is written with its ACIS data in the data store of the file: where the section ACDSDATA holds its SAB, as a DXF of R2013 and later gives it, and where it holds SAT text, as a DXF of R2004 to R2010 gives it, turned into the SAB AutoCAD 2021 writes for R2018 and named by a GUID, the one its extended data kept (else one made of its handle, so that the same drawing gives the same bytes); the 11 solids and 3 regions of a drawing of AutoCAD 2004, 2007 and 2010 written so open in AutoCAD 2021 with AUDIT finding 0 errors and the volumes and areas of the DXF. The ACIS 4.00 text of R2000 and a SAT with a record the grammars do not place are left out. The section THUMBNAILIMAGE of the DXF (a bitmap of Windows without its file header, or a PNG file) is written as the preview of the DWG, the picture of the file in Explorer and in the Open dialog. A SHAPE is written where its DXF gives its number (group 70, or a number as its name), of the first text style of a file of shapes; one given by its name alone is left out. The FIELD and FIELDLIST of fields, the SORTENTSTABLE of the draw order of a block and the DATALINK of a table linked to data are written as AutoCAD writes them, with their class listed where the DXF lists none, as a drawing made in code does. A record of another type, and a record that has no handle, which a DWG cannot name, is left out, every handle to it written as 0 and every dictionary entry naming it dropped, and one Warn line of counts them by type.

The file is of AC1032 (AutoCAD 2018 and later), the form AutoCAD 2021 saves in, unless a version is given: AC1027 (AutoCAD 2013), AC1024 (2010) or AC1018 (2004) are written too, a drawing of a later version made first into the DXF of the version, as would give it, and what the version cannot hold left out or replaced as it is there (the objects of R2007 and later that a file of R2004 keeps as AutoCAD keeps them: the multileaders with the version they were made by, the texts of their graphics in 8 bits, the fields in the form of before R2007). AC1015 (2000) is written too (the file of sections in sequence AutoCAD 2000 has), and AC1021 (2007), a container of its own, a file header and pages coded by Reed-Solomon. The same bytes come of the same drawing every time.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.AcisBoolean
member.summary: The union, difference and intersection of planar bodies (regions in one plane), keeping arcs and ellipses as arcs and ellipses where it can.

remarks.para: The library's booleans () know straight edges only. Each curve is cut into chords first, a circle on a grid of angles that depends on its radius alone, so that two regions sharing an arc of one circle cut it alike and leave no sliver between them; the booleans are run on the chords; then every edge of the answer is traced back to the chord, and so the curve, it lies on. A run of edges on one curve is one line, arc or ellipse again, its ends the exact meeting of the two curves it lies between (found by Newton's method from the point the booleans gave) or the end of an input curve where it is within the point tolerance of one. A whole circle or ellipse that no cut touched stays one edge.
An edge that lies on no chord (the booleans moved a point further than the tolerance) is kept straight.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfBlockParameterValueSet
member.summary: The values a distance or an angle of a dynamic block's parameter may take, as AutoCAD's Block Editor sets them in its Value Set: from a minimum to a maximum in steps of an increment, or one of a list. A parameter given none takes any value. An angle's set is in radians, within a turn: Increments(0, 2 * Math.PI, Math.PI / 12) lets an angle of 0, 15, 30 ... 360 degrees.
member.remarks: AutoCAD keeps the set in the parameter's flags (96): 1 a minimum, 2 a maximum, 4 an increment, 8 a list. An increment set is written with the flags 7, a list with 8, as AutoCAD 2021 read them (plugin v17): of the set from 50 to 300 by 10, a Width set to 75 became 70, 77 became 80 and 400 became 300; of the list 50, 100 ... 300, 75 and 77 became 100 and 400 became 300. Only a list is given back by , as AutoCAD gives back only a list. A set is given to a linear parameter, to either distance of an XY parameter, to the angle of a rotation parameter, and to the distance and the angle of a polar parameter; an angle's is taken round the circle, as AutoCAD 2021 took it (plugin D25): of the steps of 15 degrees from 0 to 90, 300 degrees became 0 and 200 became 90.

member.summary: Makes a set of the distances from a minimum to a maximum in steps of an increment, as AutoCAD's Value Set of the type Increment: Increments(50, 300, 10) lets a Width of 50, 60 ... 300, a value between steps going to the nearest step and one beyond an end to that end.
member.param: The least distance, nought or more.
The greatest distance, above the minimum.
The step from the minimum, above nought.
member.returns: The set.
member.exception: Thrown when a number is not finite, the minimum is below nought, the maximum is not above the minimum, or the increment is not above nought.

An angle's list may hold nought: List(new[] { 0.0, Math.PI / 2, Math.PI }) lets an arrow point along x, along y or back.
member.param: The distances or the angles, each nought or more.

member.exception: Thrown when the values are null.
Thrown when there are none.
Thrown when a value is not a finite number of nought or more.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfBlockTable
member.summary: The block table of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's BlockTable: model space, paper space and every block, each a , in the order of the file, found by name and added to.

remarks.para: db.BlockTable.Add(new DxfBlockTableRecord { Name = "BOLT", Origin = new GeoPoint3(1, 2, 0) }) adds the block BOLT drawn about (1, 2, 0), empty until entities are appended to it. In a file of R13 or later the table is its BLOCK_RECORD table, each record with its BLOCK; in one of R12 it is the blocks of the BLOCKS section, model space and paper space among them where the file has them as blocks and first where it does not.

A block named *D, *U or *T is added as AutoCAD's BlockTable.Add adds one so named: an anonymous block (, flag 1 of its BLOCK's group 70), named by the table with the first number from 1 up that no block of the drawing and no INSERT, dimension or table names. A drawing with no dimension given var picture = new DxfBlockTableRecord { Name = "*D" } names it *D1, the next *D2; one whose dimensions ezdxf drew as *D1 to *D11 names it *D12. Its lines and texts are appended to it as to any block, and it is the of a dimension made in code, so that the dimension is drawn before AutoCAD draws it anew.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfBlockTableRecord
member.summary: A block of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's BlockTableRecord: model space, paper space or a block; its name, its origin, what kind it is, and its entities, enumerated, appended to and erased.

remarks.para: db.ModelSpace.AppendEntity(new DxfLine(a, b)) adds a line to model space: its record is written at the end of the ENTITIES section, a block's before its ENDBLK, in the file's own style, with a handle of its own above every handle of the file and the block as its owner, as AutoCAD writes one. An entity is erased by its own .

The entities are enumerated in the order of the file, those appended after them, each the same object every time; a POLYLINE is one entity with its vertices and an INSERT one with its attributes, as AutoCAD keeps them together. An enumeration walks the entities the block holds when it begins: those erased on the way are passed over, those appended on the way are not reached, and nothing throws, so a loop may erase or append as it goes.
