Where the drawing's finds the SHX or TrueType font of the text's style, a text justified other than left on its baseline is put where its words stand about its , as AutoCAD 2021's AdjustAlignment puts it (check F1a), whenever its words, second point, height, width factor, turn, justification or style are set, and when one made in code is added to the drawing: "ABC" of txt.shx 4 high centred on (100, 50, 0) stands at (94.667, 50, 0), the ink of its letters 10.667 wide; an aligned text takes the height, and a fitted one the width factor, its two points give it, "ABC" aligned on two points 30 apart 11.25 high. A first point set on a text of another justification is kept as set. A TrueType font is measured as AutoCAD 2021 measures it (check F2): the box from the start of the baseline to the last pen, the ink past it counted, "ABC" of arial.ttf so centred on (100, 50, 0) at (94.259, 50, 0). A text held by a second point is turned over with its first point (10) worked out from that point as works it out, and both points carried, as AutoCAD 2021 carries them (probed on 196 texts, 14 modes, in 4 planes at 3 angles, under 7 mirrors): those held by the left, the centre or the right of their ink at the baseline, the bottom, the middle or the top (72 of 0 to 2, 73 of 1 to 3, and 1 with 73 of nought) as one aligned left on its baseline is, "ABC" centred on (30, 45), its first point (26, 45), across x = 40 standing at (45.555, 45) held at (49.555, 45); and those whose two points are the ends of their baseline (72 of 3 and 5, and 2 with 73 of nought) across the middle of those two points, so that the first point is the second mirrored and the second the first, the ink not asked: "ABC" aligned on (20, 40) and (40, 48) across x = 40 runs from (60, 40) to (40, 48), reading from the first to the second as it did. A text held by its middle (72 of 4), where it is turned across its upright, is mirrored as it stands, each point carried as the mirror carries it, so that its second point is the middle of its words again and its first, which AutoCAD leaves where the mirror takes it, is given back in ; across its baseline it is turned over like the others. member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfDimension
member.summary: A dimension of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Dimension: the points it measures between, the text it writes, the style it is drawn in and the variables of that style it overrides; each kind a class of its own, a for a linear one, a for a radius.

remarks.para: The points are in world coordinates, as AutoCAD gives them, though the file writes some in the system of the dimension's (the text's place, group 11, and the place of its block, 12). The rotated dimension of 100 from (0, 0, 0) to (100, 0, 0), its dimension line 20 above, has (0, 0, 0), (100, 0, 0), on the line 20 above and a of 100, worked out from the points as AutoCAD works it out.

What a dimension is drawn with, its lines, arrowheads and text, is the anonymous block (*D7) that AutoCAD drew for it, placed at . The library does not draw a dimension: a point, a text or a variable set is written into the record, and the block is left as it was drawn, to be drawn anew by AutoCAD when it next draws the dimension, as its RecomputeDimensionBlock would; until then AutoCAD shows the old picture. moves the points as ezdxf's transform() moves them, and the picture with them where AutoCAD gives the block to this dimension alone (flag 32 of group 70) and places it at no point of its own (no group 12): the block's entities moved by the same transformation, so that the dimension is drawn where it now stands.

A variable of the style, as , reads as the dimension draws with it: its own where it overrides the style (its extended data of ACAD, the list DSTYLE of a 1070 naming the variable's group and its value), else its style's, else AutoCAD's own. Set, it is written as an override, as AutoCAD's DIMOVERRIDE writes one; the style is left as it is. A block, linetype or text style set on a dimension of a drawing is one of that drawing; one set on a dimension in no drawing yet is held as the record it is, and taken to the record of its name in the drawing it is added to, as AutoCAD's deep clone maps one, the dimension refused where that drawing has none of that name. A copy added to another drawing keeps its overrides that point at a record, those it read and those set on it, each taken to the record of the same name there, which the drawing is given where it has none, as AutoCAD's deep clone between drawings does. An override of a variable a drawing of an older version has not is left out when the dimension is added to it, as AutoCAD's SAVEAS to that version leaves it out: DIMLTYPE and DIMFXLEN, which R2007 brought, in a drawing of R2000.

A dimension made in code, new DxfRotatedDimension(0, p1, p2, onLine, "", null), is drawn by no block until it is given one: , a block of the drawing it is added to, is needed before takes it. Its picture is a block named *D added to the drawing, which the block table names as AutoCAD names it, *D1 the first, and marks anonymous, with the lines and the text appended to it: var picture = new DxfBlockTableRecord { Name = "*D" }; db.BlockTable.Add(picture);, then a line and an MTEXT appended to picture and the dimension given DimBlock = picture, saved and read back as AutoCAD writes its own, the BLOCK *D1 of flag 1. A copy added to another drawing brings a copy of its block where AutoCAD names the block itself (*D1), and needs one of the same name there where it does not. A copy added to the drawing it came from shares its original's block, and loses flag 32, so that moving the one leaves the other's picture where it is; one made in code is written with it once given an anonymous block. A copy of a dimension that names no block, as the dimensions of the constraints of AutoCAD's Parking sample name none in the block and in its anonymous copies, names none, so that an INSERT of such a dynamic block is set.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfDimension.SetDimstyleData(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfDimStyleTableRecord)
member.summary: Gives the dimension the variables of a record, as AutoCAD's SetDimstyleData: each that differs from what the dimension reads written as an override, as its setter writes one; those the dimension reads already change nothing. A variable its file's version has not is passed over where the record holds AutoCAD's own value of it, and refused where it holds another; a record that names no text style leaves the dimension's as it is. A whole number is checked against AutoCAD's range as checks it, a Dimdec of 9 refused, and a size of the arrows, the text or the scale below nought. Every value is checked before any is written.
member.param: The record: of a table, or made in code, as gives one.
member.exception: Thrown when the record is null, or holds a null text or colour.
Thrown when a value of the record is one AutoCAD does not take.
Thrown when a block, linetype or text style of the record is of another drawing.
Thrown when the dimension is erased, or the record holds a value other than AutoCAD's own of a variable the dimension's file is too old to hold.

The value is taken to the parameter's value set, then the block worked out at the values of all its properties, the copy written as AutoCAD writes it, and the value read back. A Width of the rectangle 100 by 50 set to 200 moves the right edge to x = 200 in the copy, as AutoCAD 2021 moved it; a Mark set to Tick shows the tick and hides the cross; an Angle set to Math.PI / 2 turns the entities of its rotate action a quarter turn about its base point.

The actions are worked out in the order they were added: stretches in a row are summed point by point (a line's ends, a polyline's vertices; an arc held by one end has that end moved and keeps the height of its middle off its chord, as AutoCAD 2021 kept it; an arc held by both ends, a circle, a text, a multiline text or an INSERT held moves whole), a move moves its entities whole by the change of the point it follows (the end point of a linear or an XY parameter, the position of a point parameter), each times its distance multiplier and turned by its angle offset; a scale scales them alike about the base point of its linear parameter by the distance over the block's own, a rotate turns them about the base point of its rotation parameter by the angle less the block's own, and a flip mirrors them about its reflection line while the state is 1. A polar stretch turns its entities about the base point of its polar parameter by the angle less the block's own, and moves the points it holds in its frame besides along the parameter's line by the distance less the block's own, as AutoCAD 2021 drew it (plugin D25): a pointer from (0, 0) to (100, 0) held by its tip, set to 150 and a quarter turn, runs to (0, 150), and an entity it turns only turns alone; an entity of one point held, an arc held by both ends and an entity its selection names holding no point turn and move whole. Then each array copies its entities, as many as its spacing goes whole into the distance, one at least: a Length of 250 of a post every 60 shows four posts; an array of an XY parameter copies in rows and columns, and nothing where either count is nought, as AutoCAD 2021 drew it (plugin v21). A move listing its own parameter's grip among what it moves, as AutoCAD's point sample does, moves its entities alone. A stretch or a move following a parameter's base point (BaseXDelta and BaseYDelta, tied to its base grip) moves nothing, as a value set moves the end point only. A move holding another linear parameter carries it, as AutoCAD's Block Editor writes such a move (the parameters' node ids after the count 70 of its head): the parameter's base point and end point move by the move, its grips with them, its distance kept, and its own actions do not follow its being carried (it chains none); a frame whose Depth of 60 from (40, 60) down to (40, 0) is set to 100 carries Bottom from (0, 0)-(100, 0) to (0, -40)-(100, -40), still 100, and keeps it there when Bottom is set next. An attribute definition a move holds moves in the copy, and each ATTRIB of the INSERT of its tag moves by the change of that move, carried by the INSERT's placing, keeping a place the user gave it: Mark X set from 20 to 30 on an INSERT turned a quarter turn at the scale 2 moves the ATTRIB 20 along y in the world. A lookup set to a row's label sets the properties of its input columns to the row's values; any property set, the lookup set too, each lookup reads the label of the first row of the values then, or its label of no match, Custom as the library writes it: set to a row of the values of a row above it, it reads that row's label, as AutoCAD 2021 read Small after Twin was set, a row of Small's values further down (plugin D25b).

A distance or a position is a number (a , or a whole number taken as one); a linear distance is taken, as AutoCAD 2021 took it (plugins v17 to v20), to the nearest step of an increment set, a tie between two steps to the step below (85 to 80 and 95 to 90 of 50 to 300 by 10 for an own 100), and then into the minimum and the maximum (400 to 300); to the nearest of a list, a tie to the block's own value where it is one of the two, else to the one written first, the lesser of a list written from the least up, whatever the value the property had: of 50, 100 ... 300, 75 and 125 go to 100 and 175 to 150 for an own 100, 125 to 100 and 225 to 250 for an own 250, as AutoCAD 2021 took all 358 ties of lists of 3 to 6 values of a linear, an XY and a polar parameter, from every value before and in two sessions alike (plugin D25b); and is kept as given where the parameter has no set. A distance of an XY or a polar parameter is taken so too. A distance or a position of an INSERT scaled by 2 is twice the block's, as it is read. A distance of an XY or a polar parameter is above the point tolerance. An angle is a number of radians, taken into a turn, from nought up to 2 pi, and to the value set of a rotation or a polar parameter round the circle, as AutoCAD 2021 took it (plugin D25): to the nearest of a list, 338 degrees to 0 of 0, 90, 180 and 270; outside a minimum and a maximum to the one nearer round the circle, 300 degrees to 0 of 0 to 90; within them to the nearest step of an increment, 40 to 45 of steps of 15. A tie goes to the value behind the angle asked, clockwise, 22.5 degrees to 15 and 315 to 270: AutoCAD's own choice followed its rounding, the step behind in 26 of 58 ties of steps of 15 degrees, and the value behind in 23 of 32 of the list above, 135 degrees going to 180 each time. A flip state is a whole number, 0 or 1, and reads back as a . A visibility state is one of the parameter's, by its name, letters of either case the same, and reads back as the parameter names it; so is a lookup's label, one of a row of its table, a label given exactly first, else trimmed, and reads back as the table holds it, a space after it kept, as AutoCAD 2021 read "Size 6 " of its lookup sample (plugin v21).

A block properties table (Block Table1) is set to the index of a row, a whole number, as AutoCAD 2021 set it (plugin D26): each parameter's column takes the row's value, in the block's units (twice it on an INSERT scaled by 2), an angle taken into a turn; each user parameter's column its value; the INSERT's attribute of each attribute definition's column its text, the plate's MARK P200 for the row 1; an empty cell leaves its column as it is. It reads back the index of the first row of the values then. A user parameter of text is set to a string, one of a real to a number. Any other property set leaving no row matched gives each user parameter of a column its value of no match, as AutoCAD read Spaces Custom once Width was set off the rows of its Parking sample; a user parameter set keeps the value given.

A horizontal, a vertical or a radial constraint parameter is set by solving the block's geometric and dimensional constraints, kept in the associative network of its BLOCK_RECORD, as AutoCAD 2021 solved its Dynamic Blocks samples (plugins D27, D27b): the distance taken to its value set and to twelve significant digits, as AutoCAD solved Height 612.3456789012345 at 612.345678901, the variable of the dimensional constraint it drives given it, the variables of expressions of it worked out (numbers, names, + - * / ^, brackets and the functions sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sqrt, abs and round, angles in degrees), and the lines, arcs, circles, polyline edges and construction lines the constraints hold moved from the block's own by Newton's method, each step the least that meets the constraints, before any action works on them. Geometry the constraints leave free keeps the base point of each constraint parameter set where it is along its distance, as AutoCAD kept the left side of its Door Elevation, fixed nowhere, at a new Width; what is still free is held where the block has it, the radii and the arcs' ends before the rest where all at once cannot be met, as AutoCAD kept the fillets of its Hex Head Bolt whole at a new HdCr. Of AutoCAD's Fluorescent, Door Elevation, Window, Channel, Concrete Pipe, Hex Head Bolt, WF Beam and I Beam samples, metric and imperial, 77 of the 79 values the library set came out within 3E-12 of AutoCAD's, one of an I Beam whose own geometry is 7E-6 off its constraints 1.5E-6 off, and one of Fluorescent at Width 800 apart, AutoCAD having taken its table's row back: Width 1 200 of Fluorescent's rectangle 1 000 by 500, its corner fixed, moves its right side to x = 1 200. A table whose properties must match a row leaves a constraint parameter at the value set and the others at theirs, no row matched, as AutoCAD set Fluorescent's Width; a row that would change a constraint parameter is refused, as AutoCAD left the constraints as they were at a row of its Hex Head Bolt. A constraint parameter of no column of the table leaves its user parameters as they are, as AutoCAD kept Hex Head Bolt's Size 1 at Length 80. A flip carrying a constraint parameter mirrors its points too, as AutoCAD's Window sample's flip carries DoorWidth. The anonymous block is given a copy of the block's associative network at the values set, as AutoCAD gives its own, the dimensions of the constraints moved to the geometry and showing their values: AutoCAD 2021 set such an INSERT again from it as from its own, 15 values of 7 samples within 1E-12 of its own sets, where it set none again whose anonymous block held no copy, or one naming entities gone (eKeyNotFound).

The INSERT is made to place an anonymous block of AutoCAD's (*U1 and on, flagged anonymous) holding a copy of each entity of the dynamic block: moved, stretched, scaled, turned or mirrored by the actions, a governed entity shown or hidden by the state; the block's extended data AcDbBlockRepBTag names the dynamic block, and each copy keeps its source's tag with its own handle. The anonymous block the INSERT places already is filled anew where no other INSERT places it, else a new one is made, as AutoCAD 2021 made *U2 for a second INSERT whose value it set (plugin v17). The INSERT's extension dictionary is given AcDbBlockRepresentation, with the representation data naming the dynamic block and, in AppDataCache, the record of each parameter and action AutoCAD reads the values from (ACAD_ENHANCEDBLOCKDATA); a history of grip edits it kept (ACAD_ENHANCEDBLOCKHISTORY) is kept, the node's id, the property's name and its value read back added after it, as AutoCAD 2021 added Block Table1 2, Spaces 5 Spaces and Width 5400 to its Parking sample's (plugin D26), the same property set twice in a row keeping the last value alone, as AutoCAD 2021 kept Width 120 of Width 140 and then 120 (plugin GhDy3a); an INSERT of no history is given none, as AutoCAD gave none to the library's INSERTs it set, unless its block has a polar parameter or an array or a scale action: AutoCAD 2021 started the history at the first value set of a pointer, a panel with an array and a bar scaled (plugin GhDb4a); a distance is kept in the block's own units (Width 150 of Width 300 at the scale 2). The INSERT keeps its place, scale, attributes and look; the dynamic block is not changed.

The Origin of a linear, an XY or a polar parameter is set to a point in the coordinates of the file, as AutoCAD 2021 sets it (plugin GhDb4a): the point is taken into the block's coordinates (the Origin of an INSERT at (1 000, 500), not turned or scaled, set to (1 030, 520, 0) reads (30, 20, 0), and on one at a quarter turn and the scale 2 reads (10, -15, 0)), and the parameter's base point and end point move together to it, the distances kept: a panel 100 wide from (0, 100) whose Origin is set to (30, 120) runs from (30, 120) to (130, 120), and the edges the stretches of its base point and its end point hold move by (30, 20), the base point's off the line too; the lines of a pointer's polar stretch stay, as it measures the end point from the base point. The set is a record of the INSERT's history in a block that keeps one (the node, Origin and the point), replacing an earlier record of the same Origin. The Origin of a rotation or a constraint parameter is read only.

member.exception: Thrown when the value set is null.

Thrown when the value set is not a finite number for a distance, a position or an angle, not a point for an Origin, not a whole number for a flip state or a block properties table, not the name of a state of a visibility parameter, not the label of a row of a lookup's table, or not a string for a user parameter of text.

Thrown when a distance, taken to the value set, is not above the point tolerance of , a flip state is neither 0 nor 1, or a row is not one of the block properties table's, as AutoCAD 2021 refused -1 and the row after the last (eInvalidInput).
Thrown when the property is read only, or its INSERT is erased, in no drawing, or scaled unlike along its axes, which AutoCAD does not take as a dynamic block's.

Thrown when the block holds a parameter or an action of a kind the library does not work out (an aligned constraint parameter), constraints it does not solve (a constraint of a kind other than a coincidence, a point on a curve, parallel, perpendicular, horizontal, colinear, tangent, a middle, a centre, fixed, equal lengths or radii, a distance along x or y, an angle of two lines or of three points and a radius; geometry other than lines, arcs, circles and construction lines flat in the block, or an expression of another function), constraints that cannot be met at the value set, a block properties table's row that would change a constraint parameter, or an action it does not work out: a stretch of an entity other than those above or of a tilted arc by one end, a stretch, a scale, a rotate, a flip or an array holding other parameters, a move holding grips of a parameter it does not carry, a move carrying a parameter other than a linear one, or one that chains its actions or that a scale or an array follows, attribute definitions of one tag moved apart where the INSERT has an ATTRIB of that tag, an attribute definition worked on by an action other than a move, a scale or a rotate about another point than its parameter's base point, a polar stretch tied to its parameter's base point, of a distance multiplier other than 1 or an angle offset other than nought, or holding an arc by one end, an entity both flipped and moved by other actions, an entity both turned or scaled and stretched or moved, as AutoCAD 2021 worked such an entity out from the INSERT's last state (plugin v21), an entity both copied by an array or turned by a polar stretch and worked on by another action, a lookup table of columns other than a linear or a polar parameter's distance, a point parameter's x and y, an XY parameter's distances, a polar or a rotation parameter's angle and lookups, a block properties table of columns other than those or of user parameters, the visibility state and attribute definitions, a lookup or a user parameter of a block whose table its properties must match (290 of 1), or a parameter of such a table of a column of a user parameter or of the visibility state, a user parameter of another kind than a text or a real, or of an expression; or when the INSERT keeps the base point of a rotation or a flip parameter away from the block's own, or that of a linear, an XY or a polar parameter a move carries or a scale or a rotate follows, beyond the point tolerance of . A base point a grip moved on a linear, an XY or a polar parameter is worked out from where the INSERT keeps it, as AutoCAD does (), and a grip edit of a polar parameter from the history of the INSERT's edits where the distance or the angle was set. Nothing is written then.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.MoveBasePoint(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoVector3)
member.summary: Moves the base point of the linear, XY or polar parameter this property is a distance of, as a grip of AutoCAD's moves it: the end point stays, the INSERT keeps the base point where it was moved to, and the block is worked out from there, as with . A plate 100 by 50 of an XY parameter from (0, 0) to (100, 50), its right and top edges stretched by the end point, whose base point is moved by (20, 0) reads Width 80 and keeps its right edge at x 100, as AutoCAD 2021 read the plate whose corner of base x and end y was dragged by (20, 10), the top edge going up by 10 with the end point's y (plugin GhDy2a); a stretch or a move tied to the base point (BaseXDelta, BaseYDelta) moves its points by the move, and an array starts where the base point is, as AutoCAD drew the array of its XY sample's INSERT whose base point a grip took from (0, 5) to (0, 104.30). Moves add up: moving by (20, 0) and then by (5, 0) keeps the base point 25 along x. The distances the move leaves are taken to the parameter's value set and the base point stands where they put it, the end point staying, as AutoCAD 2021 read Width 70 and the base point 30 where a panel of Width 50 to 300 by 10 had its base grip dragged by 33, and Width 50 and 50 by 60 (plugin GhDy3a); an axis of an XY parameter the move leaves alone is not taken. The base point of a polar parameter is moved anywhere: a pointer from (0, 0) to (100, 0) whose base point is moved by (30, 10) reads Length 81.39 and Angle 354.3 degrees, its lines stay (the end point stays), and the INSERT's history gets the record GRIPLOC of the parameter's base grip, (30, 10, 0), as AutoCAD 2021 wrote it; a polar stretch worked out after it turns the lines about the new base point, and after an end grip dragged before it works the edits out one after the other, as AutoCAD did (the end grip to (0, 50), the base grip by 30 and the end grip to (35, 0) leave the first line from (45.43, 25.72) to (35, 0), plugin GhDb4a). The history keeps the move of the base grip of a linear or an XY parameter too, in a block that keeps one (a polar parameter, an array or a scale action), and a stretch or an array that follows the base point stays where it stands at the next value set. A move of no more than 1E-12, or one a second move brings back, leaves no record.
member.param: The move, in the coordinates of the file (the world's, as is given): an XY parameter's along x and along y of the block, a linear parameter's along its line alone, the part across it left out, a polar parameter's anywhere in the plane.
member.exception: Thrown when the property is not a distance of a linear, an XY or a polar parameter.
Thrown when a distance of the parameter would not be above the point tolerance of once the base point is moved and the distances taken to the value set.

A pointer of two lines from (0, 0) to (100, 0), at (1 000, 500), whose end grip is dragged to (1 000, 550) reads Length 50 and Angle 90 degrees, runs its line to (0, 50) and keeps GRIPLOC (-100, 50, 0); dragged to (1 010, 500) next it keeps the one record, (-90, 0, 0), the two moves added, unless another record came between (plugin GhDy3a). The end grip of a linear parameter takes the distance along its line from the base point, that of an XY parameter each distance along its axis, each taken to its value set, and the history keeps the same GRIPLOC of the grip in a block that keeps one (plugin GhDb4a). remarks.para: The ellipse about (0, 0, 0) with the major axis (10, 0, 0) and the ratio 0.5 is 10, 5 and 157.08, and runs through (0, 5, 0). Everything of it is in world coordinates, as the file holds it.

The angles AutoCAD calls and are another thing, those of the lines from the centre to the ends, from the major axis: on that ellipse the parameter pi / 4 is the point (7.071, 3.536, 0), at the angle 0.4636. A whole ellipse runs from 0 to 2 pi. Every other group of the record is kept as it was.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity
member.summary: An entity of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Entity is one of a drawing: what it is drawn on and with (its layer, colour, linetype, lineweight and whether it is shown), the block it is in, and its geometry as the library's shapes.

remarks.para: Each type of entity is a class of its own, named as AutoCAD names its own with Dxf in front: a LINE is a ; a type the library has no class for is a , kept as the file has it. An entity of a is changed by setting its properties: its record is written anew, every group the change is not about kept as it was, and a property given the value it has changes nothing.

An entity made in code, new DxfLine(start, end) { Layer = "steel", ColorIndex = 1 }, is added to a drawing by , which gives it its handle and owner: the same object is the entity of the drawing from then on.
The look is as AutoCAD reads it: an entity with no colour is 256, BYLAYER; with no linetype, ByLayer; with no lineweight, . Nothing is taken from a block: a LINE of a block on layer 0 is on layer 0.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.DxfName
member.summary: Gets the type of the entity as the file names it in its group 0, as AutoCAD's class names its DxfName: LINE, LWPOLYLINE, INSERT, DIMENSION, ACAD_TABLE, REGION.
member.value: The name the record is written under in the drawing's own version, which differs from one version to another where the kinds do: a 2D polyline of R2000 is an LWPOLYLINE, and the same drawing saved as R12 holds it as a POLYLINE. A class does not give one name: a , a , a and a are all POLYLINE, and every dimension class is DIMENSION. An entity made in code has the name its class is written under, before it is in a drawing.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.Layer
member.summary: Gets or sets the layer the entity is on (group 8), as AutoCAD's Layer: the name as the layer table names it, the spaces around it taken off and its escapes (\U+00E9) read as letters; 0 where the record gives none.
member.value: Set, the name of a layer. One the layer table does not list, letters of either case the same, is added to it in the colour 7 with the linetype CONTINUOUS, and the log says so; an entity made in code is given its layer when it is added to a drawing. The vertices and end of a POLYLINE follow it.
member.exception: Thrown when the name set is null.
Thrown when the name set is empty, has a space at either end, or has a control character or one of < > / " : ; ? * | = ` in it, which AutoCAD does not take in a name.
Thrown when the entity is erased.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.ColorIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the colour of the entity (group 62), as AutoCAD's ColorIndex: 1 to 255 for a colour of AutoCAD's index, 0 for BYBLOCK and 256 for BYLAYER, which an entity that gives none has.
member.value: Set, from 0 to 256. The vertices of a POLYLINE follow it, as AutoCAD keeps them, and so they do the linetype, lineweight, linetype scale, visibility, true colour and transparency; a face of a polyface mesh keeps a colour of its own.
member.exception: Thrown when the colour set is below 0 or above 256.
Thrown when the entity is erased.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.Color
member.summary: Gets or sets the colour of the entity, as AutoCAD's Color: its true colour (group 420, its book's name 430) where it has one, else its colour index (62), BYLAYER where it gives none. It agrees with and , which read the same groups; a true colour carries the index nearest it, as gives it: orange, 0xFF8000, the index 30, whatever index the record writes beside it.
member.value: Set, BYLAYER, BYBLOCK or a colour of the index writes the index and takes out a true colour and its name; a true colour writes its red, green and blue (420) and the index nearest it (62), as AutoCAD writes one, and takes out a name. A colour equal to the one read changes nothing.
member.exception: Thrown when the colour set is null.
Thrown when the colour set is by pen, the foreground, a layer's off or frozen, or none, which an entity of DXF does not hold.
Thrown when the entity is erased, or a true colour is set on one of a file older than R2004 (AC1018).

member.summary: Gets the entities the entity breaks into, as AutoCAD's Explode: new entities in no file. Any other entity refuses, as AutoCAD answers eNotApplicable for one that does not break, a LINE or a CIRCLE; and so do a HATCH filled solid or with a gradient, a MESH, and a REGION, a 3DSOLID and a BODY, which AutoCAD breaks with its solid modeler, each saying why.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.JoinEntity(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity)
member.summary: Joins another curve into the entity, as AutoCAD's JoinEntity does by the rules of its JOIN: the entity's record is written anew to run over both, its look and every group the joining is not about kept, and the other is left as it is, for the caller to erase. Ends meet within the point tolerance of , 0.001, measured in space.

remarks.para: What joins into what, as AutoCAD's JOIN says. A takes lines along its line, overlapping or with gaps between them, and runs from the lowest of all their ends to the highest in its own direction: the line from (0, 0, 0) to (10, 0, 0) joined to the one from (25, 0, 0) to (15, 0, 0) runs to (25, 0, 0). A takes arcs of its circle, gaps and all, counter-clockwise from its start: the quarter from 0 to pi / 2 joined to the arc from pi to 3 pi / 2 runs from 0 to 3 pi / 2, and to one that reaches back over its start, from that one's start; a takes elliptical arcs of its ellipse alike, by its parameter. An arc whose normal is the other way is the same arc run the other way. One that would make the whole circle or ellipse is refused, as AutoCAD's JOIN makes a CIRCLE of it, which an ARC is not. Where either end moves both are written, the start within a turn: an ellipse whose file gives the parameters -3 and -2 joined to its arc from 2 pi - 2 to 2 pi - 1.5 runs from 2 pi - 3 to 2 pi - 1.5. The gaps follow the JOIN command; that AutoCAD's JoinEntity fills them too is not confirmed.

A or a takes lines, arcs and polylines of the plane of its normal at its elevation, the whole of each arc within the tolerance of that plane, end to end at either of its ends, each turned to run on along it: an arc as a segment of its bulge, turned over where its normal is the other way, a polyline with its bulges and widths, a line or an arc of no width; the polyline (0, 0), (10, 0) joined to the arc of radius 5 about (10, 5) from -pi / 2 to pi / 2 is (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 10) with a bulge of 1 on its second vertex. A takes lines, 3D polylines and polylines of the plane with no arc, in any plane; a curved one is refused, as AutoCAD's JOIN makes a spline of a 3D polyline joined to a curve, which a POLYLINE does not become in place. A takes lines, arcs, elliptical arcs, polylines and splines, each as the spline that is exactly it (, a polyline fitted with a spline as the one of the vertices it is drawn through), all raised to the highest degree among them and joined with their knots run on one from the other, the spline's own kept (an arc run on by its angle, a polyline by 1 a segment and a line by 1, as AutoCAD 2021 ran them on a spline of knots 0 to 56.57); it is given by its control points from then on. Where the joined ends come back together the polyline or spline is closed, its last vertex the first: the polyline of one side of a square 10 by 10 joined to lines of the other three is closed, of area 100.

A closed curve is not joined, nor is a fitted polyline or a polyline of no vertices, and a piece of no length at an end is joined and adds nothing. A piece that would run back over the one at the end it meets, to that one's far end through its middle, is not joined, as a line drawn twice is not: the line from (10, 0) back to (0, 0) is not joined to the polyline (0, 0), (10, 0), which it would close into a loop of no area. A spline's flags that it is planar and linear (8 and 16 of group 70) are taken off where it no longer is. The vertices of a POLYLINE are written anew, each with a handle of its own, the POLYLINE and its SEQEND keeping theirs; a LWPOLYLINE keeps the groups of its own vertices.

member.param: The curve to join, in this entity's drawing, another or none.
member.exception: Thrown when the curve is null.

Thrown when the curve is this entity or erased, or is not joined: of a kind this one does not take, closed, out of its plane, not along its line or of its circle, meeting neither end within the tolerance, running back over the piece at that end, having no vertices, or making an arc whole. Nothing is written then.
Thrown when the entity is erased, or has no ends to join at: a closed polyline or spline, a whole ellipse, a fitted polyline, a line of no length, a polyline of no vertices.
Thrown for a class AutoCAD's JOIN joins nothing into, as a CIRCLE or a TEXT.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.JoinEntities(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity})
member.summary: Joins other curves into the entity, as AutoCAD's JoinEntities does, by the rules says: those that join, in one writing of the entity, and the others left out, each left as it is for the caller to erase. Pieces joined end to end are chained on from the entity's end, then back from its start, each time the one of lowest index of those that meet the end reached, so that the lines of a square given in any order close a polyline of one of them; 10 000 lines in any order are chained in time along their count. Lines join whatever their order. Arcs and elliptical arcs are taken in the order of their starts counter-clockwise from the entity's end, the lower index first at one angle, each run on from the entity as it stands then, so that their order does not change what they make: the quarter from 0 to pi / 2 given the arcs from 3 pi / 2 to 7 pi / 4 and from 7 pi / 4 round to pi / 8, in either order, runs to 7 pi / 4 and leaves out the second, which would make it whole.
member.param: The curves to join; one given twice is joined once.
member.returns: The indices of the curves joined, in increasing order; none where none joins, and nothing is written then.
member.exception: Thrown when the list is null.
Thrown when a curve is null, erased or this entity.
Thrown when the entity is erased, or has no ends to join at, as says.
Thrown for a class AutoCAD's JOIN joins nothing into, as a CIRCLE or a TEXT.

member.summary: Gets the points where the entity and another meet, as AutoCAD's IntersectWith: worked out by the library's shapes for both (), each pair of a shape of this entity and one of the other, to . As AutoCAD's, it meets curves and edges, not areas: a closed polyline, a SOLID, a 3DFACE and a mesh by the segments and arcs of their edges, so that the square of side 4 about the origin meets the line from (-10, 0, 0) to (10, 0, 0) at (-2, 0, 0) and (2, 0, 0), and the line through its middle up the z axis nowhere. A chain the library has no intersection of with a shape is taken segment by segment and arc by arc, and a POINT meets a shape where it lies on it. An entity that is to run on past its ends, as the type of intersection says, is taken as its line or circle where it is a LINE or an ARC; any other is taken as it is.
member.param: Which entity runs on past its ends.
member.returns: The points, each once, in the order they are found: the line from (0, 0, 0) to (10, 0, 0) meets the circle of radius 3 about (10, 0, 0) at (7, 0, 0), and extended () at (13, 0, 0) too.
member.exception: Thrown when the entity is null.
Thrown when the type is not one of .
Thrown for a pair of shapes the library has no intersection of, as a text and a line, rather than giving none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.Erase
member.summary: Erases the entity from its block, as AutoCAD's Erase does: every record of it goes, a POLYLINE's vertices and end and an INSERT's attributes with it, its handle is not given again, and what pointed at it is seen to when the file is saved: a GROUP no longer lists it, a list of reactors no longer holds it, and the objects it owned, such as its extension dictionary, go with it; any other pointer at it, as a table cell's at an attribute definition (331) or an XRECORD's data, stays where it stands, named in the log once. member.summary: The object of a record: the one made for it before, else one of the class its type has, else a .

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity.Glance
member.summary: The objects of the records a read looks at once and keeps nothing of, as the display of a drawing reads each entity once: gives the object the record holds where there is one; else, for a LINE, an ARC, a CIRCLE or an LWPOLYLINE, whose objects hold nothing a display reads but the record (a polyline's vertices are not read by it), an object the record does not hold, the same one for every record of its class that follows, aimed at each in turn; else the object makes and keeps. A million entities of those four classes had an object each kept by the display, 24 to 32 bytes of each, 28 MB, which it never read again but through the record. The record holds no object made here, so the one makes for it later is the only one anything else is given: one object for one record, for every reader that keeps it. The object gives is read before the next record is asked for and let go of: it reads that record from then on.
member.remarks: A TEXT, whose object keeps the contexts it read, was tried the same way and left as it was: its contexts were read again at each REGEN, 6 per cent slower for 8 MB. An object made for each record and let go of, in place of one aimed at each, made a REGEN of a million entities 7 to 10 per cent slower.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfHatch
member.summary: A HATCH of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Hatch: an area closed by loops in the plane of its at its , filled solid, with a pattern of lines or with a gradient of colours.

remarks.para: A square 30 by 20 with a circle of radius 5 inside it, filled with ANSI31 in the style, has two loops and 600 less 78.54, 521.46; read from a file AutoCAD wrote, its pattern holds the one line of ANSI31 (), at 45 degrees and 3.175 apart, where the same made in code holds none, as the next paragraph says. The loops are given in the world as the library's shapes (); the file holds them in the system of the normal, as AutoCAD's GetLoopAt gives them.

Each property is read from and written to the HATCH's own groups, every group a change is not about keeping its text, and a property given the value it has changes nothing. A change to the loops of an associative HATCH () takes its association away with the handles of the objects it followed, as AutoCAD's does: its loops are its own from then on. A copy () follows nothing; one copied with every object it follows by follows their copies. The lines a pattern draws are worked out by AutoCAD from the pattern and the loops (EvaluateHatch), and are not in the file; works them out as ezdxf draws them, and gives them as lines in the plane. A pattern of AutoCAD's own pattern file the HATCH does not hold the lines of is not known to the library: new DxfHatch() given ANSI31 by holds no lines of it ( 0), its name and type written for AutoCAD to take the lines from its own file; unless the drawing's finds it in the caller's own pattern files, which give it its lines as AutoCAD gives them: ANSI31 of acadiso.pat, the one line at 45 degrees 3.175 apart.

A file older than R2000 has no HATCH: refuses one there, and a gradient needs R2004 (AC1018). A HATCH copied into a drawing of another version is written as that version writes it, as AutoCAD's SAVEAS writes it: each spline edge's count of fit points (97) as says, and its gradient taken out in a drawing before R2004, the HATCH left filled solid.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfHatch.TransformEntity(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoTransform3)
member.summary: Moves, turns, scales or mirrors the HATCH, as AutoCAD's TransformBy, as ezdxf carries one: each loop taken from the old plane to the world, moved, and into the plane of the new normal, its arcs and ellipses turned with it; the elevation that of the old plane's origin there; the pattern's lines scaled, turned and their base points moved, its scale and angle with them; and, past ezdxf, the seed points moved, as AutoCAD moves them. The angle of a gradient (460) is left as it is, as AutoCAD 2021 leaves it under every turn and mirror. Of an annotative hatch the contexts of its scales move with it (MoveContexts) and its view context is written first, replaced where it has one (KeepHatchView), a move by nought included.
member.remarks:
A transformation that scales the plane unlike along its axes, or shears it, makes the arcs of the loops, and the arcs of a polyline loop, ellipse edges, and each ellipse edge the ellipse it becomes, as ezdxf makes them; the pattern is scaled by the length its x axis takes, as ezdxf scales it.
A mirror (a transformation of negative determinant) keeps the normal as the transformation takes it (a mirror across a plane that holds the normal leaves it as it is, one across the plane of the hatch turns it over), as AutoCAD 2021 keeps it, and reflects what lies in the plane: the loops (a bulge changes its sign, an arc and a circle run the other way round, an ellipse's major axis is reflected) and the seed points. The lines of the pattern are left as they were, as AutoCAD's own TransformBy leaves them while its MIRRHATCH is 0, its default (probed in AutoCAD 2021's console, a mirror across a vertical plane, the plane of the hatch and a tilted plane): a hatch over (42, 50) to (58, 58) mirrored across the line through (0, 0) and (10, 10) lies over (50, 42) to (58, 58), its normal still (0, 0, 1), and a pattern line at 30 degrees is still at 30; with true reflects the lines with the rest, as MIRRHATCH 1 does, a line at 30 degrees across that line coming to 60. The direction of the pattern of each context of an annotative hatch is reflected either way.
member.exception: Thrown when it takes the plane of the HATCH to no plane.
Thrown when the HATCH is erased.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfHatch.TransformBy(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoTransform3,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Moves, turns, scales or mirrors the HATCH as does, and says whether a mirror reflects the lines of its pattern: AutoCAD's TransformBy follows its system variable MIRRHATCH, 0 by default, which leaves them as they were, and 1, which reflects them with the rest; TransformBy(transform) is the 0 form.
member.param: True to reflect the lines of the pattern, in the record and in the contexts of an annotative hatch, as MIRRHATCH 1 does; false to leave them, as MIRRHATCH 0 does. It changes nothing for a transformation that is not a mirror.
member.remarks:
The line of a user pattern at 30 degrees through (0, 0), its offset (-1, 1.732), across the line through (20, 5) and (30, 20) is written as it was with false; with true it is at 82.6198649480404 (twice the angle of the mirror line, 56.31 degrees, less 30), its base at (23.0769, -15.3846) and its offset reflected.
The direction of the pattern of each context of an annotative hatch (groups 10, 20 and 30) is a vector of the world, and is carried by the transformation, but AutoCAD 2021 leaves it as it was where the transformation takes the axes of the hatch's own system (the x and y of its normal) straight to those of the system of the new normal, no turn or reflection between them: a hatch of normal (0, 1, 0), (1, 2, 3) or any but the drawing's, turned about z, a hatch of the plane of the drawing turned 40 degrees about x, a move, a scaling. A pattern at 30 degrees of the plane of the drawing turned 40 degrees about z holds (0.342, 0.940) in its context where it held (0.866, 0.5) and a hatch of normal (0, 1, 0), whose direction is (-0.866, 0, 0.5), turned the same keeps it. Probed over 11 annotative hatches of 6 planes, 16 contexts, turns about x, y, z and two slanting axes by 6 angles each: the 463 hatch and transformation pairs where the direction could tell are all on this rule.
member.exception: Thrown when the transformation is null.
Thrown when it takes the plane of the HATCH to no plane.
Thrown when the HATCH is erased.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfHatch.Explode
member.summary: Gets the lines a HATCH filled with a pattern breaks into, as AutoCAD's EXPLODE breaks one: the dashes of each line of its pattern (), as the HATCH holds them, cut by its loops, each a LINE with the HATCH's look, a dot of the pattern a LINE of no length, as ezdxf's hatch_entity draws them. The lines of a pattern line run from its base point and every offset from it; each is cut where it crosses the loops, its stretches inside them kept by the even-odd rule, and its dashes laid from the line's own base point. The loops it is cut by are those the fills: every loop in the normal style; in the outer style those flagged external or outermost (1 or 16 of their type), and ignoring islands those flagged external, as AutoCAD 2021 and ezdxf take them, so that a square in the outer style round a circle of radius 7 and one of radius 3 in it, both flagged outermost, is hatched inside the smaller circle too, as AutoCAD's Explode hatches it; where no loop is so flagged, by how deep each lies among the others as counts it, the outermost and those just inside them in the outer style, the outermost alone ignoring islands. Lines, arcs, ellipses and splines of a loop are cut where they are crossed, an arc and an ellipse exactly, a spline to the bit within each sixteenth of a span of its knots; a dot that falls on a loop where its line crosses it is kept, but a line of the pattern that runs along a straight edge of a loop gives nothing along it, as AutoCAD gives nothing there: a square 30 by 20 filled with DOTS from its corner, the dots 1.5875 apart, gives 228 dots, none on its bottom edge. A square 30 by 20 filled with ANSI31, the one line at 45 degrees 3.175 apart, gives 11 LINEs; the same round a circle of radius 5 about its middle in the normal style gives 14, the three lines that cross the circle broken in two. The parts run pattern line by pattern line, then by the index of the line from the base point, the least first, then along the line, each from its start along the angle of its pattern line.
member.returns: The entities, in no file, to be added to a drawing by .
member.exception: Thrown for a solid fill and a gradient, which the library does not break; and for a pattern the HATCH holds no lines of, AutoCAD's own pattern file being AutoCAD's: one the drawing's found in none of its files when the pattern was given.

Thrown, before anything is made, when a loop has an edge that is no shape; when the pattern would give more than the 2 000 000 entities of , or its lines would cross the loops more than 32 000 000 times, which holds what the crossings take to half a gigabyte, the parts they give aside; or when the loops lie more than 2^52 of the pattern's spacings, or of the lengths of its dashes, from its base point, where one line or length is not told from the next.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfHatch.Area
member.summary: Gets the area the HATCH fills, as AutoCAD's Area: that of each loop, worked out exactly on its lines, arcs, ellipses and splines (a spline by Gauss's rule, sixteen points to each span of its knots), added or taken off by how deep the loop lies among the others and the : in the normal style every other one, from the outermost in; in the outer style the outermost less those just inside them; ignoring islands, the outermost alone. A square 30 by 20 round a circle of radius 5 fills 521.46 in the normal style.
member.remarks: A loop lies within another where more of the points it is drawn through, and the middles between them, lie inside the other than outside it, by the even-odd rule, those within of the other's edge not counted; where all of them are on that edge, a point inside the loop decides. So an island that touches the outer loop, a triangle in a corner of a square or a notch on its side, is taken off: the square 10 by 10 with the triangle (10, 5), (5, 10), (5, 5) fills 87.5. Loops that cross each other are not cut where they cross: each is within the other or not as most of its points are, so two squares 10 by 10 that overlap by a quarter fill 200, where AutoCAD fills 150. Two loops each within the other, as one loop given twice, count the later within the earlier, as the even-odd rule counts them: a square 10 by 10 given twice fills nothing, and the same round an island given twice fills 100.
member.exception: Thrown when a loop has an edge that is no shape, as says.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfHatchStrips
member.summary: Cuts the area a HATCH fills into the horizontal trapezoids AutoCAD 2021 draws a solid fill of in R12, each with a left and a right side that run from one level of the region's corners to the next, and says in which order and with which sides AutoCAD writes them.
member.remarks: A level is the height of a corner of any loop. A strip between two levels is cut by the edges that cross it, paired off from the left; a trapezoid runs on over a level as long as the same two edges bound it, so a square 100 by 100 with a hole 20 by 20 has trapezoids of different heights on its left and right, unless a convex tip of an outer loop stands at the level (the foot of an arch cuts a slanted piece far from it), and unless the level is the end of the shorter of two sides that meet at the highest or lowest corner of a hole that the loop is walked into by the right-hand side first: the piece beyond the longer side is cut there too, as AutoCAD cuts it. A trapezoid whose top or bottom is a point is a triangle.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfLeader
member.summary: A LEADER of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Leader: a line through its vertices in the world, with an arrow at its first, drawn straight or as a spline, that points to an MTEXT, a TOLERANCE or an INSERT (), drawn by its dimension style with the overrides of its extended data.

remarks.para: The leader through (0, 0, 0), (10, 10, 0) and (20, 10, 0) has three vertices, where its arrow is and where its words are; as a curve its parameter is AutoCAD's, the index of a vertex plus how far along the segment it leaves, so that 1.5 is (15, 10, 0), and its length is 24.14. Splined (), it is walked along the spline fitted through its vertices, as fits one, its parameter the lengths of its chords, the spline fitted once and kept until the drawing is next changed. gives that curve, the polyline of its vertices or the spline, so that meets the leader on it, as AutoCAD's does: the leader from (0, 0, 0) to (10, 5, 0) meets the line x = 5 at (5, 2.5, 0).

The size of its arrow, the gap to its words and the other variables of its dimension style AutoCAD lets one leader have of its own are read from its overrides where it has them, the extended data of ACAD between DSTYLE and its braces, as AutoCAD and ezdxf write them, and from its dimension style where it has not: 2.5 of the style Standard until it is set to 3.5, which writes the override 1070 41, 1040 3.5. A variable a style gives no value of is AutoCAD's own default, the one of its imperial drawing (DIMASZ 0.18). A copy in no file () reads the dimension style, the arrow block and the linetype of the drawing it was copied from, as its original does.

Each property is written into the LEADER's own groups, every other group keeping its text; a property given the value it has changes nothing. AutoCAD draws a leader anew from its vertices and its annotation (EvaluateLeader): what it draws is not in the file, and the library writes the data it is drawn from. A file older than R13 has no LEADER, and refuses one there.

member.summary: The variables of the dimension style a LEADER is drawn with, read and given whole, as AutoCAD's GetDimstyleData and SetDimstyleData of a Leader read and give them.

The leader through (0, 0, 5), (10, 10, 5) and (20, 10, 8) put in the floor runs through (0, 0, 0), (10, 10, 0) and (20, 10, 0), its normal (0, 0, 1). A vertex and a direction in the plane already keep their numbers, a hook (2, 0, 0) as a scale of 2 leaves it among them, and a normal the plane's to 1E-12 keeps its own, so that the leader put in its own plane changes nothing. The annotation is an entity of its own, and stays where it is; the offsets of the last vertex from it (212 and 213) are kept.
member.exception: Thrown when the plane is not valid: a point not finite, or a normal of no length.
Thrown when the leader is erased.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfLeader.Explode
member.summary: Gets the arrowhead and the line, or the spline, the leader breaks into, as AutoCAD 2021's Explode gives them: first, where it has an arrow (), its arrowhead at the first vertex pointing away from the second, times long (a scale of nought taken as 1): an INSERT of the block of turned and scaled so, or, where it names none, AutoCAD's closed filled arrow as a SOLID a third as wide as long, its corners the one on the right of the leader, the tip, and the one on its left; then one LWPOLYLINE through its vertices on its plane (a LINE between each two, a leader whose vertices stand off the plane of its normal, which a polyline cannot hold), or for a splined one () one SPLINE of degree 3 through them, starting along its first segment and ending along its last, its knots the lengths of the chords. Where it has an arrow, the line starts at the arrow's back, the arrow's length along its first segment. Each has the leader's own look, its colour, true colour, linetype and lineweight, whatever its dimension style or its overrides draw a leader with, as AutoCAD 2021 gives them. The leader from (0, 0, 0) through (10, 10, 0) to (20, 10, 0) with an arrow 2.5 long gives a SOLID of the corners (2.06, 1.47, 0), (0, 0, 0) and (1.47, 2.06, 0), and a polyline from (1.77, 1.77, 0) through (10, 10, 0) to (20, 10, 0). The hook AutoCAD runs on under the words of a leader that has one and holds its words above or below its line ( not nought), to where they end, is AutoCAD's to work out from its fonts, and is among them where the drawing's measures the MTEXT it points to (check F1b): the last vertex moved along the hook to the far end of the words, "ABC" of txt.shx 2.5 high held at (22, 10, 0), its hook ending at (21.375, 8.125, 0), giving a polyline ending at (28.667, 8.125, 0).
member.returns: The entities, in no file, to be added to a drawing by .

member.summary: Where the hook of a leader runs on to under its words, as AutoCAD 2021 explodes a leader of words above or below its line (check F1b): along the hook, as far as the far end of the MTEXT it points to, from where the MTEXT is held, as wide as the drawing's measures it (): "ABC" of txt.shx 2.5 high held at (22, 10, 0), its hook ending at (21.375, 8.125, 0), to (28.667, 8.125, 0). False where the leader points to no MTEXT of its drawing, the fonts do not measure it, or the hook has no length.

Through (0, 0, 0), (10, 10, 0) and (20, 10, 0) it runs from 0 to 24.14, its point at 12.07 the one fitted from 0 to 1 has at 0.5. Null where its vertices are all one point. member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader
member.summary: A MULTILEADER of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's MLeader: words of an MTEXT or a block (its content) with leaders that point from it, each leader a dogleg and one or more leader lines, drawn by its multileader style with the properties it overrides.

remarks.para: The file holds a MULTILEADER as AutoCAD keeps one: its own properties, then its context data (groups 300 to 301) with the content, the plane and the leaders (302 to 303), each with its lines (304 to 305). A MULTILEADER of the words "Line one" held at (800, 0, 0) with one leader whose line runs from (780, -10, 0) to its dogleg at (790, -1.25, 0) has , 1, 1, and its line 0 has 2: (780, -10, 0) where its arrow is, and (790, -1.25, 0), the point of its leader the dogleg starts at, which every line of the leader ends at.

Leaders and lines are named by their indices, as AutoCAD names them (90 of a leader, 91 of a line), not by their place. A property set writes the MULTILEADER's own group and the one of its context data AutoCAD keeps with it, and sets its bit of the overrides of the style (group 90), as AutoCAD sets it for a property given a value of its own. A property given the value it has sets its bit all the same and changes nothing else, as AutoCAD 2021 sets it ( is written anew too, and a dogleg's length lands the leaders anew, ); the colour of the words, the content, the block, the direction of the attachment, the annotation scale, the places and the style change nothing. The sizes (, , , and ) are read and set unscaled, as AutoCAD 2021's API reads and sets them, and drawn times the . What AutoCAD works out when it draws the MULTILEADER (where the leaders meet the words, the box of the words, the breaks) is not worked out here: the library writes the data AutoCAD draws it from. Where AutoCAD 2021 moves the words or block, or lands a leader anew, when a property is set, so that each leader still meets the content (the gap, the doglegs, the height, the scale, an attachment, the words given anew, a leader's last vertex), the library moves them as AutoCAD does where that needs no font: words met on their left, by AutoCAD's rules of the lines of words, and a move of words met on their right that keeps them as wide; what AutoCAD lands as far right as its font makes the words wide is left as it was, but where the drawing's measures the words (one line in an SHX or TrueType font), which are then met on their right, lower where their ink reaches below their baseline, and kept readable when mirrored, as AutoCAD 2021 does it (check F1b). Words mirrored across their plane, which then run against its x axis and say so (294 of 1), are moved by the same edits, as AutoCAD 2021 moves them, held at their right, where their width is needed only where the fonts measure them (check D38).

gives the lines of its leaders, as reads a MULTILEADER, so that meets it on them: for each leader line a from its first vertex, where its arrow points, through its vertices and the last point of its leader to the end of the dogleg, a vertex on the one before it left out, along the path draws with the line and its dogleg; splined, a fitted through those points, leaving along the first segment and reaching along the dogleg. Both start at the arrow's point, where starts its line at the back of the arrow, and the spline of a line splined of its own runs on through the dogleg, where the spline exploded ends at the dogleg's start, so that the two part near the arrow and near the words; a multileader whose leader lines are all splined has no dogleg drawn, and its splines run to the end the dogleg would have, exploded too. The line above is met by the line y = -3 from (780, -3, 0) to (795, -3, 0) at (788, -3, 0), on its way up to the dogleg. Its words or block, its arrowheads and the lines AutoCAD draws under the words are not among them, and invisible lines give none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader.Explode
member.summary: Gets the entities the multileader breaks into, as AutoCAD 2021's Explode gives them from its context data: its content first, an MTEXT of its words (, as wide as the context data says, which the scale has scaled already, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it, in its text style and colour) or an INSERT of its block ( at , scaled, turned and coloured so, its attributes given the values the multileader holds), either in the multileader's own linetype and lineweight, as AutoCAD 2021 gives them; then, leader by leader, its dogleg, a LINE from the last point of the leader along its direction, of no length where the dogleg has none, as AutoCAD 2021 draws it, where the multileader has one, its leader lines are not splined and the leader runs left or right of the words, a leader of no line giving its dogleg alone and one of no landing yet () nothing, as AutoCAD 2021 draws them; then line by line, unless the line is invisible, an LWPOLYLINE through the vertices to the last point of the leader, and the arrowhead at the first vertex. A splined line is one SPLINE fitted through the same points, leaving along its first segment and reaching along its dogleg, its knots the lengths of the chords, as AutoCAD's. Without a dogleg, a line on the left or right of the words runs on to the end the dogleg would have; so does every line of a multileader whose leader lines are splined (), which AutoCAD 2021 draws with no dogleg: two lines splined from (0, 0) and (0, 100) to a dogleg from (90, 48) to (98, 48) give two SPLINEs fitted from the backs of their arrows to (98, 48) and no LINE. The arrowhead is drawn where the first segment is more than twice as long as the arrow, as AutoCAD draws it: an INSERT of the line's or the multileader's arrow block, turned to point away from the line, by an angle from nought to a whole turn, and scaled to the arrow's size, or AutoCAD's closed filled arrow as a SOLID a third as wide as long, its corners the one on the right of the line, the tip and the one on its left; the line then starts at the back of the arrow. Each part is on the multileader's layer, and a colour of BYBLOCK, as the style Standard gives the words and the lines, is the multileader's own colour, as AutoCAD 2021 gives it; the arrowhead has the multileader's own linetype, and the SOLID its own lineweight, the INSERT the lineweight of its line, as AutoCAD 2021 gives them: a multileader of lineweight 0.30 and linetype Continuous of its own, its leader lines 0.50, gives a SOLID of 0.30 or an INSERT of 0.50, both Continuous. A line is drawn with the type, colour, linetype, lineweight and arrow size of its own where its flags (93) say it has them, BYBLOCK among them, and its colour where it has no flags and its colour is not BYBLOCK, as ezdxf writes one; else with the multileader's (, , ): a line splined of its own is one SPLINE among the straight lines of the others, one invisible of its own gives nothing, and a line of arrows 2 of its own under arrows 4 starts 2 from its tip; a size of its own is unscaled, as the multileader's own (42), and drawn times the scale of the context data, 4 at a scale of 2, where a line of none is drawn with the size of the context data (140). The words on the right of two leader lines with a dogleg of 8 give an MTEXT, the dogleg's LINE, and for each line an LWPOLYLINE and a SOLID. A multileader scaled to nothing gives nothing. The lines AutoCAD draws under or over the words, as long as the words are wide, are AutoCAD's to work out from its fonts, and are not among them. A copy in no file, made by , finds the blocks, the linetype and the text style its record names in the drawing it was copied from, as a dimension's copy finds its block, and gives what the original gives, the values of its attributes among it; where that drawing has erased a block it names since, it is refused, rather than drawn without it.

With leaders on the left, the words and the leaders on the right move, for the left; with leaders on the right, for the right, the words move where there are none on the left, else the leaders on the right are landed anew. The left of no leader moves words of no leader to meet the base point again, and puts the base point of words met on their right where the left now meets them, as AutoCAD 2021 does (check D38b): "ABC" at (100, 50, 0) of no leader stand at (100, 52.8, 0) met at the bottom line. Another side with no leader moves nothing.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader.FinishMirror(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoTransform3,System.Boolean,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Puts right a MULTILEADER that has mirrored, as AutoCAD 2021's MIRROR command leaves one, which is not as its TransformBy leaves one (probed in its console, mirror-mleader GHMM1 and GHMM3). The plane stays the drawing's: its x axis the mirrored one turned back where the mirror turns it back (a mirror across an upright), else its y axis the mirrored one turned back, 297 nought. Words kept readable (MIRRTEXT 0) keep their normal and their direction in the plane, and stand where they stood from the mirrored landing of the first leader, across it where the mirror turns the plane's x axis back; words mirrored (MIRRTEXT 1) are mirrored with the rest. Where the mirror turns the plane's x axis back, the words are held by their other side (171 of 1 made 3), the content lined up the other way (176), with bit 14 of the overrides. The base point of words is then the left of their box, along the plane's x axis, short of it by the landing gap; that of a block where a leader from the left meets it, and the block's matrix its transform where it now stands. Words that run against the plane's x axis say so (294 of 1). "ABC" of arial.ttf 0.18 high at (30.45, 20.09) held at its top left, landed at (30, 20) by a dogleg of 0.36, mirrored across x = 100 stands at (169.55, 20.09) held at its top right, its base point at (168.95, 20); mirrored across y = 100, at (30.45, 180.09).
member.param: The MULTILEADER as it was before the mirror, which is left as it is.
The mirror, across a plane upright to the MULTILEADER's.
Whether the words are mirrored with the rest (MIRRTEXT 1), not kept readable.
The width of the ink of the words' widest line, from where it starts, as AutoCAD's ActualWidth.
The height of the words, as AutoCAD's ActualHeight.

member.summary: The words of a MULTILEADER mirrored by MIRROR (): their normal, place, direction, turn and attachment, whether they run against the plane's x axis (294), and the base point at the left of their box.

member.summary: Gives a MULTILEADER made in code the handles of the drawing it is added to: its multileader style (340), the drawing's CMLEADERSTYLE or Standard, and the text style (343) of that style's words, else Standard, where it names none of the drawing's; its words (340 of the context's MTEXT) are given the same text style, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them, or the text style they named when given, where the drawing has it (with bit 11 where it is not the style's), moved then to where the style's font would meet them where the drawing's fonts measure both (check D38). In a drawing of R2013 or later its leaders run on to its content (295 of 1), as AutoCAD 2021 makes every new multileader; in an older one it has no 295, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it (check D38b). Words given in no drawing, where no leader is landed, have the base point of their content put again as the drawing's fonts meet them ().
member.exception: Thrown when the drawing has no multileader style of the name, or no text style Standard.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader.TransformEntity(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoTransform3)
member.summary: Moves, turns, scales or mirrors the MULTILEADER, as AutoCAD's TransformBy, as ezdxf carries one: the base point, the plane, the leaders' points, doglegs and breaks, the lines' vertices, the MTEXT's place, direction and normal and the block's place, normal, scale and turn as it is drawn, its matrix written as its transform where it then stands, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it; the sizes the words, arrows, landing and doglegs are drawn with scaled with it (41, 140 and 145 of the context data, 40 of each leader, and the widths of the words), left to the bit by a turn or a mirror alone, as AutoCAD 2021 leaves them (words 0.18 high mirrored across a line at 45 degrees stay 0.18, check mirror-3 GHM3B), and the scale of the context data (40), the MULTILEADER's own scale (45), length of the doglegs (41), size of the arrows (42), block scale (10) and block turn (43), and the arrow sizes leader lines have of their own, left as they are, as AutoCAD 2021's TransformBy leaves them: a multileader of scale 1, its doglegs 8, scaled by 2 is still of scale 1, its doglegs drawn 16 and 41 still 8, its words 60 wide then 120 wide, a line's own arrows of 2 still drawn 2, and its block drawn twice the size with still 1. Where it scales, by 2 or by 0.5, turned or mirrored too, the scale is marked as the multileader's own (bit 24 of its overrides, 90), as AutoCAD 2021 marks it, and stays marked once scaled back; a move, a turn or a mirror alone leaves the mark as it was. A block mirrored is drawn where the mirror puts it, its normal mirrored with it, its x scale turned negative and its turn read from its y axis, and the plane of a multileader of a block takes the mirrored normal, an x axis on the side the old one keeps and its y axis across them (297 of nought), as AutoCAD 2021 writes them: the box of lines from (-10, -5) to (20, 15) at (100, 50, 0), turned 30 degrees and mirrored across the XY plane, is of normal (0, 0, -1), scales (-1, 1, 1) and turn 330 degrees, its plane's y axis (0, -1, 0); mirrored across the YZ plane, of normal (0, 0, 1), its plane's x axis (1, 0, 0). Words mirrored are carried as ezdxf carries them, but where the drawing's measures them (one line held at its top), which are kept readable as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them, the plane taken as a block's is (check F1b): "ABC" of txt.shx 10.67 wide at (100, 50, 0) mirrored across the XY plane held at (110.67, 50, 0), facing (0, 0, -1) and running against x, which they say (294 of 1, check D38); across the YZ plane held by its top right at (-100, 50, 0), running along x, the base point of the content at (-112.67, 48, 0). A mirror that turns the plane's x axis back, a block's or such words', lines the content up the other way, the context's alignment (176) of the left made the right's and the right's the left's, a centred one kept, and sets bit 14 of the overrides, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it (check D38): the box mirrored across the YZ plane, or across a plane of normal (1, 0.2, 0), has 176 of 2; mirrored back, 0, the bit kept, and says so (294 of 1, then of nought), as AutoCAD 2021 writes it (check D38b). Of the two ways to read words kept readable, the one kept is the one turned in the system of their normal nearer the turn they had, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them (check D38b): across XZ, or a plane of normal (0.2, 1, 0), "ABC" runs the mirrored way, upright, met again at its attachment by the mirrored leader, at (100, -46, 0) running along x; across XY against x, as above; turned a quarter first, across XY, up y still.
member.exception: Thrown when it scales the MULTILEADER more one way than another, which ezdxf and AutoCAD refuse, or shears it, keeping its axes as long as each other but not square, which AutoCAD refuses too.
Thrown when the MULTILEADER is erased.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader.GetOverridedMLeaderStyle(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeaderStyle)
member.summary: Gives a style made in code the values the multileader is drawn with, as AutoCAD's getOverridedMLeaderStyle, named here as the library names its members: those of its multileader style (), and in place of each it overrides (a bit of its 90) its own, as ezdxf's MLeaderStyleOverride reads them. A multileader of the style Standard, its words 2.5 high of its own, gives 2.5 and the style's arrows, 4 long. An override is the value the multileader's group gives, the style's kept where the multileader has no group of it, but for the arrows: a multileader of AutoCAD's closed filled arrow gives a style of no arrow block. Each is read as the multileader writes it, as MLeaderStyleOverride reads it: the height of the words (bit 16) and the landing gap (bit 5) from the context data, scaled (its 41 and 145, as drawn, which and read over the scale); the size of the arrows (bit 9) from the multileader's own 42, unscaled, as the style holds it; the length of the doglegs (bit 7) from its own 41, unscaled too, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it. A multileader of scale 2 with words 8 high, arrows 4 and doglegs 8 of its own, drawn 16, gives a style of words 8 high, arrows 4 and doglegs 8, whose scale is the multileader's 2 where it overrides that too (bit 24).
member.param: The style, made in code by new DxfMLeaderStyle(); given these values in place of any it had.
member.exception: Thrown when the style is null.
Thrown when the style is one of a drawing, whose record is not written.
Thrown when the multileader names no multileader style of its drawing, or is in none.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMLeader.SetFromStyle
member.summary: Gives the multileader the values of its multileader style and takes away its overrides of it, as AutoCAD's SetFromStyle: the style's scale first, then its look of the leader lines, the landing, the dogleg, the arrows, the words and the block, each written by the property of its name (, ... ) in the multileader and its context data, its linetype (341) and text style (343, and 340 of its words) by the style's handles; then its overrides (90) set to nought. A multileader of the style Standard, its words 2.5 high of its own, has words 4 high, as the style. The sizes, unscaled in the style, are scaled once by the scale the multileader then has: the height of the words, the landing gap and the size of the arrows of the context data (41, 145 and 140) and each leader's length of the dogleg (40) are the style's times the scale, and the multileader's own size of the arrows (42) and length of the doglegs (41) the style's, unscaled, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them; Standard scaled 2 gives words 8 high, a gap of 4, arrows 8 drawn (42 of 4) and doglegs 16 drawn (41 of 8). A value the style gives that the multileader cannot take keeps the multileader's own and its bit: a content (172) or a block (344) it does not hold, a size or a type out of AutoCAD's range, a linetype or a text style the style names none of or one its drawing has not, an arrow block or a block a copy in no drawing cannot be given (it keeps its own arrow, and takes the rest), and the attachments of the top and bottom and their direction in a file older than R2010; so do the bits of no property the library writes (18, 26 and 30). What it cannot take is judged before anything is written, so that nothing is left half set. The overrides of each leader line (its 93) are the multileader's own, not the style's, and stay. The words, the block and the landings stay where they are, the properties written here not moving them as they do when set one by one: how AutoCAD 2021 moves them when a style is taken has not been read.
member.returns: Whether the multileader names a multileader style of its drawing it is set from (for a copy in no file, of the drawing it was copied from); false, and nothing changed, where it names none, or has no context data to be drawn from.
member.exception: Thrown when the multileader is erased and differs from its style.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfMlineBuilder
member.summary: Builds an MLINE as AutoCAD writes it, from the points it is drawn through, its style, scale and justification, and builds the record anew after an edit, as AutoCAD's Mline (AppendSegment, MoveVertexAt, IsClosed) does: its direction, miter and the offset of each element at every vertex worked out as AutoCAD works them out. A multiline is a whose is MLINE.

remarks.para: A multiline of the style STANDARD (two elements 0.5 either side of the line) at scale 1, justified at its top, through (0, 0), (100, 0) and (100, 100), is written as AutoCAD writes it: the style's name (2) and handle (340), scale (40), justification (70: 0 top, 1 zero, 2 bottom), flags (71: 1, plus 2 closed, 4 start caps left off, 8 end caps left off), vertex count (72), element count (73), the first vertex (10) and the normal (210); then at each vertex its point (11), the direction of the segment it starts (12; the last vertex has that of the segment before it), its unit miter (13) and for each element the count (74) and parameters (41) and 75 of 0. At the corner (100, 0) the miter is (-0.7071, 0.7071), the half angle's cosine 0.7071, and the elements' first parameters 0 and -1.4142 (the offset of the element from the top, 0 and -1, divided by the cosine); the straight vertices give 0 and -1. At scale 20 and justified at its middle they are 10 and -10, and justified at its bottom 20 and 0.

The miter of an inner vertex is the bisector of the normals of the two segments, that of an open start the direction turned by the style's start angle, that of an end the direction of its last segment turned by the end angle; the cosine in the division is the miter's against the normal of the segment, never less than 1E-4 in magnitude, as AutoCAD's. After the first parameter of an element come the stretches it is drawn along the segment, a start and a stop by turns, measured from where the element stands at the vertex: a start of nought and no stop is the whole segment, as a multiline is written, and the cuts of MLEDIT are the gaps between a stop and the next start. These are read from an existing multiline and written back with it, so that after a point is moved leaves the cuts of the segments that stay where they were.
