member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.TryRead(System.String,System.Globalization.CultureInfo,System.DateTime@)
member.summary: Reads the words as a date or a time, as AutoCAD 2021 does in the culture given: a date in the order of the culture (1/2/2020 the second of January in en-US), with a month in words (Jan 1 2020, 1 January 2020), a year of two figures (1/1/49 is 2049 and 1/1/50 is 1950), no year (the present one), a time of 12 or 24 hours (12:30, 12:30:45, 12:30 PM, 1 AM) alone or after the date, and 1-2 and 2020-01. It reads no fraction of a second, no name of a weekday, no zone and no point where the culture has none as its mark (12:30:45.5, Sat Jan 4 2020, 12:30Z, 3.4.2020 in en-US, a date in de-DE), nor a day or a time that does not exist (2/30/2020, 24:00), nor a year before 100; those stay words.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.FormatOf(System.DateTime)
member.summary: The format AutoCAD 2021 gives a date typed in a cell of no kind: %x, the date, where the day has no time or the time is that of midnight (12:30 AM is a time, and 0:00 is the date 12/30/1899), %X, the time, where it is on the day of a time alone, and %c, both, otherwise.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.Text(System.DateTime,System.String,System.Globalization.CultureInfo)
member.summary: The words a date shows in a format, as AutoCAD 2021 shows them in the culture given: the date for none or %x, the time for %X, both for %c, the letters of a C library's strftime after a percent (%A %a %B %b %h %C %d %e %H %I %M %m %p %S %u %w %Y %y %D %F %R %r %T %z %Z, as %d/%m/%Y 07/03/2020 for the 7th of March 2020; %u counts the week from 1 on a Monday to 7 on a Sunday, %r is the time as %X shows it, and %z and %Z are the machine's zone, +0700 and its daylight name, as AutoCAD shows them), the figures d, M and y of a format with no percent (M/d/yyyy), the rest as it is; the date for a format the library does not write, those whose words AutoCAD gets wrong among them (%j is 001 for every date it reads, %U and %W are 01 on a Sunday or a Monday and 00 on any other day).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.Offset(System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: A zone's offset from UTC as %z shows it: a sign, then hours and minutes of two figures each (+0700).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.Editing(System.DateTime,System.Globalization.CultureInfo)
member.summary: The words a cell of a date opens as in AutoCAD 2021's editor, GetTextString(FormatOption.ForEditing), whatever its format: the date alone where the day has no time (1/1/2020), the time alone where it is on the day of a time (12:30:00 PM), and both otherwise (1/1/2020 12:30:00 PM).

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.Bytes(System.DateTime)
member.summary: The 16 bytes AutoCAD 2021 keeps a date in (310 after a 92 of 16), a SYSTEMTIME of its year, month, day of the week from Sunday, day, hour, minute, second and thousandths, each of two bytes, the low one first, in capital letters of hexadecimal: 1/1/2020 12:30 is E4070100030001000C001E0000000000.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.NoDateBytes
member.summary: The 16 bytes of a date AutoCAD 2021 could not make: all nought, which read as no date.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.Seconds(System.DateTime)
member.summary: The seconds a date is after the epoch, 1 January 1970, as the C library's mktime counts them from the date as the cell shows it (read as the machine's own time, its zone taken off): -1 where that is before it, as AutoCAD 2021's series of dates went on from it (D42): 1/1/2020 is 1 577 836 800 less the zone, and 1/1/1970 or 12:30 alone, which is on the 30th of December 1899, -1.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.TryFromSeconds(System.Int64,System.DateTime@)
member.summary: The date and time a count of seconds after the epoch makes, as gmtime gives them, with no zone put back; false where AutoCAD 2021 could make none, a count before -43 200 or one past the year 9999.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableDate.TryFromBytes(System.String,System.DateTime@)
member.summary: The date the 16 bytes of a cell's 310 hold, as writes them; false for any other group.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText
member.summary: The text a table's cell opens as in AutoCAD 2021's editor, GetTextString(FormatOption.ForEditing), from the number the cell holds and the units of its format (D40): the number as it is, to 16 figures with the zeros left off, where the cell shows it to the places of the drawing. Every function is exact in decimal digits, so that .NET Framework, which writes 15 figures of a double, and .NET Core give the same words.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Decimal(System.Double)
member.summary: A number in decimals: 16 figures, 15 places at most, rounded half away from nought, the zeros after the point left off, 1/3 as 0.333333333333333, 123456789.12345679 as 123456789.1234568, 0.1 + 0.2 as 0.3 and 1E-16 as 0. A number of more than 16 figures before the point is in powers of ten, as .

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Architectural(System.Double)
member.summary: A number of inches in feet and inches to 1/32768 of an inch, the fraction reduced and what is nought left out: 12.5 as 1'-0 1/2", 12 as 1', 7 as 7", 0.5 as 1/2" and 0 as 0". A number of more feet than 32 bits hold is in powers of ten.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Engineering(System.Double)
member.summary: A number of inches in feet and decimals of an inch: 75.25 as 6'-3.25", 12 as 1', 0.5 as 0.5" and 1500.5 as 125'-0.5".

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Fractional(System.Double)
member.summary: A number in whole numbers and fractions to 1/32768: 12.5 as 12 1/2, 0.1 as 3277/32768, -0.5 as -1/2 and 100 as 100.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Point(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: A point's three coordinates in decimals, one comma and space between: 1.5, 2.25, -0.1.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Split(System.Double,System.String@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: The digits of a positive number without their zeros at either end, and where the point stands: 0.digits times ten to the point.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Round(System.String,System.Int32@,System.Int32)
member.summary: The digits kept to a count of them, the rest rounded half away from nought; the count may be nought or below, which keeps none or a one.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Place(System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: The digits laid out about the point: 0.0015, 1500 and 12.5.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Counted(System.Double,System.Int64,System.Int64@)
member.summary: A length counted in the parts of an inch it is read to, half away from nought; false for one of more feet than 32 bits hold.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTableEditingText.Reduced(System.Int64)
member.summary: A count of parts of an inch as the fraction it is, reduced: 16384 of 32768 as 1/2; empty for none.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTextSymbols
member.summary: The symbols AutoCAD 2021's text editor enters from its Symbol menu, each the letter it stands for, and the three control codes of that menu, to be put into the words of a TEXT, an MTEXT, an attribute or a dimension without remembering a code: new DxfMText { Contents = DxfTextSymbols.Diameter + "20" } reads ∅20. The letters are those of AutoCAD's help, "Text Symbols and Special Characters Reference", and of its menu, and nothing else. Each is written as AutoCAD writes it: as it is in a drawing of R2007 or later, and before, where the code page has not the letter, as its escape, so that ∅20 in an MTEXT of R2004 is \U+220520. Written by the library into an MTEXT, a TEXT, an attribute and a dimension of R2004 and of R2018, each of the 21 was read back by AutoCAD 2021 as the same letter, in its Contents, Text, TextString and DimensionText alike, and AutoCAD wrote its own texts of them in the same bytes. A letter shows only in a font that has it: AutoCAD's help names simplex, romans, gdt, amgdt, isocp and isoct among the SHX fonts, and isocpeur and isocteur among the TrueType.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTextSymbols.DegreeCode
member.summary: The control code of the degree sign, %%d, which AutoCAD draws as in a TEXT, an attribute, a dimension and an MTEXT. The words keep it as written: a TEXT's TextString and an MTEXT's Contents of 45%%d are 45%%d, and the MTEXT's Text is 45°, in AutoCAD 2021 and in alike, as reads either.

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTextSymbols.PlusMinusCode

member.name: F:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTextSymbols.DiameterCode

AutoCAD 2021 gives the Text of an MTEXT of %%c20 as ∅20, the letter , and and read it so too, in an MTEXT and a TEXT.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfTolerance
member.summary: A TOLERANCE of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's FeatureControlFrame: a feature control frame of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, its words in group 1 as AutoCAD's TOLERANCE command writes them, put at its insertion point along its direction in the plane of its normal and drawn by its dimension style.

remarks.para: The words () hold one row of the frame to a line, a line feed between rows (^J in the file), and its cells in the row with %%v between them: the symbol, the two tolerances, the three datums. A symbol is a letter of AutoCAD's gdt font, {\Fgdt;j} the position, {\Fgdt;n} the diameter sign and {\Fgdt;m} the maximum material condition, so that the position of a diameter 0.1 at the maximum material condition to the datums A, B and C is {\Fgdt;j}%%v{\Fgdt;n}0.1{\Fgdt;m}%%vA%%vB%%vC. The height of a projected zone and the datum identifier are rows of their own: 5{\Fgdt;p} and D.

The record holds the dimension style (group 3), the insertion point (10, 20, 30), the words (1), the normal (210, 220, 230) and the direction (11, 21, 31), the last two left out where they are the world's z and x, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them. Overrides of the dimension style are the list DSTYLE of its extended data of ACAD, as a dimension's are: reads them. A file of R12 has no TOLERANCE.

moves it as AutoCAD 2021 moves one, and so do MOVE, COPY, ROTATE, SCALE and MIRROR: its point moved, its direction turned, its normal the one its direction and the frame's up make after the move, so that a mirror turns it over (normal (0, 0, -1)); a move that scales it writes its text height and gap scaled as overrides (DIMTXT, then DIMGAP), as AutoCAD 2021 writes them: a frame of the style's 0.18 and 0.09 scaled by 3 holds 1070 140, 1040 0.54, 1070 147, 1040 0.27. It is not exploded: AutoCAD 2021's Explode refuses one too.
is the box of its rows as AutoCAD 2021 lays them out, where the drawing's measures its words.

A frame of the style ISO-25 given a text height of 5 gives Dimtxt 5 and Dimgap 0.625, the style's. member.summary: Gets the box the frame fills, as AutoCAD's GeometricExtents: that of its rows as AutoCAD 2021 lays them out (probes GHTQ1 and GHTQ2), each twice the text height high (Dimtxt times Dimscale of ), the first about its , each next under the one before on the same left side, each as wide as its cells, a cell its ink and the text height, along its in the plane of its . {\Fgdt;j}%%v0.1 at (0, 0, 0) in a style of Arial 0.18 high is from (0, -0.18, 0) to (0.92296, 0.18, 0), and a frame of no words from (0, -0.18, 0) to (0, 0.18, 0). The words are measured in the drawing's fonts (), in the text style of Dimtxsty, the symbols of the gdt font by the widths AutoCAD gives them. Elsewhere, where a cell holds words the fonts do not measure, as gives it.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity
member.summary: An entity of a type the library has no class for, such as a REGION, a SHAPE or an ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY: kept as the file has it, its groups read as they are, its look editable and the entity erasable.
member.remarks: Its , colour, linetype, lineweight and visibility are set as any entity's are, every other group of its record kept as it was; its geometry is not changed, so is refused, but for an MLINE, which a transformation that scales alike moves ( builds one), and a REGION, whose ACIS data is written anew for the body it becomes (a move, a turn, a scale or a mirror). It is copied as it is by , and by with the identity. gives what reads of it, nothing for a type it does not read. An MLINE is exploded into its lines and caps, and a MESH into the 3DFACEs of its faces ().
member.content: A REGION: made from its shape, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it, read back from the ACIS data it holds, and moved by writing the data of the body it becomes.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity.Groups
member.summary: Gets every group of the entity's record, in the order of the file, after the group 0 that names its type, each value the text the file prints; a new list on each call. Of a POLYLINE they run on through its vertices and of an INSERT through its attributes, each opened by its own group 0. A comment (999) is not among them, though the file keeps it.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity.Explode
member.summary: Gets the entities an MLINE breaks into, as AutoCAD's Explode, as ezdxf's virtual_entities gives them, from the geometry its record holds and the MLINESTYLE it names: for an open one its start caps, then a LINE for each element along each segment, the miter lines at each joint where its style draws them, then its end caps. A cap across the elements is two LINEs, from the outer elements to the point halfway between them; an outer cap a half circle from the outer element on the left round to the one on the right, two quarter ARCs where their colours differ; inner arcs join each pair of inner elements, the second and the last but one, the third and the last but two, as AutoCAD's MLSTYLE draws them. A LINE has the element's colour and linetype, an ARC its colour, each the MLINE's look besides, its true colour left off. An element broken along a segment (MLEDIT) gives a LINE for each piece left, and caps the MLINE leaves off (flags 4 and 8 of its group 71) are not drawn; a line of no length is left out, and the fill of a filled style too. The MLINE of the style Standard, two elements 0.5 either side, through four vertices gives six LINEs. A MESH not smoothed (level 0) breaks into a 3DFACE for each face, in the order of its list of faces, each with the MESH's look and every edge drawn, as AutoCAD's EXPLODE breaks one and ezdxf's MeshBuilder renders it: a face of four corners a 3DFACE of them, of three one ending on its third; a cube 10 by 10 by 10 of eight vertices and six faces gives six 3DFACEs. A face of more than four corners breaks into a strip of triangles, as AutoCAD 2021's Explode breaks one: from two corners on, the rest taken by turns from the far end and the near one, each triangle after the first the other way round; from the face's first two corners, or from its last two back the other way where it faces into a closed MESH whose other faces face out, as AutoCAD turns every face of a closed mesh to face out. The face of the corners 0 to 4 alone, or one of an open MESH, gives the triangles (0, 1, 4), (2, 4, 1) and (4, 2, 3), and as the base of a pyramid facing up into it (4, 3, 0), (2, 0, 3) and (0, 2, 1); of 0 to 5, (0, 1, 5), (2, 5, 1), (5, 2, 4) and (3, 4, 2) alone and (5, 4, 0), (3, 0, 4), (0, 3, 1) and (2, 1, 3) as such a base. A face of four corners or three that faces into a closed MESH is turned as well, its corners read from its last back, as AutoCAD 2021 explodes one: the square base (0, 1, 2, 3) of a pyramid facing up into it gives the 3DFACE of (3, 2, 1, 0), a side (0, 3, 4) facing in (4, 3, 0); every other is given as the file holds it. A face given a colour of its own (an override of the MESH, its subentity 1 the first face) keeps it on its 3DFACEs, as AutoCAD keeps it. A MESH smoothed, and one that gives a face a material or a transparency of its own, or an edge or a vertex anything of its own, is refused. A REGION breaks into the curves of its loops, a hole before the loop it is cut from, as AutoCAD's Explode gives them: a box 40 by 30 with a circular hole gives a circle and four lines, a stadium two lines and two arcs, each with the REGION's look; a REGION of several faces (the union of two regions far apart) breaks into a REGION for each face, as AutoCAD's does, and its arcs run counter-clockwise about the face's normal. Any other type refuses: a 3DSOLID, a BODY and a surface, which AutoCAD breaks with its solid modeler, and every type AutoCAD does not break.
member.returns: The entities, in no file, to be added to a drawing by .
member.exception: Thrown for an MLINE whose drawing has no MLINESTYLE of its handle or name, or whose vertices hold another count of elements than its style; and for a MESH missing the count of its vertices, faces, edges or creases, or holding fewer than it counts, as ezdxf refuses one, or with a face of fewer than three corners, past the end of its list of faces or naming a vertex it has not.
Thrown for a MESH smoothed, or with overrides other than the colours of its faces, for a REGION whose ACIS data is not readable flat faces ( gives null), and for any other type.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity.MeshEdges
member.summary: The edges of a MESH as its record lists them (94 and two indices each), each as the two points of its vertices, in the order and the direction the record gives: AutoCAD writes a MESH saved as R12 as these edges. Null where the record lists none or is not readable.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity.MeshParts
member.summary: The faces of a MESH, as sets them out, read in one pass over its record (AcDbSubDMesh) by its counts, as AutoCAD writes them: its level of smoothing (91), its vertices (92 and a point 10 for each), its faces (93, the count of the groups 90 after it, each face the count of its corners and their indices), its edges (94 and two indices each) and creases (95 and a value each), then the count of its overrides (90), each a subentity (91), the count of its properties (92), and each property its kind (90) and value: a colour (0) its 63, and its 420 where it is true.
member.exception: Thrown where a count the record should hold is missing, below nought or more than the groups after it, as ezdxf refuses such a MESH.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity.FacingIn(System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32[]})
member.summary: Which faces of a MESH face into it, to be read the other way round, as AutoCAD 2021 turns every face of a closed mesh to face out: of each piece of faces joined edge to edge that is closed (each of its edges shared by two of its faces) and whose faces can all be turned to agree, those that, once they agree, face into the room it closes. A piece that closes no room beyond a point's tolerance by its area, an open one, and one whose faces cannot agree, is read as the file holds it. The pyramid on six corners whose base faces up into it and whose sides face out has its base read the other way round.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfUnknownEntity.TransformEntity(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoTransform3)
member.summary: Moves an MLINE or a REGION by a transformation that scales alike (a move, a turn, a mirror, a scale). An MLINE has its points moved, its normal moved (turned the other way by a mirror, so that its elements stay on the same side of its line), its scale and the stretches of its cuts multiplied by the scale of the transformation. Refuses every other type, the geometry of a type the library keeps as it is not being changed, and an MLINE or a REGION moved by a transformation that scales more one way than another or shears. A REGION has every edge and plane moved and its ACIS data written anew for its drawing's version (), the loops kept in their order, the normal turned over by a mirror, as AutoCAD's TransformBy leaves a region.
member.exception: Thrown for a type other than MLINE and REGION, for an MLINE or a REGION moved by a transformation that does not scale alike, and for a REGION whose ACIS data is not readable flat faces.
Thrown for an MLINE whose drawing has no style of its handle or name.

member.summary: Makes a REGION of a shape, for a drawing: its ACIS data written as AutoCAD 2021 writes it for the drawing's version, SAT text in the groups of the entity for R2000 to R2010 (version 400 of ACIS for R2000, ASM 208, 212 and 215 for R2004, R2007 and R2010) and, for R2013 and R2018, SAB in the data store of the file (the section ACDSDATA, which writes the record of), the entity naming its data by a GUID.
member.param: The shape: a box 40 by 30 with a hole of radius 5 makes a region of area 1 121.46.
The drawing the region is made for; it is added to a block of that drawing.
member.returns: The region, on layer 0 in no drawing, to be added by .
member.exception: Thrown when the shape or the drawing is null.
Thrown when the drawing is of a version before R2000, whose regions are not written.
member.remarks: The groups are those of AutoCAD's own: for R2000 to R2010 the marker AcDbModelerGeometry, group 70 of 1 and a group 1 for each line of the SAT, each character but a space written as 0x9F less it and a caret followed by a space; for R2013 and R2018 group 290 of 1 and group 2 with the GUID. A shape of several faces (the union of two regions far apart) is one region of several lumps, as AutoCAD keeps it. Appended to a drawing of another version than it was made for, refuses it.

member.remarks: A region AutoCAD 2021 wrote in a box 40 by 30 gives one loop of four lines, area 1 200 and perimeter 140; the same with a circular hole of radius 5 two loops, the circle (a hole) first, area 1 121.46 and perimeter 171.42. A region read from a file is read again on each call.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfVertex
member.summary: A VERTEX of a POLYLINE, as AutoCAD's Vertex is one of a polyline: the record that follows the polyline in the file and gives one of its points, of the class its polyline has (, , , or ).

remarks.para: A vertex is reached by walking its polyline, foreach (DxfVertex2d v in polyline), as AutoCAD walks the vertices of one: the same object each time while its record is there. Its is the polyline; its point, look and extended data are read from its own record and written into it, its handle kept.

A vertex made in code, such as new DxfVertex2d(point, 0.5, 0, 0, 0), is in no polyline until it is appended to one, as AutoCAD's AppendVertex takes it; it is the vertex of that polyline from then on, every other vertex keeping its handle. takes a vertex out of its polyline the same way.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport
member.summary: A VIEWPORT of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Viewport: a window of a layout's sheet onto model space, its place and size on the sheet, the view it shows, its snap and grid, its user coordinate system and the layers frozen in it.

remarks.para: A viewport 200 wide and 150 high about (150, 100) on the sheet that shows model space about (5 000, 3 000) at 1:50 has (150, 100, 0), 200, 150, (5 000, 3 000) and 7 500: is 150 / 7 500, 0.02, and . Its is the id the file gives it (group 69) while it is on, 1 for the viewport that shows the sheet itself, and -1 turned off.

A file of R2000 or later holds the view in the viewport's own groups (12 to 51, 90 for its flags, 331 for its frozen layers); one of R12, R13 or R14 in its extended data of ACAD, after MVIEW, each value in its place, read and written there. What those have not, as the user coordinate system or the plot style, reads as AutoCAD's default and is not set there.

The view is not drawn anew: a change to it is written, and AutoCAD shows it when the drawing is next opened. moves and scales the viewport on its sheet, as AutoCAD's TransformBy does, the view in it kept: a viewport scaled by 2 shows the same part of model space twice as large. (AutoCAD's SCALE command does otherwise, keeping the scale of the view; the presenter's SCALE follows the command.)

member.summary: Initializes a viewport made in code, as AutoCAD's new Viewport(): about the origin, 1 by 1, off, showing the top view of model space about its origin; give it its place, size and view, append it to a layout of paper space and turn it .

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.Number
member.summary: Gets the number of the viewport in its layout, as AutoCAD's Number gives it once the layout is shown: the id of group 69 for a viewport that is , 1 for the viewport that shows the sheet itself and 2 and on for those on it; -1 for a viewport turned off, as AutoCAD 2021 gave its viewport 94 of id 3 turned off, which a file still writes the id of. A viewport made in code is given the next free id of its layout when appended. AutoCAD gives -1 for every viewport of a layout not yet shown as well, which a file does not say: the library reads the layout as shown.

member.value: Set off, the status 0 and the flag set; set on, the flag cleared and the status the next above those of the other viewports of its layout, as AutoCAD stacks them.
member.exception: Thrown when the viewport is erased.

member.exception: Thrown when the viewport is erased, or set in a file older than R2000, which has no such flag.

member.summary: Gets or sets whether the viewport is clipped by another entity (flag 0x10000 of group 90, the entity group 340), as AutoCAD's NonRectClipOn; and set it with the entity.
member.exception: Thrown when the viewport is erased, or set in a file older than R2000.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.NonRectClipEntity
member.summary: Gets the entity that clips the viewport (group 340), as AutoCAD's NonRectClipEntityId names it: a circle, an ellipse, a closed polyline, a closed spline or a REGION of the same layout, drawn as the border of the viewport. Null for a viewport that is not clipped (), one whose boundary the drawing no longer holds, and one of a file older than R2000.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.ClipTo(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity)
member.summary: Clips the viewport to a closed entity of its layout, as the VPCLIP command does with an object: the viewport shows model space only inside the boundary, and its frame becomes the box of the boundary, its view kept in place. A viewport 100 by 80 about (100, 100) at 1:2 clipped to a circle of radius 30 about (110, 105) is 60 by 60 about (110, 105), the model point at its centre now the one that lay 10 right and 5 above, 20 and 10 in model units. The boundary stays the entity it is, with the viewport among its reactors (102 {ACAD_REACTORS), as AutoCAD writes it; the boundary the viewport had before stays an entity of the layout, let go. A region is a boundary as it is: one of a ring (a circle of radius 40 less one of 15) makes the frame 80 by 80, the box of its outer loop, and shows nothing in the hole, and one of two squares apart has a frame round both.
member.param: A circle, a whole ellipse, a closed polyline (LWPOLYLINE or 2D POLYLINE), a closed spline or a REGION whose shape is read () of the viewport's block, which is not the viewport.
member.exception: Thrown when the boundary is null.
Thrown when the boundary is not an entity of the viewport's block, is erased, has no area, or is not a closed circle, ellipse, polyline or spline, as AutoCAD says "Clip object must be closed."
Thrown when the viewport is erased or in no file, or the file is older than R2000, which has no such link.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.FitToClip
member.summary: Fits the frame of the viewport to the box of its clip boundary again, as AutoCAD does when the boundary is moved, scaled, stretched or turned: the frame is the box of the boundary, and the view keeps its scale and its place, so that a boundary moved 10 to the right takes the viewport 10 to the right showing what it showed. Nothing for a viewport that is not clipped, and nothing where the frame is already the box.
member.returns: Whether the frame changed.
member.exception: Thrown when the viewport is erased.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.FitToClip(System.Nullable{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3})
member.summary: Fits the frame to the box of its clip boundary as does, the view's centre moved by the step from to the new centre of the frame instead of the step from where the frame is: the place the frame would be at had it followed the edit that moved its boundary (a MOVE leaves the view as it was).
member.param: Where the frame's centre would be with the view kept; null for where it is now.
member.returns: Whether the frame changed.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.FitFrame(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Gives the frame a new box as AutoCAD's STRETCH, a stretch grip and SCALE of a viewport do, the model standing still on the sheet: the view keeps its scale, its height the new frame's over that scale, and its centre moves by the step of the frame's centre over the scale. A frame 200 by 100 about (110, 60) at 1:50 showing (1 000, 500) whose right side is moved 20 to the right is 220 by 100 about (120, 60), its view's centre (1 500, 500). The view's centre is in the viewport's own coordinates, which a twist of the view turns with the sides, so a twist leaves the step as it is.
member.param: The left side of the new frame.
The lower side of the new frame.
The right side of the new frame.
The upper side of the new frame.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.RemoveClip
member.summary: Takes the clip off the viewport, as the Delete of VPCLIP does: the boundary is erased, the link and the flag go, and the frame stays the box the boundary had. Nothing for a viewport that is not clipped.
member.exception: Thrown when the viewport is erased.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfViewport.TieClip(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfEntity)
member.summary: Ties the copy of a clipped viewport to the copy of its boundary that was copied with it, as AutoCAD's map of ids does: the group 340 names the copy and the viewport is its reactor. member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWipeout
member.summary: A WIPEOUT of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Wipeout: a mask that hides what is drawn under it in the colour of the background, an image of one pixel with no picture, clipped by the polygon it hides. Under the words of a tag of a Tekla or AutoCAD drawing it is moved, copied and mirrored with them.

remarks.para: Its record is that of an IMAGE, its only marker AcDbWipeout as AutoCAD 2021 writes it: the corner of its frame, the vectors of the frame's sides as those of its one pixel (11 and 12), and its boundary in -0.5 to 0.5 of the frame, x along it and y down; it shows no IMAGEDEF (340 of 0). A frame of side 40 placed at (-30, -10) holding the boundary (-0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5), (0.5, -0.25), (-0.5, -0.25) hides the rectangle from (-30, -10) to (10, 20).

What a has of a picture it has not: its brightness, contrast and fade and its display options are refused, as AutoCAD 2021 refuses or ignores them, and , and are null. takes any transformation; refuses one that scales more one way than another or shears, as AutoCAD 2021 answers eCannotScaleNonUniformly.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWipeout.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a wipeout made in code, as AutoCAD's new Wipeout(): of no polygon yet, to be given one by before it is appended, as AutoCAD 2021 writes a wipeout never set as one of no boundary and then cannot open the drawing. Its groups are those AutoCAD 2021 writes: a frame of one pixel, shown and clipped (70 of 7, 280 of 1), no IMAGEDEF (340 of 0). Appended, it lists the variables of wipeouts (ACAD_WIPEOUT_VARS) in a drawing that has none.

A copy of a polygon another writer left not closed, which the library reads closed and AutoCAD 2021 as of no corners, is taken, and written closed.

member.summary: Hides a polygon anew, as AutoCAD 2021's SetFrom: its corners in the plane of a normal, in the system of that normal (the arbitrary axis algorithm, the world's xy for (0, 0, 1)), the first again at the end. As AutoCAD 2021 writes it, the frame is the square on the box of the corners and the origin of the plane, its side the box's longer: the rectangle (-30, -10) to (10, 20) has the frame of side 40 at (-30, -10, 0), the rectangle (200, 100) to (230, 110) the frame of side 230 at the origin. The corners are written in the frame as a polygon, the record said to be clipped (280 of 1).
member.param: The corners, three or more, the first again at the end within the point tolerance of .
The normal of the plane, of some length.
member.exception: Thrown when the corners are null.

AutoCAD 2021 writes a polygon not closed as a WIPEOUT of no boundary, which it then cannot open.
Thrown when the wipeout is erased.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfXline
member.summary: An XLINE of a DXF file, as AutoCAD's Xline: the line without ends through along , both ways, in world coordinates.

remarks.para: The xline through (0, 5, 0) along (0, 1, 0) is the y axis moved 5 along itself: it runs through (0, -100, 0) and (0, 100, 0) alike. Its parameter is the distance from its base point along its direction, below nought behind it, so and are infinite and it has no start or end point.

The file holds the base point (groups 10, 20, 30) and the direction (groups 11, 21, 31), as AutoCAD gives them; a direction set is written made of unit length, and every other group of the record is kept as it was. A file of R12 has no xlines: one made in code is added to a drawing of R13 or later.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfFastNumber
member.summary: The numbers of a record read from its bytes, for the fast read of a LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE, TEXT or MTEXT: the number reads from the same text, to the bit, without the text made a string where it need not be; and the same read of a string, the first thing does with it.

remarks.para: A decimal of at most 19 digits is the digits times a power of ten. Where the digits are at most 2^53 and the power is within 1E22 one multiplication or division gives the number nearest it, since both are doubles exactly (Clinger's fast path). A number of 16 to 19 digits, as AutoCAD writes them (1234.5678901234567), or of a power beyond 1E22, takes the product of its digits and the first 128 bits of the power of ten, 192 bits worked out exactly. The power is cut off short of its true value by less than one in its last bit, so the true product lies between that product and the same plus the digits, and the number is the double that both ends round to (the nearest, an exact half going to the even one). A power of ten up to 1E38 is held whole by the 128 bits, its product is exact and a tie between two doubles, 9007199254740993, goes to the even one with no second end to the range. Where the two ends round to different doubles, which a tie of a negative power does and about one number in 10^22 else, and for any other text, reads it.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader
member.summary: Reads a DXF file into the library's shapes: what writes, back to the bit where the file holds the number, and what AutoCAD and the other CAD programs write of the same kinds, from R12 to R2018.

remarks.para: The entities of the drawing are read in the order of the file, each with its layer, its colour and its handle: a POINT, LINE, RAY and XLINE as the point, segment, ray and line without ends they are; a LWPOLYLINE and a POLYLINE of the plane as a chain or a polygon, with arcs where an edge has a bulge; a 3D POLYLINE as a chain or a polygon in space; a polyface or polygon mesh as a body of its faces; a CIRCLE, ARC and whole ELLIPSE as themselves; a part of an ELLIPSE and a SPLINE as a spline, exactly; a 3DFACE as a triangle or a face, a SOLID or TRACE as a polygon; a TEXT and an MTEXT as a ; a LEADER as its curve, the chain of its vertices or, splined, the spline fitted through them, as fits one; and a MULTILEADER as the lines of its leaders, as sets them out. Entities of space are read as shapes of space unless asks for those lying on the floor as shapes of the plane. An INSERT is read as the entities of its block, each placed where the INSERT puts it, with the look it takes from the INSERT and the names of the blocks it was placed through (); the blocks themselves are in , and the layers of the layer table in . DIMENSION, HATCH, ATTRIB and the other types are left out and counted in , and so is an entity with no shape to it, a LINE of no length among them; the entities of paper space are not read, and a warning counts them.

Every number is read as the file prints it, the double nearest it on either runtime, so a file the library wrote gives back every coordinate, radius, bulge, knot and weight it holds to the bit: a polyline of the plane read with is the polyline written. What the file holds in another form comes back to the last place or two: the angles of an ARC are degrees in the file, an ELLIPSE keeps the end of its major axis and the ratio of its radii, and a circle, arc or polyline in a tilted plane keeps its coordinates in the plane's own system.
A file that is not a DXF, or is cut short, is refused with a that names the line; a binary DXF is refused the same way. One entity that cannot be read never stops the others.
remarks.code: DxfDocument drawing = DxfReader.Read("plan.dxf", new DxfReadOptions { PlanAs2D = true }); foreach (GeoPolygonArc2 outline in drawing.OfType<GeoPolygonArc2>()) { ... }

member.summary: The placements of an INSERT, one to each cell of its array, after the placement it is read through: the system of its extrusion (210) times the shift to its insertion point (10, 20, 30, in that system) times the turn about z by its rotation (50, degrees) times its scales (41, 42, 43, each 1 where not given) times the shift of the block's base point to the origin. member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.RootSizeOf(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.Block,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: At most how many entities a block places: one for each entity of a type that is read, two for a 3DFACE, which may be two triangles, as many as its vertices for a polyline, which may be its edges, and for an INSERT its cells times its block's; nought for one that is not placed. A block met again while it is being worked out is inside itself there and is not placed again, so it counts nought; but that nought holds only on the way it was met by, so a size worked out through it is worked out again each time, and only one that met no such block is kept. The size worked out from the block of an INSERT is kept for its other INSERTs even so: the blocks counted nought on that walk are those being placed when it is, which refuse them too. Once 1 000 000 blocks have been worked out in the reading, in all, no more is: a size that needs one more is taken as the largest long and said to be stopped, and its INSERT is not placed, nor the other INSERTs of its block, whose walk would stop again. The sums stop at the largest long.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.ReadSpline(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Record)
member.summary: Reads a SPLINE by its degree (71), its knots (each 40), its weights (each 41, none where it is not rational) and its control points (each 10, 20, 30), every number as the file prints it, in world coordinates. One whose knots are not clamped, as AutoCAD writes a closed one, is clamped by knot insertion, the same curve over the same span. One given by its fit points alone (each 11, 21, 31), with the tangents at its ends where it has them (12, 22, 32 and 13, 23, 33), is the cubic AutoCAD fits through them, and said in a warning; so is one of fit points whose control points are not that cubic, as AutoCAD reads it ().

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.ReadFitSpline(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Record,System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3},GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoVector3,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoVector3,System.Int32)
member.summary: The spline through fit points, as AutoCAD 2021 reads one: the cubic it fits through them whatever degree the file gives (), its knots the chords, at an end of a tangent its derivative that tangent as the file has it, at one of none bent no more; through (0, 0) and (100, 0) the cubic straight line of 4 control points a third apart. The knots go up by the square roots of the chords, or by 1, where the flag 64, or 128, of group 70 says so.

The control points, knots and weights of a spline with its knots clamped: as they are where they are, and where they are not, as a closed spline of AutoCAD's, the same curve over the span its knots of index degree and count give, by inserting each end of that span until it stands degree times, as Boehm's insertion does it in the homogeneous coordinates of a rational spline, and keeping the control points and knots of the span. False where the knots are not the count and order a spline's are.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.Chain(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Record,System.Collections.Generic.List{GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPoint3},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Double},System.Boolean,System.Boolean,GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoVector3)
member.summary: Makes a chain or a loop of vertices, with arcs where an edge has a bulge: the bulge on a vertex belongs to the edge leaving it, and on the last vertex of an open chain to nothing. A vertex within the point tolerance of the one kept before it is dropped with the edge between them, the vertex kept taking the bulge of the edge running on, as the constructors of the chains drop one; a last vertex on the first of a loop goes with its edge back to the first. A loop of two vertices with an arc, a circle drawn as two halves, has its first arc halved at its middle, so that it is a loop of the three vertices a loop has; a loop that encloses no area, or in space does not lie in one plane, is an open chain that ends on its first vertex, and said in a warning. A typed conversion may ask for a loop whatever the flag says, the bulge of the last vertex closing it (), for a chain, a closed polyline opened as such a loop is, or for the kind with arcs though there are none ().

The shape makes of the vertices, the tolerance and what a typed conversion asks for given; false where fewer than two of the vertices are distinct; counts up the loops made an open chain, as they are made. Where the two lists are the call's own, and are the vertices kept where no vertex lies on the one before it, changed as the shape is made, where they would be copied.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.ReadText(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Record)
member.summary: Reads a TEXT or an MTEXT. A TEXT stands in the system of its extrusion's plane, at its first alignment point (10) where it is aligned left on its baseline (72 and 73 nought) or aligned or fitted between its two points (72 3 or 5, 73 nought), which start at the first, and at its second (11) otherwise, turned by its group 50 in degrees, its letters widened by its group 41. An MTEXT stands at its insertion point (10) in world coordinates, turned as its direction (11) says, or by its group 50 in degrees where it has none, its paragraphs wrapping at its width (41). Placed by an INSERT, its x and y axes are carried: it stands where its point lands, faces the way the carried axes span, turned to the carried x axis, its height stretched as the y axis is and a TEXT's letters widened as the x axis is against it. The rotation is brought into a turn, from nought up to 2 pi.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Reading.MText(System.String)
member.summary: The words of an MTEXT from its pieces and its last joined, as reads them.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.Read(System.String,GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions)
member.summary: Reads a DXF file from a path.
member.param: How to read it; null reads it with the defaults of .
member.returns: The entities of the file and what it says of itself.
member.exception: Thrown when the path is null.

Thrown when the file is not a DXF, is binary, or is cut short, the message naming the line; or when its header names a code page that does not read each byte of ASCII as itself, such as UTF-16 or ISO-2022, the message naming the page.
Thrown when the file cannot be read.
member.remarks: The text of a file from R2007 on is UTF-8; that of an older one is in the code page its header names ($DWGCODEPAGE, ANSI_1252 when it names none), where the runtime has it: Windows-1252 always, and the others on .NET Framework, or on .NET (Core) once the caller has registered CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance with ; without it such a file is read as Latin-1 with a warning. Letters beyond ASCII written as escapes, \U+00E9 for an e acute as writes them, are read as the letters.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReader.TextDecoding
member.summary: How the bytes of a file are read as text, chosen once for the whole file: Latin-1 for a file all ASCII, after the mark of UTF-8 where it has one. A line reads the same alone as within the whole, as AutoCAD reads a file line by line: a file in a code page of letters of more than one byte, such as 932, is split into its lines at the byte 0x0A before it is read, so that a byte that opens a letter at the end of a line does not take the line feed after it; in any other the line feed is the one byte 0x0A already.

None where the first is a letter alone and the second another, as A4 and A1 are in Shift-JIS, which AutoCAD keeps as written but for the plain words of an MTEXT, which take the first, U+FF64 of \M+1A4A1; nor where a byte, or the two, are no letter of the page, a letter of private use alone counted as none (A0, FD, FE and FF of Shift-JIS), as \M+100FF and \M+18200: AutoCAD makes of each such code a letter of its own, U+E800 and on, in the order it meets them in all it has read since it started, and so different from one session to the next; nor where the runtime has not the page, as .NET (Core) has not until the caller registers CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance.

A code with no semicolon after it is kept as written, as ezdxf keeps it, unless a later semicolon ends it, as it ends it in ezdxf too.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions
member.summary: How reads a DXF file: whether a drawing in the plan comes back as shapes of the plane, whether its numbers are scaled to millimetres, and the tolerance that says which entities have no shape to them.
member.remarks: The defaults read a file as it is: every shape of space, the numbers as the file prints them, and the default tolerance. new DxfReadOptions { PlanAs2D = true } reads a plan drawn in AutoCAD as polylines, arcs and circles of the plane.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.PlanAs2D
member.summary: Gets or sets whether an entity that lies on the floor is read as the shape of the plane it is. False by default, which reads every entity as the shape of space it is.

remarks.para: An entity in world coordinates (POINT, LINE, RAY, XLINE, SPLINE, 3D POLYLINE) lies on the floor where every height of it is nought, whatever its extrusion, which for a POINT or a LINE says only which way its thickness stands. One in the coordinates of its extrusion's plane (CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE, 2D POLYLINE, SOLID, TRACE) and an ELLIPSE lie on it where the extrusion is (0, 0, 1) or (0, 0, -1) exactly, or not given, and every height is nought. On (0, 0, -1), as AutoCAD writes a mirrored entity, x is turned over and a bulge negated, the vertices kept in their order, and an ARC from a to b runs clockwise from pi - a to pi - b, from the start the file gives as the arc read in space does: the ARC of radius 10 about the origin from 0 to 90 degrees on it is the clockwise from (-10, 0) to (0, 10). A part of an ELLIPSE and a SPLINE keep the direction of the file too.

A file wrote from shapes of the plane reads back so as those shapes: a closed LWPOLYLINE with bulges at no elevation is a , and the same polyline at an elevation of 5 a at z = 5. A 3DFACE and a mesh are of space either way.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.ToMillimeters
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the coordinates and sizes are scaled to millimetres by the unit the file says it is in (): a drawing in metres has its numbers times 1 000. False by default, which keeps the numbers as the file prints them.
member.remarks: Points, radii, elevations and the lengths of axes are scaled, and so are the insertion point of an INSERT, the base point of a block and the spacings of a MINSERT; angles, bulges, ratios, weights, knots, directions and the scales of an INSERT are not, having no unit. A file in millimetres is read to the bit either way. A file with no unit, or one the DXF reference does not list, is not scaled, and a warning says so.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.Tolerance
member.summary: Gets or sets the tolerance that says which entities have no shape to them and which four corners of a 3DFACE lie in one plane; unless set.

remarks.para: The global tolerance is not read. The point tolerance says that a LINE is of no length, a CIRCLE, ARC or ELLIPSE of no radius or axis, that two neighbouring vertices of a polyline are one (as the polyline constructors drop such a vertex), that two fit points of a SPLINE are one, and which corners of a polygon, a face or a mesh are one. The vector tolerance says that a RAY or XLINE has no direction, and, read as an area as a polygon reads it, that a closed polyline with arcs encloses no area. The planar tolerance says whether the four corners of a 3DFACE, the vertices of a closed 3D POLYLINE and the faces of a mesh lie in one plane. The point tolerance also says whether an INSERT's scaling is so nearly even that a circle, an arc or a chain with arcs of its block stays one (). It is used for nothing else.

A LINE 0.0004 long is no segment within the default tolerance and is left out; within 1E-5 it is a segment. A 3DFACE whose four corners stand off one plane by more than the planar tolerance is two triangles.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.KeepGroups
member.summary: Gets or sets whether each entity keeps every group of its record as the file has it, in ; true by default. False leaves them empty, which a large file reads in less memory: the shapes and the look of the entities are read either way.
member.remarks: Of 100 000 entities of eight kinds, a file of 34 MB, the document holds about four times as much with the groups as without; the guide gives the numbers.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.ExpandBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets whether each INSERT is read as the entities of its block, placed where it puts them; true by default. False leaves the INSERTs out, counted in : the blocks are read into either way.

remarks.para: An entity of a block is placed by the INSERT's own system: the block's base point taken to the origin, the scales along x, y and z, the turn about z, the insertion point, then the system of the INSERT's extrusion; a MINSERT's cells, row after row, each shifted along the turned axes by its column and row spacing, not scaled. An INSERT inside a block is placed within it, the two placements composed, to a depth of 64; a block that inserts itself, at once or through others, is not placed again, and a warning says so. An entity on layer 0 takes the layer of its INSERT, and a colour, linetype or lineweight BYBLOCK the INSERT's.

Points, segments, rays, lines without ends, chains and polygons without arcs, faces, meshes and splines are carried point by point, a spline by its control points, which any placement carries exactly, and an ELLIPSE by the images of its semi-axes. A turn, an even scaling and a mirror place a circle, an arc and a chain with arcs as the same shape, the arc running the way its image runs, so a mirrored arc runs the other way round. An uneven scaling places a circle as the ellipse it becomes, an arc as the spline that is exactly that part of the ellipse, and a chain with arcs as a segment for each straight edge and such a spline for each arc edge, each an entity of its own, in the order of the chain: the circle of radius 10 scaled by 3 along x is the 30 by 10. A scaling so nearly even that the circle placed whole lands within the point tolerance of of where the scaling puts each of its points keeps it a circle, by the rule of : the circle of radius 10 scaled by 1.0000001 along y is the circle of radius 10, and by 1.001 the ellipse 10.01 by 10.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.SupportFolders
member.summary: Gets or sets the folders a DWG's files of shapes are looked for in, in their order, as AutoCAD looks in its support folders; empty by default. Used where reads a DWG.
member.remarks: A DWG keeps a SHAPE by its number in the file of shapes of its text style, where DXF gives its name (group 2). The file the style names, ltypeshp.shx say, is looked for in each folder in turn, with .shx where the name has no extension, and first where the style gives it with its folder; the first compiled file of shapes found names the shape. Where none is found, or it has no shape of that number, the SHAPE gives its number instead, as group 70, as AutoCAD writes a shape whose file it does not find: shape 130 is TRACK1 with ltypeshp.shx in one of the folders and 70 = 130 without it.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.UnsizedBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the size of a block is taken as nought before its INSERT is placed, so that only the count of what is placed holds the bound of ; for the tests of that count alone.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.MostSizedBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets how many blocks are worked out, in all, for the sizes of the INSERTs of one reading, the drawing's and those of the blocks read on their own; 1 000 000, and smaller for the tests of that bound alone.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfReadOptions.MaxPlacedEntities
member.summary: Gets or sets how many entities the INSERTs may place from blocks in one reading, counted across the drawing and the blocks read for ; 2 000 000 by default.
member.remarks: Blocks placed inside blocks multiply: a block of 100 INSERTs of a block of 100 INSERTs of a block of 100 INSERTs of a line is a file of 18 KB and 100 000 000 lines. An INSERT is placed whole or not at all: where the entities it would place, worked out from its block before any is placed, would take the count past this number, it places none, is counted in , and a warning names the number and how many entities the INSERTs left out would have placed. The INSERTs of the drawing are placed first, in the order of the file. Whatever the working out says, of blocks that insert each other among them, the count of what is placed holds the bound too: an INSERT whose entities would pass it is taken back whole, with what its placing counted.
member.exception: Thrown when the number set is not above nought.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfShape.Groups
member.summary: Gets every group of the entity's record, in the order of the file, after the group 0 that names its type: extended data (1000 to 1071) and groups no reader looks at among them, each value the text the file prints.

remarks.para: Of a POLYLINE they run on through its VERTEX records and its SEQEND, each opened by its own group 0, as the file has them. Two entities made from one record, the two triangles of a 3DFACE out of flat, share its groups.

The reader takes from them the layer (8), the handle (5), the colour (62 and 420), the linetype (6), the lineweight (370), the thickness (39), paper space (67) and the groups of the shape: the points (10 to 13 with 20 to 23 and 30 to 33), the extrusion (210, 220, 230), the sizes, angles, bulges and elevation (38 to 51), the flags and counts (70 to 74), the knots, weights and points of a spline, and the words of a text (1 and 3). member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfText
member.summary: A text of a DXF file, a TEXT of one line or an MTEXT of paragraphs, as reads it into : where it stands, which way it faces and reads, how tall it is, and its words.

remarks.para: A text is the same in the plan and in space, so reads it as this class either way: it has no twin of the plane. A TEXT 2.5 high reading "Grid A" at (1 000, 500) on the floor is at (1 000, 500, 0), its normal (0, 0, 1) and its rotation nought.
It cannot be changed once made, and two texts are the same only where they are one object: it does not compare its numbers.

member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfText.Rotation
member.summary: Gets how far the text is turned, in radians counter-clockwise about from the x axis of the normal's own system by the arbitrary axis algorithm: a TEXT's group 50 in degrees made radians, an MTEXT's from its direction (group 11) where it has one and from its group 50 in degrees otherwise, as AutoCAD writes it (the DXF reference says radians). member.name: P:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfText.Value
member.summary: Gets the words: a TEXT's as written, an MTEXT's with its formatting taken out and its paragraphs (\P) a line feed apart. In both, %%c, %%d and %%p (either case) are the diameter (∅, U+2205), degree and plus-minus signs; in a TEXT %%% is a per cent sign and %%nnn the character of the code nnn, which an MTEXT keeps as written, as AutoCAD 2021 does; an MTEXT's \~ is the space that does not break, U+00A0; a letter written as an escape, \U+00E9, is the letter, and so is the text \U+0041 written in the words, which reads as A, an MTEXT's escapes read before its formatting, as AutoCAD 2021 reads them: \\U+0110 is a backslash and Đ, \U+005CP a new line; a control character in AutoCAD's caret form, ^J, ^M or ^I, is the character, and ^ a caret. A TEXT is one line, so a line feed in its words is a space; a carriage return is left out of either.

member.name: T:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter
member.summary: Writes shapes as a DXF file of version R2000 (AC1015), which AutoCAD, Tekla Structures and every CAD viewer open.

remarks.para: Every shape added is drawn on a layer, named as given and made on first use in the colour AutoCAD calls white, with the continuous line; none given means layer 0. CAD colours by layer, so there is no colour to pass. The drawing is in millimetres. Numbers are written exactly, as a text that reads back to the same double on .NET Framework and on .NET 10 alike (the digits may differ between the two). A shape with a number in it that is not finite (NaN or infinity) is refused with an before anything of it is written.

In the plane a shape is written as the entity AutoCAD has for it, not as chords: a polygon, a rectangle, a triangle and each ring of a face as a closed lightweight polyline, a chain or loop with arcs as one too with the bulge of each arc edge, a circle as a CIRCLE, an arc as an ARC, an ellipse as an ELLIPSE, a ray as a RAY, a line without ends as an XLINE and a spline as a SPLINE of its own knots and control points. A clockwise arc is written from its end to its start, since DXF arcs run counter-clockwise only. A face is its rings and not a filled area: fills.

In space a segment, a point, a ray, a line without ends, an ellipse and a spline are written as they are, a chain and a polygon as a 3D polyline, and anything with a surface as 3DFACEs: one per triangle of a face, a body or a ball, one per face of a mesh that has three or four corners and turns one way, and six for a box, written from its corners. Where a face, a side of a body or a face of a mesh is cut into triangles, the edges between its own triangles are marked invisible, so a wireframe shows its outline and not the cut; triangles given as they are keep every edge.

A curve in space (an arc, a circle, a chain or loop with arcs) is written as itself when no chord tolerance is given: an arc as an ARC and a circle as a CIRCLE, each in the coordinate system of its own plane (the arbitrary axis algorithm AutoCAD itself uses), a chain or loop that lies in one plane as one lightweight polyline with the plane's extrusion and elevation and the bulge of each arc edge, and a chain that bends out of one plane as a LINE or an ARC for each edge. Given a chord tolerance, which has no default, it is cut into chords no further from the curve than that: a circle of radius 100 at 0.1 is 71 chords, one of radius 50 000 at 0.001 is 15 708. A curve that would take more than 1 048 576 chords, counted over a whole chain or loop, is refused.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoSpline2,System.String)
member.summary: Adds a spline as the SPLINE it is, at height nought: its degree, its knots, its weights where it is rational and its control points, as the spline holds them.
member.param: The layer; layer 0 when none is given.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when the spline is null.

remarks.para: Nothing is refitted or rescaled, so a reader gets the very curve back, every number to the bit: the cubic with the control points (0, 0), (100, 150), (200, 150), (300, 0) is a SPLINE of degree 3 with its 8 knots 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1 and its 4 control points, and the circle of radius 100 that builds is its 12 knots, 9 weights and 9 control points. No fit points are written: the control points are the curve.

The flags say what the SPLINE is: 1, closed, only where its first and last control points are the same point exactly, as the clamped spline then ends where it starts (it is never flagged periodic; the circle of ends on its start exactly and is flagged closed, where ends only within the tolerance of each other are not); 4, rational, where a weight is other than one, and only then are the weights written; 8, planar, always, with the extrusion (0, 0, 1). The knot, control point and fit tolerances are written as 1E-10.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoArc3,System.String)
member.summary: Adds an arc in space as the ARC it is, in the coordinate system of its own plane, with no chords.
member.param: The layer; layer 0 when none is given.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when a coordinate or an angle is not a finite number, or the normal has no length.
Thrown when the radius is not a finite number above nought.

remarks.para: The normal of the arc, turned if need be to point up in its largest component (ties go to z, then y, then x), is the extrusion of the ARC; the centre is written in the coordinates of the plane it stands on and the angles are degrees counter-clockwise about the extrusion, from the x axis of the plane. That x axis is the one AutoCAD works out itself from the extrusion by the arbitrary axis algorithm: the world y crossed with the normal where both x and y of the normal are less than 1/64 from nought, and the world z crossed with it otherwise. A quarter of the circle of radius 10 about (0, 0, 5), from (10, 0, 5) to (0, 10, 5), is an ARC with centre (0, 0, 5) and angles 0 and 90, and the same quarter on the normal (0, 0, -1) is written the same way, since an arc counter-clockwise about down is clockwise about up. An arc lying on the floor is written exactly as writes it: the extrusion (0, 0, 1) is what a CIRCLE or ARC has when its groups are left out, and they are.

An arc that turns clockwise about the extrusion is written from its end to its start, as does, since DXF arcs run counter-clockwise only. An arc of a whole turn is written as a CIRCLE. The result is the arc itself: over 20 000 random arcs (radii 0.5 to 500, centres up to 1 000 from the origin, any normal, both ways round) its start, middle and end, worked back from the groups written, are within 8.3E-13 of its radius, or 1.4E-15 of its radius plus its centre's distance from the origin, which is the rounding of the coordinates themselves. gives chords instead.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoCircle3,System.String)
member.summary: Adds a circle in space as the CIRCLE it is, in the coordinate system of its own plane, with no chords.
member.param: The layer; layer 0 when none is given.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when a coordinate is not a finite number or the normal has no length.
Thrown when the radius is not a finite number above nought.
member.remarks: The normal of the circle, turned up as turns an arc's, is the extrusion and the centre is written in the coordinates of the plane by the arbitrary axis algorithm described there; a circle on the floor is written exactly as a is. A circle of radius 25 about (10, 20, 30) on the normal (1, 1, 0) is a CIRCLE with extrusion (0.7071, 0.7071, 0) and centre (7.0711, 30, 21.2132), where at 0.1 gives 36 chords.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPolylineArc3,GeometryHelper.Tolerance,System.String)
member.summary: Adds a chain with arcs in space as it is: one lightweight polyline in its plane where it lies in one, and a LINE or an ARC for each edge where it does not.
member.param: The tolerance that judges whether the chain lies in one plane, as does.
The layer; layer 0 when none is given.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when the chain is null.
Thrown when a coordinate, a bulge or a direction is not a finite number.

remarks.para: A chain that lies in one plane within the planar tolerance is a single LWPOLYLINE whose coordinates are those of the plane (extrusion, elevation, x and y) and whose bulges are those of the chain, negated where the arc turns about the opposite side of the extrusion. The extrusion is the normal of the plane turned, where it has to be, to point up in its largest component, so a chain on the floor is written with the extrusion (0, 0, 1), plain x and y and its height as the elevation, whichever way its arcs turn. A vertex off the plane by less than the tolerance is written on it, and so is an arc that stands off it by less: its bulge is written times the cosine between its normal and the extrusion, so an arc bowing square to the plane (bulge 1.8E-5 about (0, 1, 0) on a chord of 100 along x in the plane z = 0, which bows 0.0009 up) is written straight.

A chain that bends out of one plane, such as a reinforcing bar with bends in two, is a LINE for each straight edge and an ARC, in the coordinate system of its own plane as writes it, for each arc edge, in the order of the chain. An arc edge too shallow to place a circle for is read by its chord and is a LINE. A chain with no arc whose vertices all lie on one line lies in no one plane, so it too is a LINE for each edge.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Geometry.GeoPolygonArc3,System.String)
member.summary: Adds a loop with arcs in space as one closed lightweight polyline in its plane, each arc edge carrying its bulge.
member.param: The layer; layer 0 when none is given.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when the loop is null.
Thrown when a coordinate, a bulge or a direction is not a finite number.
member.remarks: A loop lies in one plane by construction, so it is always one LWPOLYLINE, written as writes a chain that lies in one. A slot 80 long and 20 wide (straight sides of 60) with a half circle at each end, lying in a plane tilted 30 degrees about the x axis, is four vertices and two bulges of 1, where chords at 0.01 are 74 segments.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfText,System.String)
member.summary: Adds a text: a TEXT of one line, or an MTEXT where it is multiline, in the plane of its normal.
member.param: The text, read by or made in code.
The layer; layer 0 when none is given.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when the text is null.

remarks.para: A TEXT is written aligned left on its baseline, its position in the system of its normal's plane, with its height, its rotation in degrees and its width factor, in the text style Standard. An MTEXT is written at its position in world coordinates, attached at its top left, with its height, its width where it has one and the direction it reads along in world coordinates, its words in pieces of 250 characters, a line feed written as a new paragraph (\P) and a backslash and a brace as the codes that keep them. A letter beyond ASCII is written as its escape, \U+00E9 for an e acute, and a control character in AutoCAD's caret form, a tab as ^I, with a caret written ^ and a space, as AutoCAD reads them.

reads it back as the same text: its words, its height, its width factor and width and its normal to the bit, and its position too where the normal is (0, 0, 1) or (0, 0, -1) or the text an MTEXT; a TEXT on a tilted normal comes back to the rounding of its plane's system, and the rotation to the last place or two, going through degrees or a direction. A %%c, %%d, %%p, %%% or %%nnn in the words comes back as the character it stands for, and so does the text \U+0041 in them, and the alignment and the attachment a text had in the file it was read from are not kept: it is written where it stands.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Words(System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: The words of a text as its group values hold them: a letter beyond ASCII as its escape, a control character in AutoCAD's caret form and a caret as ^ and a space; of an MTEXT, a backslash and the braces as the codes that keep them and a line feed as a new paragraph. Asked to keep letters, as writes them in the file's own code page, a letter beyond ASCII is kept as it is.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.Add(GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfShape)
member.summary: Adds an entity read: its shape, written by the overload of Add for it, on its layer, and in its colour, true colour, linetype and lineweight and with its thickness, each written only where the entity has one.
member.returns: This writer, for adding the next shape.
member.exception: Thrown when the entity is null.
Thrown when there is no overload of Add for the type of its shape, which it names.

remarks.para: A drawing read and written again keeps its shapes and the look of each: a LINE on the layer steel in colour 1, DASHED, 0.35 wide and 50 thick is read back as the same segment, to the bit, with the same five. A linetype the writer's table does not have is added to it by name, with no pattern, so that AutoCAD opens the file and draws the line solid until the drawing is given the linetype's pattern. The thickness is written on the entities that have one in DXF, the LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE and TEXT, and on no other. A text is written as a TEXT or an MTEXT, as writes it. The entity is given a handle of its own, and its are not written: only what the shape and the five say is.

A face of three or four corners with no hole, as a 3DFACE reads, is written as one 3DFACE of its corners again, in their order, with the edges the file hid hidden again where the 3DFACE was read whole; any other face, and a body, a polyface mesh among them, is written as its triangles at the global tolerance, as and write them. A needs a chord tolerance, and has no overload without one.

What is not kept: a circle or an arc in space on an extrusion that points down, as AutoCAD writes a mirrored one, is written about its normal turned up, as writes every arc, so a mirrored arc comes back running the other way, from its end to its start, over the same points; read with it is a either way. A linetype is written as the table spells it, so BYBLOCK comes back ByBlock and CONTINUOUS Continuous. The handle is new, the groups are not written, and a mesh comes back as the 3DFACEs of its triangles.

member.name: M:GeometryHelper.Dxf.DxfWriter.RecordsOf(System.Object,System.Int32,System.Double,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Double[]@)
member.summary: The records a shape is written as in a file edits, by the overload of Add for it: for each, its type and its groups after the head of an entity (its handle, owner, layer and look, which the file writes itself), those of a POLYLINE followed by its VERTEX records and its SEQEND. The thickness is written where the entity has one, the edges of a 3DFACE hidden as given, a text's letters beyond ASCII as they are; without subclass markers for a file of R12, and a polyline of the plane as a POLYLINE for one older than R14. The extents are the least and greatest x, y and z the shape reaches, null where it reaches none.
